studio:prompts3:ours-683.content:
[INPUT]
- language: Korean
- output_size: 1024x1024

[1. PURPOSE]
9-grid Instagram feed design for a store account, presented as a cohesive square social-media template with repeated visual identity across all tiles.
Designed for {매장유형} feed that needs one unified look across product photos, menu cards, interior shots, quote cards, daily-life posts, event notices, and save/share-friendly Instagram micro information.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- 전체 캔버스는 정사각형 1024x1024이며, 3x3 그리드로 정확히 9칸을 나누고 각 칸의 간격과 정렬 기준을 동일하게 유지한다.
- 각 타일은 {매장명}의 개성을 반영하되, 전체적으로 같은 톤과 필터가 적용된 듯한 일관된 인스타그램 피드 느낌을 유지한다.
- 사진/메뉴/매장/인용/일상/이벤트 콘텐츠가 섞여도 모두 같은 프레임 규칙, 같은 색감, 같은 타이포 시스템을 따른다.
- 상단/중앙/하단 9칸 모두 실제 매장 피드처럼 자연스러운 소품, 질감, 메뉴판, 영수증, 컵, 패브릭, 식물, 조명 반사, 손글씨 라벨 등을 포함해 생활감 있는 브랜드 무드를 만든다.
- {피드구성}, {그리드구성}, {컬러팔레트}, {타이포스타일}, {피드무드}는 실제 피드 콘셉트를 정의하는 핵심 스타일 지시로 반영한다.
- 각 타일 안에 Instagram card 요소를 자연스럽게 배치한다: {계정명}, {해시태그}, 저장/공유 micro icons, 짧은 캡션, 위치 라벨, 날짜 라벨, 작은 CTA 문구.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
1) Grid foundation: 3x3 equal tiles, precise gutters, all nine panels aligned with identical spacing and consistent cropping rules.
2) Content rhythm: alternate visual types across the grid so the feed reads as balanced — product/photo tiles, menu/info tiles, interior/store tiles, quote tiles, daily-life tiles, event notice tiles — while preserving one unified identity.
3) Suggested tile plan: top-left brand intro with {계정명} and {매장명}; top-center hero product photo featuring {대표메뉴}; top-right quote card with a short Korean line; middle-left menu card with prices; middle-center interior/lifestyle photo; middle-right event notice with date/time; bottom-left behind-the-scenes daily post; bottom-center location/contact card; bottom-right save/share CTA end-card.
4) Store identity tiles: use {매장명}, {매장유형}, {위치라벨}, {연락처}, {영업시간} as repeated real-account details across multiple panels, making the feed feel ready for an actual Instagram account.
5) Typography tiles: integrate short Korean headlines, hashtag-style text, menu names, price labels, and caption snippets in the same serif-led system, with Instagram micro UI details such as ♡, 저장, 공유, DM 문의, 위치 태그.
6) Texture and realism: include natural paper grain, ceramic or glass reflections, menu board edges, napkin folds, counter texture, seasonal flowers or small table objects that match {컬러팔레트} and {피드무드}.
7) Uniform finish: apply the same editorial-style finish across all 9 tiles so the final feed looks curated, premium, and intentionally planned as a single store account set.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: Korean serif in a refined traditional style, such as Noto Serif KR or Nanum Myeongjo, with medium-to-bold weight for headers and small English sublabels in Pretendard Light or Inter; create clear hierarchy between headline, caption, hashtag, price, and micro UI text.
- Color palette: {컬러팔레트} should translate into a signature palette paired with white, cream, warm amber, and tactile neutral tones; use the accent color repeatedly in labels, dividers, stickers, underlines, and small Instagram UI marks.
- Instagram identity details: display {계정명} like a real handle on at least two tiles, include {해시태그} on hashtag/caption tiles, and include tiny save/share/heart/comment icons as decorative micro UI elements.
- Store information: include realistic information blocks such as {영업시간}, {위치라벨}, {연락처}, {대표메뉴}, {가격표기}, and {이벤트문구} as if the feed is announcing actual store content.
- Dividers and cards: use fine hairline dividers, small labels, rounded caption stickers, paper-note overlays, subtle shadows around 4px y-offset, 12px blur, 15% opacity, and neatly aligned card blocks to separate content inside each tile.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: clean editorial social-media grid look, shot consistently as if with a Canon EOS R5 and 35mm f/1.8 for general scenes, plus 50mm f/1.8 for tighter detail tiles; flat-lay panels can use a 24mm top-down setup.
- Lighting: soft diffused daylight from a large window at 45° upper-left, with gentle fill from the opposite side; keep shadows light, even, and repeatable across all tiles.
- Color grade: warm cream, amber, muted neutral tones, and a subtle signature accent derived from {컬러팔레트}, with slightly reduced saturation for a polished feed look.
- Surface detail: show realistic tabletop texture, paper fibers, cup glaze, menu card ink, flower petals, fabric weave, glass highlights, and small sticker edges so the feed feels photographed and designed rather than empty.

[6. MOOD]
Curated boutique Instagram grid — like a refined editorial brand page with warm daily-life storytelling, consistent store identity, and save-worthy card design for {매장명}.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: the rendered image must preserve clear, legible Korean typography with no broken characters.
- Verbatim Korean strings that must appear correctly when used in the design: {매장명}, {계정명}, {해시태그}, {대표메뉴}, {영업시간}, {위치라벨}, {연락처}, {가격표기}, {이벤트문구}.
- Include realistic Korean feed text examples where appropriate: “오늘의 추천”, “저장하고 방문하기”, “DM 예약 가능”, “신메뉴 출시”, “이번 주 이벤트”, “가까운 날에 만나요”.
- All 9 panels must share the same grid logic, same tone, and same overall visual system; the set should read as one planned Instagram feed.
- Text must remain sharp, properly spaced, and aligned to the grid; no distorted Hangul, no merged syllables, no mirrored letters.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]
- Fake official seals / certifications
- Broken Korean characters
- Unauthorized celebrity face composites
- Fake government or legal document styling

[1. PURPOSE]
Store pickup station 안내 poster for delivery and takeaway, designed as a realistic vertical service infographic displayed inside a busy cafe, restaurant, chicken shop, or snack/dessert venue. It should feel like a printed in-store poster mounted near the counter, with practical operational details, readable Korean signage, and a lively retail atmosphere.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Main title sits at the top 12–15% as a strong headline, with the central service board occupying about 60% of the frame.
- Use {매장} as the venue context, showing a believable pickup-counter scene with order shelves, receipt slips, food bags, drink trays, a small tablet/kiosk screen, and a QR block arranged into a clear service layout.
- The procedure line should read naturally left-to-right or top-to-bottom depending on panel fit, with {절차} displayed as the core workflow.
- Place {위치 안내} in a secondary information zone near the lower half, aligned with the pickup counter visual and supported by directional arrows, floor-marker graphics, and a small counter map.
- Add realistic poster information such as operating hours, pickup etiquette, order-number display, short notices, and contact/parking microcopy while keeping the workflow instantly readable from a distance.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
- Top header band: set the poster title “매장 픽업 스테이션” in a bold, highly legible Korean headline treatment, with a small English subtitle line beneath it such as “DELIVERY · TAKEOUT · QUICK PICKUP”. Include a small store label using {매장}, plus a date-style service label like “2026 SPRING SERVICE GUIDE”.
- Center hero area (mid 40–50%): depict a pickup counter with a compact kiosk-like feel, a glowing number display showing realistic sample numbers like “A-017” and “B-022”, neatly stacked takeout bags, drink carriers, a receipt printer, condiment tray, and labeled pickup shelves. The scene should visually explain where customers and riders collect orders.
- Procedure strip: show {절차} as four steps using numbered blocks, arrows, circular markers, or receipt-ticket tabs. Each step should be evenly spaced and easy to read, with the required labels “01 주문”, “02 알림”, “03 픽업”, “04 음식 확인”. Add tiny supporting Korean microcopy under each step, for example “앱 또는 카운터 주문”, “번호 호출 확인”, “픽업존에서 수령”, “메뉴·수량 확인”.
- Information block: place {위치 안내} beside or below the workflow, as a concise location note tied to the pickup counter and waiting area. Include the required text “픽업존 위치 + 번호표 시스템” and a small directional map with labels like “입구”, “카운터”, “대기선”, “라이더 픽업”.
- Visual support elements: integrate {비주얼} as practical diagram-like illustrations and real poster details: a QR square labeled “주문 확인 QR”, a sample ticket/receipt marked “NO. 024”, a bell notification icon, a food-bag icon, arrow decals, counter shelf labels, and a small safety notice strip.
- Bottom utility band: create a strong footer zone using {컬러} and {타이포} styling cues. Add realistic service details such as “운영시간 10:00–22:00”, “문의 02-000-0000”, “포장 주문은 알림 후 10분 내 픽업 권장”, and a compact address line like “1층 카운터 오른쪽 픽업존”.
- Size cue: keep the composition optimized for {비율}, with vertical poster readability, strong top-to-bottom hierarchy, and enough density to feel like a real operational poster in a store.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: bold Korean sans serif such as Pretendard ExtraBold or Noto Sans KR Bold for the main title; English subtitle in Pretendard Medium or Inter Medium; step labels in Pretendard SemiBold at compact sizes; microcopy in Noto Sans KR Regular with high contrast.
- Color palette: use {컬러} as the base system, supported by off-white #F7F7F4, charcoal #2B2B2B, warm paper white, and one clear accent tone for arrows, number tags, QR label, and pickup-zone markers.
- Border/shadow: use thin divider lines, subtle card borders, receipt-paper textures, acrylic sign shadows, and a soft drop shadow with 4px y-offset, 12px blur, 15% opacity for floating info blocks.
- Layout treatment: sharp rectangular panels, readable spacing, disciplined alignment, service-counter realism, small practical decals, shelf labels, printed paper grain, and everyday retail details that support the pickup guidance.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: clean product-poster look with a 50mm standard lens aesthetic, straight-on framing, and shallow perspective only if needed for the counter area.
- Lighting: bright diffused studio light from upper-left at about 45°, with a gentle fill from the right to keep the counter, printed Korean text, number display, and QR elements readable.
- Color grade: neutral retail palette with white, charcoal, and the venue accent color, crisp and slightly cool for operational clarity, with subtle warm highlights from the counter lights and realistic printed poster texture.

[6. MOOD]
Practical service-signage editorial — the clarity and layout discipline of modern wayfinding posters used in premium cafe interiors, enriched with real in-store pickup details, friendly customer guidance, and a believable takeaway counter environment.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: the following strings must appear exactly as written in the rendered image: “매장 픽업 스테이션”, “01 주문”, “02 알림”, “03 픽업”, “04 음식 확인”, “픽업존 위치 + 번호표 시스템”.
- Additional Korean poster text should be realistic and short, such as “주문 확인 QR”, “운영시간 10:00–22:00”, “대기선”, “라이더 픽업”, “음식 수령 후 메뉴와 수량을 확인해 주세요”.
- The workflow must remain four steps, clearly separated, with no merged or missing stage.
- Keep the pickup counter, QR element, number display, receipt/ticket details, and location guidance visibly connected as one service system.
- Maintain a vertical poster structure with clean hierarchy and no distorted Korean characters.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]
- Fake official seals / certifications
- Broken Korean characters

[1. PURPOSE]
Seasonal new-menu announcement card for social media feed, story repost, and in-store countertop promo use, designed as a tall editorial product poster.
Showcase a single signature drink or dessert hero with clear launch price, period, opening-week event callout, cafe identity, and realistic purchase information.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Main subject: {신메뉴} placed as the central hero occupying about 58% of the frame, surrounded by practical seasonal styling and tactile cafe details.
- Brand header: {매장명} and {슬로건} placed near the top with a small English NEW accent, giving the card a real cafe campaign identity.
- Launch information: {출시일} and {가격·기간} anchored in the lower third as a readable product-info block, with price emphasized as the second-most visible text after the headline.
- Product copy: {제품설명} placed near the hero as a short editorial tasting note, like a real seasonal menu card.
- Seasonal accent props: {비주얼} arranged around the hero in a natural tabletop or studio-still-life frame, including small leaves, fruit slices, florals, napkin texture, spoon, coaster, condensation, or paper menu pieces when appropriate.
- Color direction: {컬러} applied through background tint, garnish accents, menu strip, and small highlight elements, while keeping the product itself true-to-life.
- Typography block: {타이포} set in a stacked promotional hierarchy with one dominant Korean headline, compact secondary line, and a small English NEW accent.
- Event badge: {이벤트} placed as a rounded chip, ribbon, or sticker-style callout near the top-right or bottom-right corner for fast readability.
- Footer information: include {주소}, {연락처}, {인스타핸들}, {해시태그}, small save/share micro icons, and a compact allergy/origin note {원산지·알레르기} along the bottom edge like a realistic cafe promo card.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
1) Header zone (top 14%): set "신메뉴 출시" in bold Korean display type, with {매장명}, {슬로건}, and a small "NEW" accent nearby; spacing should feel editorial and campaign-ready.
2) Hero zone (center 55–60%): render {신메뉴} as the clear focal object, sharply lit, with realistic surface texture, condensation, crema, frosting, cake crumb, fruit pulp, ice, foam, garnish, label, straw, spoon, or topping detail depending on the item.
3) Seasonal staging: add {비주얼} as a surrounding layer—leaf, flower, fruit slice, ice cube, linen napkin, kraft paper texture, menu slip, coaster, teaspoon, or small tray—so the product feels tied to the season and cafe setting.
4) Editorial product note: place {제품설명} as a short caption beside or below the hero, using a smaller text size and a light divider line for magazine-like hierarchy.
5) Offer zone (lower third): place {가격·기간} and {출시일} inside a contrasting label strip or paper-ticket block, making price and campaign period instantly readable.
6) Promotion chip: place {이벤트} as a compact badge with rounded corners, ribbon tail, or small sticker texture; keep it secondary but highly legible.
7) Footer utility row: show {인스타핸들}, {해시태그}, {주소}, {연락처}, and small outline micro icons for save/share/comment, plus {원산지·알레르기} in tiny but formed Korean type.
8) Final balance: use {컬러} to unify background, props, typography highlights, label strip, and footer details, ensuring the composition feels polished, seasonal, and launch-ready.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: Pretendard ExtraBold or Noto Sans KR Black for the main Korean headline, Pretendard SemiBold for price details, Pretendard Regular for footer information, and a small condensed sans for the English NEW accent; headline size should feel poster-scale, with tight line spacing and strong hierarchy.
- Color palette: derive from {컬러}, grounded with one light neutral base and one deep contrast tone; apply accent colors to the badge, divider lines, fruit/floral props, and product-info block for readability and product separation.
- Border/shadow: use a soft drop shadow under the hero at 4px y-offset, 14px blur, 16% opacity; use crisp product edges, refined sticker texture on the event badge, and subtle paper depth in the footer strip.
- Surface treatment: matte paper, soft gradient backdrop, or lightly textured cafe poster stock with fine grain; allow natural gloss, condensation, syrup shine, crema sheen, frosting texture, or fruit moisture when the menu item requires it.
- Information design: make price, period, store contact, handle, hashtag, and allergy/origin note feel like real printed cafe collateral rather than placeholder text.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: 85mm f/1.8 product-portrait look, slightly compressed perspective, framed like a premium cafe campaign poster.
- Lighting: soft window light from upper-left at about 45°, with a gentle reflector fill from lower-right and a faint rim highlight to separate the product from background.
- Color grade: seasonal signature tones with controlled saturation, clean whites, and slightly warm highlights; preserve appetizing but realistic product color.

[6. MOOD]
Premium seasonal cafe launch editorial — a polished Korean dessert-cafe promo card with tactile menu-board realism, seasonal still-life styling, and social-media-ready typography.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: 반드시 아래 문구가 깨지지 않고 정확히 보여야 함: "신메뉴 출시", "NEW", "{매장명}", "{신메뉴}", "{제품설명}", "{가격·기간}", "{출시일}", "{이벤트}", "{인스타핸들}", "{해시태그}", "{주소}", "{연락처}", "{원산지·알레르기}"
- Layout invariant: the hero product must remain the dominant subject, and the launch copy must stay readable without overlapping the product core.
- Render the footer like a real cafe card: "저장", "공유", "댓글" micro labels may appear beside simple icons if space allows.
- If text is rendered, Korean characters must be fully legible and correctly formed; no partial glyphs, no warped spacing.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]
- Fake official seals or certifications
- Broken Korean characters
- Fake government, medical, or award-style certification marks
- Celebrity composites or impersonation-style faces

[INPUT]

[1. PURPOSE]
Korean regular-customer appreciation event card, vertical poster-style loyalty promo for in-store display or social sharing.
Realistic printed coupon-based thank-you card with handwritten warmth, local café/editorial stationery detail, and practical event information customers can immediately read.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Center the main thank-you message in the upper-middle 42% of the frame, with the coupon/event element anchored in the lower 28% like a tear-off voucher.
- Use a soft cream paper background with visible tactile grain, slightly warm and matte, with natural ink absorption and subtle printed imperfections.
- Compose as a real printed card photographed flat-lay on a warm café counter or textured paper surface, with small believable edge details such as a kraft tape tab, tiny stamp marks, a receipt corner, or a soft coffee-ring trace near the outer edge.
- Place {매장} as the business context in a small supporting line near the header area, and keep {이벤트} as the most prominent sales-facing text.
- Integrate {비주얼} as layered paper-cut or sticker-like elements, such as a small coupon stack, loyalty stamp row, tiny cake icon, drink cup sticker, ticket stub, or hand-drawn sparkle marks.
- Use {컬러} consistently across headers, accents, coupon borders, stamp icons, date chips, divider rules, and tiny decorative marks.
- Set {타이포} as the type direction for the headline and subline, with the main title slightly tilted or hand-drawn for a human touch.
- Maintain a clear vertical hierarchy: headline first, event details second, visual accent third, coupon/CTA last, with enough real promotional information to feel like an actual in-store event card.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
- Header area (top 18%): a short gratitude title in bold handwritten Korean, with a small English subline "Thank You" underneath in lighter weight, centered; add a tiny date label such as "2026.05 감사의 달" and a small store line using {매장}.
- Main message area (middle 24%): {이벤트} rendered as the largest text block, with the key benefit line emphasized using a stronger weight or a small highlight strip; include short Korean event copy such as "단골 5회 방문", "음료 1잔 무료", "생일 케이크" as clearly readable reward lines.
- Brand context area (upper-lower transition): {매장} shown as a small descriptor line, subtle and secondary, to clarify the venue type without overpowering the headline; include realistic micro information such as "이벤트 기간 2026.05.01–05.31", "매장 방문 고객 대상", and "문의 02-000-0000" in small Korean type.
- Visual motif area (mid-lower 22%): {비주얼} appears as a compact gratitude card stack, ticket stub, loyalty stamp card, or coupon illustration with soft shadows, slightly rounded corners, perforation dots, stamped hearts, handwritten arrows, and small sticker labels.
- Color application area: {컬러} should define the card border, divider lines, highlight chips, coupon perforation, loyalty stamp circles, CTA badge, and small accent icons such as stars, hearts, check marks, or spark marks.
- Texture area: {결} should be visible as warm paper grain, slightly rough fiber edges, letterpress-like ink pressure, stamped ink variation, and gentle ink absorption for a handcrafted printed feel.
- Footer/coupon area (bottom 26%): {비율} respected as a tall vertical layout, with a coupon-like block that feels detachable and clearly structured for quick reading; add coupon details such as "COUPON", "THANKS-05", "사용 기한 2026.05.31", "직원 확인란", a tiny QR-code-like square graphic, and a barcode-style strip area.
- Final polish: keep the whole composition aligned and balanced like a premium local-business promo card, while allowing realistic printed marks, labels, dividers, stickers, shadows, and café-stationery details to enrich the scene.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: use Pretendard Bold or Noto Sans KR Bold for the main benefit line, a hand-drawn Korean script style for the gratitude title, and a small clean sans serif for "Thank You"; headline around 54–72px, subline 18–24px, body 28–40px, micro details 12–18px.
- Color palette: cream #F6F0E6, warm amber #D98A3A, soft brown #7A5432, muted signature accent from {컬러}, and dark cocoa #3E2A1F for text.
- Border/shadow: use a thin 2px border in warm brown with a soft drop shadow of 4px y-offset, 12px blur, 15% opacity; coupon block can have a slightly stronger shadow for layered depth.
- Printed details: include dotted perforation line above the coupon, small loyalty stamp circles, tiny rule lines, date chips, a hand-written memo label, and a realistic paper edge shadow so the card feels physically printed.
- Text hierarchy: make the offer text and coupon CTA legible at first glance, while micro-copy, contact, code, and date information remain crisp enough to read up close.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: flat-lay poster look shot as a high-resolution studio still, simulated with a 50mm lens at f/5.6 for crisp text edges and gentle depth separation.
- Lighting: soft studio softbox from upper-left at about 45°, with a faint fill from the right and no harsh specular highlights.
- Color grade: warm cream + amber + cocoa with slightly desaturated midtones, like a boutique stationery brand shoot.
- Realism: show subtle paper thickness, tactile fibers, tiny ink misregistration, shallow shadow under layered stickers, and natural surface variation from the café counter or paper backing.

[6. MOOD]
Premium local-business appreciation card — Kinfolk-style stationery spread meets warm neighborhood café branding, friendly, sincere, gift-like, and ready to be placed near a cashier counter.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: 반드시 다음 문구가 또렷하게 정확히 보여야 함: "단골", "감사", "이벤트", "Thank You", "단골 5회 방문", "음료 1잔 무료", "생일 케이크".
- Additional Korean micro-copy should be clean and realistic: "2026.05 감사의 달", "이벤트 기간 2026.05.01–05.31", "매장 방문 고객 대상", "사용 기한 2026.05.31", "직원 확인란", "THANKS-05".
- Layout invariant: vertical single-card composition, with headline top-centered, offer details central, visual motif mid-lower, and coupon block bottom-anchored.
- Text must remain clean and fully legible with correct Korean character rendering, no broken glyphs.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]
- Fake official seals / certifications
- Broken Korean characters
- Celebrity composites or unauthorized likeness

studio:prompts3:ours-679.content:
[INPUT]
- language: Korean
- output_size: 1024x1536

[1. PURPOSE]
Seasonal sale poster for Black Friday, Christmas, and New Year promotions, designed as a high-impact vertical retail banner for social media, storefront signage, and mobile commerce event pages.
Bold price-led commercial layout with strong urgency, clear discount hierarchy, realistic shopping-event details, premium holiday-sales energy, and enough retail information to feel like an actual campaign poster.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Main headline zone sits in the upper 22% with oversized typography; {시즌명} is the dominant title, followed by a smaller Korean supporting line reading {세일부제}.
- Add a compact retail header above or beside the title: {매장명}, {이슈번호}, {발행일}, and a small vertical spine credit reading {스파인문구} along the left or right edge.
- Center composition uses a product collection cluster occupying the mid 48% of the frame, with {대표비주얼} arranged like a dense retail campaign collage and a large percentage mark as the focal anchor.
- {할인율} appears as the primary numerical emphasis near the center-right or center-left, sized to be readable at thumbnail scale, supported by a coupon badge showing {쿠폰코드}.
- Include 2–3 realistic feature callouts around the collage, such as {특가문구1}, {특가문구2}, and {특가문구3}, styled as small editorial sale headlines.
- {행사기간} is placed as a compact countdown/event strip in the lower 12%, visually separated from the main offer with a thin divider, boxed label, or ribbon tag.
- Add practical event details near the bottom: {장소}, {운영시간}, {구매안내}, a small barcode/QR-style block, and a sponsor/partner strip reading {후원문구}.
- Background uses a dark premium surface with festive accents, subtle wrapping-paper texture, confetti flecks, ribbon shadows, gift-tag labels, and warm reflected highlights that support the promotional hierarchy.
- {컬러팔레트} should be applied as the dominant palette across headline, accent shapes, sale badges, sponsor strip, barcode label, and highlight ribbons, with metallic gold used for premium emphasis.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
1) Top header band: set {시즌명} in a bold editorial masthead style, spanning most of the width with tight kerning and strong visual weight; place {매장명}, {이슈번호}, and {발행일} as small but readable retail-poster metadata.
2) Main offer block: place {할인율} large and central, using the biggest type on the poster, with a subtle offset shadow so it stays readable over the product collage.
3) Product collage area: build {대표비주얼} beneath and around the discount number, stacking items with slight overlap, crisp cutout edges, price-tag stickers, ribbon tabs, gift-box corners, and controlled depth layering.
4) Feature headline system: place {특가문구1}, {특가문구2}, and {특가문구3} in small boxed callouts or angled tags around the main offer, making them readable without overpowering the discount percentage.
5) Countdown and event strip: place {행사기간} inside a small rounded rectangle or slim bar near the bottom, using condensed text and a high-contrast fill for urgency; add {운영시간} nearby as a secondary line.
6) Store and purchase info: include {장소}, {구매안내}, {쿠폰코드}, barcode/QR-style graphic, and {후원문구} in a realistic retail footer area.
7) Supporting typography: add {타이포스타일} as a secondary lockup, aligned to the main hierarchy without competing with the sale percentage.
8) Color reinforcement: use {컬러팔레트} across badges, separators, corner accents, ribbon graphics, confetti, coupon labels, and background gradients to keep the whole poster in a coherent seasonal sale system.
9) Final framing: keep the layout centered and vertically balanced, with major information comfortably away from trim edges and readable on a 1024x1536 vertical canvas.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: headline in Pretendard ExtraBold or Noto Sans KR Black, 86–120px equivalent; secondary text in Pretendard SemiBold, 28–40px; countdown text in Pretendard Medium, 18–24px; footer metadata in 14–18px but still legible.
- Color palette: matte black #0B0B0D, deep red #C1121F, warm gold #D4AF37, ivory highlight #F5F1E8, optional charcoal #2B2B2F, with festive red-gold sparkle points and subtle paper-grain texture.
- Border/shadow: subtle soft drop shadow 0px x-offset, 6px y-offset, 18px blur, 18% opacity; thin gold rules 2px for separators; glossy badge sheen may appear on coupon stickers and discount tags, not as a full plastic UI.
- Poster realism: include retail artifacts such as a barcode block, coupon tag, tiny SKU-like numbers, event footer, sponsor/partner strip, ribbon corners, gift-tag labels, and sale category chips.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: high-end commercial product composite look, equivalent to a Sony A7R IV with 50mm f/1.8 for main product clarity and 85mm f/1.4 for headline depth separation.
- Lighting: studio softbox key from upper-left at 45°, weak fill from front-right, faint rim light to outline product edges and metallic highlights.
- Color grade: black velvet base with crimson and antique gold accents, slightly lifted shadows, crisp contrast, holiday campaign finish.

[6. MOOD]
Premium holiday retail campaign — a Vogue Business x Apple keynote promo aesthetic with Black Friday urgency, luxury department-store polish, festive gift-market details, and a believable limited-time shopping-event atmosphere.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: 반드시 정확히 보여야 하는 문자열: "블랙프라이데이 시즌 세일", "단 5일, 올해 마지막 쇼핑 찬스", "최대 50%", "2026.11.27 ~ 12.01 (5일)", "오전 10시 - 밤 10시", "네오마켓 강남 플래그십 & 온라인몰", "쿠폰코드: BF50", "선착순 한정 수량 · 멤버십 추가 5%", "겨울 아우터 특가", "선물세트 1+1", "오늘 밤 12시 타임딜", "NEO MARKET", "VOL.247", "2026년 11월 27일", "PROMO DESIGN BY NEO STUDIO", "제휴: 네오페이 · 로컬배송", "굵은 영문 BLACK FRIDAY + 한글 부제", "1024x1536".
- Layout invariants: large discount percentage must remain the primary focal point; countdown must stay smaller than the headline; product collage and sale badges must support the offer rather than hide it.
- Readability: all required Korean text, coupon code, event period, store name, and footer details must be sharp and fully legible at vertical poster scale.
- Realism: barcode/QR-style block, sponsor strip, date, issue number, coupon badge, category callouts, and decorative holiday graphics should feel like a real retail campaign poster.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]
- Fake official seals / government-style certifications
- Broken Korean characters
- Illegible tiny text in required sale information
- Unauthorized celebrity composites

[1. PURPOSE]
Korean store 5th anniversary commemorative card, vertical poster-style social post for in-store display and messaging channels.
Create a warm, premium retail-brand anniversary announcement that feels like a real printed celebration card, combining a realistic store photo, anniversary medal, cake illustration, event information, gratitude message, and small customer-facing details.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Main subject placement: centered vertical layout with the store celebration title occupying the upper 18%, the hero visual block in the middle 50%, and message, event, and contact details in the lower 22%.
- Background treatment: warm white and cream paper stock with visible fine grain, subtle printed ink texture, gold-accent framing elements, faint confetti speckles, and a soft shadow suggesting a premium card photographed on a tabletop.
- Spacing and framing: layered editorial card grid with rich but orderly anniversary details, realistic print alignment, readable hierarchy, and a balanced text-to-image ratio.
- Include realistic card-news style micro details: small date stamp, anniversary issue label, page-style number such as CARD 05, short Korean caption, store handle, address/contact line, and a tiny QR/ticket-style event marker.
- Use {매장·기간}, {감사 메시지}, {이벤트}, {비주얼}, {컬러}, {타이포}, {비율} placeholders as the editable content anchors.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
1. Top header area: set the anniversary title as a bold Korean masthead, with {매장·기간} placed prominently and a small English anniversary subline integrated near it. Add small supporting labels such as ‘THANK YOU WEEK’, ‘VOL.005’, ‘2026 ANNIVERSARY CARD’, and a tiny date mark ‘2026.05’.
2. Middle hero area: combine the store photo with a small 5th-anniversary medal and a cake illustration, arranged as a layered celebratory collage with realistic paper cutout edges, taped-photo corners, a gold ribbon, small balloons, flower sprigs, and subtle confetti around the frame. The store photo should show believable interior details such as counter lighting, shelves, menu board blur, packaging, and a welcoming entrance mood.
3. Message block: place {감사 메시지} beneath the hero visual in a refined centered composition using clear line breaks, accompanied by a short caption line in Korean such as ‘함께해 주신 모든 고객님께 감사드립니다’ and a tiny signature text ‘From. 우리 매장 스태프 일동’.
4. Offer block: render {이벤트} as a highlighted promotional line with gold rules, a small coupon-style badge, and additional realistic event metadata such as ‘기간 내 방문 고객 대상’, ‘매장 소진 시 조기 종료’, ‘EVENT TICKET NO. 005’, and a small QR placeholder box.
5. Footer styling: reinforce the visual identity with {컬러}, {타이포}, and {비율} in a stable, print-ready poster layout. Include a footer row with ‘주소 서울시 동네로 25’, ‘문의 @our_store’, ‘OPEN 10:00–21:00’, tiny social/share-like icons, and a small copyright-style credit line ‘Photo & Design for 5th Anniversary’.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: use a Korean serif such as Noto Serif KR or Nanum Myeongjo for the main message, paired with a clean sans-serif like Pretendard for supporting text; headline weight 700-800, body weight 400-500, with a slightly expanded tracking for the English line ‘5th Anniversary’.
- Color palette: gold #C8A24A, warm white #F7F3EA, signature store accent color, and soft charcoal #2B2B2B; keep gold as the premium accent rather than a flat neon tone.
- Border/shadow: use a subtle soft drop shadow with 4px y-offset, 12px blur, and 15% opacity; thin gold divider lines, decorative corner flourishes, foil-like medal highlights, printed coupon perforation marks, and soft paper layering.
- Text details should look professionally typeset, with Korean headline, date, event notes, handle, and footer microcopy remaining legible and aligned.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: front-facing retail poster composition, simulated with a 50mm lens look at f/4 for natural perspective and balanced product-display clarity.
- Lighting: soft diffused studio light from upper-left with a gentle fill from front-right, producing clean highlights on gold details and mild shadow separation.
- Color grade: warm cream + gold + neutral white with slightly muted contrast, similar to a polished lifestyle brand anniversary flyer.
- Material realism: visible matte paper grain, slight embossing on the 5th-anniversary medal, soft printed edges on the cake illustration, gentle reflections on the store photo surface, and believable ink density on Korean text.

[6. MOOD]
Premium neighborhood café anniversary card — feels like a refined Kinfolk-style brand print with a heartfelt local-store celebration mood, warm customer appreciation, and realistic in-store promotional details.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: must appear exactly as rendered text for {매장·기간}, {감사 메시지}, and {이벤트}.
- Additional Korean text may include realistic supporting labels such as ‘5주년 감사제’, ‘함께해 주셔서 감사합니다’, ‘방문 감사 쿠폰’, ‘기간 내 방문 고객 대상’, ‘문의 @our_store’, and ‘OPEN 10:00–21:00’.
- The composition must remain vertical, with the main title at the top, the collage visual in the middle, and the message/offer blocks clearly separated.
- Keep the store photo, medal, and cake illustration all visible and neatly layered without overlap confusion.
- Preserve the premium gold, warm cream, and signature accent color direction from {컬러}, and respect {타이포} and {비율} as the guiding design anchors.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]
- Fake official seals / certifications
- Broken Korean characters
- Celebrity composites / unauthorized likeness

[1. PURPOSE]
Grand opening poster for a storefront, vertical promotional print design for social media, street display, elevator notice boards, and in-store window posting.
Clear Korean headline hierarchy, festive launch announcement, offer blocks, venue information, opening schedule, and local promotional details.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Main subject placement: the {업종} storefront for {매장명} occupies the lower-middle 50–55% of the frame, with visible signage, entrance door, window display, sidewalk sign, flower stands, and celebratory balloons.
- Top announcement zone: place a large Korean headline in the upper 20–24%, with English "GRAND OPEN" as a supporting line and a small launch badge such as "NEW SHOP" or "OPEN WEEK".
- Central information zone: place {오픈일}, {오픈시간}, and {이벤트혜택} in layered ribbon cards, coupon labels, or rounded promotional panels that feel like realistic retail advertising.
- Environmental details: include {비주얼요소}, small confetti pieces, ribbon streamers, price-tag icons, a QR coupon card, a map-pin icon near the address, and subtle neighborhood sidewalk details.
- Footer utility zone: include {주소}, {연락처}, {SNS계정}, sponsor/support text {스폰서문구}, and a small coupon/ticket-style strip reading "OPEN COUPON 001".
- Use {매장명}, {업종}, {오픈일}, {오픈시간}, {주소}, {연락처}, {SNS계정}, {이벤트혜택}, {대표메뉴}, {스폰서문구}, {비주얼요소}, {컬러팔레트}, {타이포스타일} as editable text/content and visual-spec placeholders.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
1. Top header area (upper 18–22%): render the main title "매장 그랜드 오픈" in bold Korean, place "GRAND OPEN" directly underneath, and add a small issue-like opening badge with "OPEN WEEK / VOL.01" for a polished campaign feel.
2. Launch details band (upper-middle 12–15%): show {오픈일} and {오픈시간} in a clear date-time capsule, with a short celebratory subcopy such as "우리 동네 새 공간이 문을 엽니다".
3. Mid hero area (middle 40–45%): create a realistic illustrated or photo-composite-style exterior of {매장명}, including its storefront sign, glass reflections, flower wreaths, balloons, banner bunting, sandwich board, and {비주얼요소} arranged around the facade.
4. Offer and menu area (lower-middle 18–22%): place {이벤트혜택} in a prominent promotional box; add a smaller "대표 메뉴" panel listing {대표메뉴} and an opening coupon/ticket strip such as "선착순 쿠폰 · OPEN COUPON 001".
5. Footer information area (bottom 10–12%): include {주소}, {연락처}, {SNS계정}, {스폰서문구}, a tiny QR-code placeholder, map-pin icon, and sponsor/supporter micro logos or text blocks.
6. Whole-page polish: maintain a clear reading order from headline to date/time to storefront to offer to footer, while allowing festive retail elements, decorative graphics, and realistic store-opening details to make the poster feel commercially complete.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: use {타이포스타일}; use Pretendard ExtraBold or Noto Sans KR Black for the main Korean headline at 64–88px, a condensed uppercase sans for "GRAND OPEN" at 28–40px, and Pretendard SemiBold for event/date copy at 30–46px.
- Color palette: build from {컬러팔레트}, with white or cream base tones, warm gold accents #D8B25C or #C9A24A, and one strong brand color for ribbons, badges, balloons, and CTA buttons.
- Poster graphics: use layered paper-card panels, rounded coupon boxes, gold separator lines, small confetti, tiny spark icons, ribbon banners, hanging garlands, map-pin icon, phone icon, SNS icon, and a compact sponsor/support area.
- Storefront detail: render readable but fictional signage for {매장명}, window reflections, door handle, menu board, potted plants, flower stands with Korean congratulatory ribbons, and sidewalk textures appropriate to a local shopping street.
- Border/shadow: apply soft drop shadows under storefront, balloons, coupon panels, and paper labels, about 4px y-offset, 14px blur, 15% opacity; use thin gold dividers and sticker-like labels for hierarchy.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: polished commercial poster look, equivalent to a 35mm lens at f/5.6 for the storefront hero, with mild perspective correction so the facade stays straight.
- Lighting: bright soft daylight simulation from upper-left, with a gentle fill from front-right to keep the signage readable; add subtle specular highlights on balloons, glass windows, metallic gold accents, and glossy coupon labels.
- Color grade: crisp retail-poster finish with warm gold highlights, slightly saturated signature colors, believable shadows, tactile paper-panel overlays, and realistic storefront materials.
- Rendering approach: high-resolution Korean promotional poster design, clean vector typography combined with semi-realistic storefront illustration/photo-collage textures, suitable for 1024x1536 vertical output.

[6. MOOD]
Modern neighborhood retail launch poster — festive, welcoming, and polished Korean local-brand opening campaign aesthetic with a premium yet friendly street-level atmosphere.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy must be sharp and legible: "매장 그랜드 오픈", "그랜드 오픈", "GRAND OPEN", "오픈 기념", "우리 동네 새 공간이 문을 엽니다".
- Render key information clearly: "{매장명}", "{오픈일}", "{오픈시간}", "{주소}", "{연락처}", "{SNS계정}".
- Include realistic promotional copy: "{이벤트혜택}", "대표 메뉴: {대표메뉴}", "선착순 쿠폰", "OPEN COUPON 001".
- Add footer/support text: "{스폰서문구}", "QR 쿠폰", "오시는 길", "문의".
- Maintain a strict vertical poster hierarchy: headline first, date/time second, storefront third, offer and coupon fourth, footer information last.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]
- Fake official seals / certifications
- Broken Korean characters
- Celebrity composites or recognizable public figures
- Distorted storefront geometry

studio:prompts3:ours-675.content:
[INPUT]
- language: Korean
- output_size: 1536x1024

[1. PURPOSE]
Korean seasonal festival landscape editorial image, wide scenic composition with optional human presence, designed for magazine-style travel or cultural feature use.
Capture a Korean festival scene with seasonal landmarks, regional details, real crowd energy, and natural atmosphere, making it feel like an on-location photo essay for a premium Korean travel magazine.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Main scene occupies the middle 70% of the frame, with the horizon placed slightly above center for a spacious landscape feel.
- Use {장면} as the primary environment, rendered with clear regional identity, recognizable seasonal cues, and realistic festival infrastructure.
- Include {인물} as a supporting element, placed in the foreground or midground as visitors, couples, families, volunteers, photographers, or food-stall customers so the landscape remains dominant.
- Add believable Korean festival details: temporary information booth, banner flags, local food stalls, folding tables, safety cones, trash-sorting bins, guide map board, photo-zone sign, and small crowd clusters appropriate to {장면}.
- Background treatment should stay natural and location-realistic, with tree lines, festival crowds, riverbanks, mountain ridges, heritage rooftops, temple silhouettes, or landmark structures depending on {장면}.
- Keep {구도} broad, layered, and balanced, with a travel-editorial framing direction that feels photographed during a real public festival day.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
1. Foreground layer: Place {인물} near the lower third or side area, naturally interacting with the festival setting: taking photos, walking along the path, checking a pamphlet, carrying street food, or looking toward the seasonal landmark.
2. Midground layer: Build the festival activity around {장면} with readable seasonal details such as blossoms, foliage, lantern strings, vendor tents, walking paths, heritage rooflines, local craft booths, or riverside railings as appropriate.
3. Festival signage layer: Include realistic Korean environmental text such as a main banner reading “{축제명}”, a date placard reading “{날짜표기}”, a location label reading “{지역표기}”, and a small guide sign reading “{안내문구}”. Text should appear on physical banners, booth boards, wayfinding signs, pamphlets, or temporary event panels.
4. Local texture layer: Add ground details and tactile realism: fallen petals or leaves, paving stones, grass patches, portable mats, vendor menu boards, paper lanterns, camera straps, umbrellas, reusable cups, brochure stands, and crowd shadows.
5. Background layer: Extend the scene into distant hills, sky, river, street trees, palace walls, festival arches, bridges, or architectural silhouettes, keeping atmospheric depth soft but still clearly legible.
6. Lighting layer: Apply {조명} as an outdoor natural-light setup, with realistic shadows, sun direction, and specular highlights on banners, leaves, tents, water, or stone surfaces.
7. Color layer: Render {컬러} with authentic seasonal contrast, preserving natural greens, pinks, reds, golds, blues, browns, or winter neutrals without synthetic oversaturation.
8. Framing and finish layer: Use {구도} and apply {결} so the image feels like a refined Korean travel magazine spread with crisp environmental detail, natural crowd density, subtle film-like grain, and believable documentary texture.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: environmental Korean signage may be visible and should use clean Noto Sans KR or Pretendard-style lettering, medium to bold weight for banners and medium weight for guide boards. It must look printed or physically installed in the scene, not like a floating graphic overlay.
- Signage hierarchy: main banner “{축제명}” should be the most readable, while “{날짜표기}”, “{지역표기}”, and “{안내문구}” appear smaller on boards, flags, booth panels, or brochures.
- Color palette: seasonal real-world tones derived from {컬러}, such as cherry-blossom pink, forest green, autumn amber, maple red, stone gray, soft sky blue, hanok wood brown, festival tent cream, and muted street-market colors.
- People styling: visitors should wear realistic Korean seasonal clothing matching the scene: light spring jackets, sun hats, denim, linen shirts, autumn coats, scarves, sneakers, small backpacks, camera bags, or casual family outfits.
- Environmental realism: include authentic public-event traces such as queue ropes, safety staff vests, local vendor signs, event maps, paper cups, pamphlets, stroller wheels, bicycle racks, and casual crowd movement where appropriate.
- Material rendering: blossoms, leaves, banners, fabric tents, stone paths, metal railings, food-stall plastic covers, and wooden signboards should have tactile texture and natural imperfections.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: full-frame landscape photography look, 35mm lens at f/5.6 for broad environmental clarity and moderate depth of field.
- Lighting: outdoor natural light with golden hour glow, sun angled from upper-left or side, gentle highlights on key festival elements, soft shadow falloff across the scene.
- Color grade: editorial seasonal grade with warm highlights, balanced midtones, and slightly subdued shadows; preserve authentic local color rather than cinematic neon.
- Image texture: premium travel editorial finish with realistic optical sharpness, fine grain, natural lens contrast, subtle atmospheric haze in the distance, and no synthetic 3D-rendered surface feel.

[6. MOOD]
Premium Korean travel magazine spread — like a National Geographic Korea cultural feature with the calm realism of a refined landscape editorial, enriched by lively local festival texture, seasonal nostalgia, and the feeling of a real weekend outing.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: no broken Korean characters anywhere in the image.
- Render the main banner exactly as “{축제명}”, with supporting signs that may read “{날짜표기}”, “{지역표기}”, and “{안내문구}”.
- If menu boards, wayfinding signs, event maps, booth labels, or pamphlets appear, they must use natural Korean such as “종합안내”, “먹거리장터”, “사진촬영구역”, “화장실”, “셔틀버스”, “지역특산품”, without random gibberish.
- Maintain a wide scenic composition with landscape dominance; if {인물} is present, keep the person secondary and naturally integrated into the public festival scene.
- Preserve the intended seasonal identity of {장면} exactly, without mixing incompatible festival motifs.
- Keep the image photographic and location-realistic, with believable crowd scale, weather, signage placement, and seasonal details.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]

- Human presence: if silhouettes appear, keep them small and secondary near the lower edge, promenade, or far bank, facing the river or walking along the path, with no facial detail.

- Primary styling variables: {한복 종류}, {인물 결}, {배경}, {조명}, {컬러}, {비주얼}

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]

- Palette application: {컬러} should guide the garment accents and background harmony, with warm beige, hanji ivory, lacquer red, muted jade, or deep indigo accents that make the hanbok colors feel vivid and culturally grounded.
- Editorial finish: {비주얼} should read like a refined portrait photograph with a Korean cultural showcase feeling, including realistic fabric tactility, atmospheric background depth, and small designed portrait-card details.

[4. STYLE RULES]

[5. VISUAL STYLE]

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
- Center hero layer: {컨셉} rendered as the focal NFT-style emblem or avatar, sharply defined with neon edge glow, crisp vector-like edges, holographic highlights, and a subtle raised-card shadow.
- Secondary geometry layer: {비주얼} arranged behind and around the hero as stacked polygons, pixel fragments, orbital rings, cyber glyphs, and sci-fi interface shards, creating depth and Web3 atmosphere.

- Light accent layer: thin rim light, glow outlines, small highlight particles, and pixel sparks in {컬러} placed at key contours, especially around the top edges, eyes/emblem points, and outer silhouette.

[4. STYLE RULES]

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]

- Finish language: {스타일결} expressed through refined edges, realistic fabrics, wood grain, brushed polymer, translucent glass, soft UI reflections, and practical home technology rather than exaggerated cyberpunk effects.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
1) Foreground: place a low table, sofa edge, tablet, mug, toy block, and folded throw blanket to establish domestic scale and make the scene feel inhabited.
2) Midground center: depict the core interaction of {주제} inside {장면}; the humanoid robot may be handing a cup, helping with a schedule, monitoring a child’s homework tablet, or controlling home lighting while human figures respond naturally.
3) Supporting elements: include smart speaker, wall climate panel, small indoor delivery drone on a dock, autonomous vacuum, transparent recipe display, health sensor band, and subtle exterior cue such as an autonomous vehicle visible beyond the window.

6) Color emphasis: apply {컬러팔레트} through interface lights, robot status indicators, display panels, reflected cyan edges, warm oak midtones, and natural daylight on furniture.
7) Typography zone: integrate the text into a glass wall display, floating AR card, or keynote-style lower third using {타이포}; include a small footer credit “{하단크레딧}” as if this were an editorial technology concept slide.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: Pretard or Noto Sans KR, medium to semibold weight, 28–42px equivalent for headline and callout labels, 16–22px equivalent for date/location/footer, modern UI-like clarity with precise Korean spacing.
- Color palette: white #F7F8FA, warm oak #C9A77D, cool cyan #4ED8E6, pale gray #D8DDE3, soft graphite #2E3137, warm skin tones, muted plant green #7A9272.
- Graphic treatment: use translucent glassmorphism panels, soft ambient occlusion, subtle UI glow, small rounded information chips, status dots, thin connector lines, and realistic screen reflections on nearby surfaces.

- Lighting: large diffused daylight from left-side windows at 45°, gentle fill from the right, faint cyan UI glow on nearby surfaces, soft reflections on glass and polymer, no harsh specular highlights.
- Color grade: clean white balance with slight cool cyan lift in the shadows and warm wood retention in midtones, controlled contrast, premium product-photography finish.
- Realism cue: humanoid joints, hands, facial sensor area, fabric contact shadows, device ports, charging cables, and family body language must feel mechanically and anatomically plausible.

[6. MOOD]
Apple keynote-meets-Kinfolk home editorial — calm future-living optimism with a believable premium consumer-tech aesthetic, warm family presence, and practical next-generation AI assistance.

- Composition invariant: wide horizontal framing, balanced household scene, realistic coexistence of human and robot elements, and a premium future-living atmosphere must remain consistent.

- Rendered Korean must be legible, correctly spaced, and integrated into the environment as smart-wall UI, AR caption, or presentation lower-third text.

- Broken Korean characters
- Celebrity composites or recognizable public figures

[1. PURPOSE]
Metaverse / VR virtual space concept image for promotional key art or concept presentation. Wide-format scene with a futuristic digital environment, avatar character, immersive UI overlay, and realistic event-promotion information rendered as part of the virtual world.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Main scene: a broad virtual interior space based on {가상공간}, designed as a panoramic environment with strong depth, layered foreground / midground / background separation, and a lively simulation atmosphere.
- Subject placement: {아바타} positioned as the visual focal point in the central 40–55% of the frame, surrounded by interactive kiosks, floating name tags, portal gates, and holographic interface panels.
- Promotional identity: integrate a large Korean title banner reading {메인타이틀}, a short subtitle reading {서브카피}, and event-detail blocks for {행사일시}, {가상장소}, and {티켓정보} as glowing signage inside the virtual space.
- Background treatment: glossy futuristic surfaces, volumetric haze, digital grid floors, portal arches, avatar silhouettes, neon signboards, and distant world modules that reinforce the sci-fi simulation setting.
- Format: maintain a cinematic wide composition suited to {비율}, with the title and UI content balanced across the architecture rather than isolated on a blank backdrop.
- Overall surface language should follow {시각스타일} and the palette of {컬러팔레트}, while maintaining readable silhouette contrast against the environment.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
- Background layer: construct a large-scale virtual architecture or environment based on {가상공간}, with perspective lines, glowing floor tiles, curved LED walls, portal doors, avatar traffic, and repeating digital grid patterns.
- Mid layer: place {아바타} in a clearly readable pose, using a stylized cyber or mini SD character treatment depending on the selected default, with clean outline separation from the background.
- Foreground layer: add floating UI overlay panels, holographic icons, status bars, transparent interface frames, mini-map widgets, chat bubbles, quest cards, and user-status chips emphasizing a metaverse dashboard look.
- Information layer: include realistic Korean UI labels such as world code {월드코드}, user status {UI상태}, channel handle {채널핸들}, sponsor area {후원표기}, and small wayfinding signs like “입장 대기”, “월드 선택”, “라이브 스테이지”, “아바타 라운지”.
- Accent layer: distribute neon edge lights, scan-line highlights, particle trails, emoji-like reaction icons, QR-style ticket blocks, translucent badges, and light particles in cyan, pink, purple, lime, and white to reinforce {컬러팔레트} and {시각스타일}.
- Typography layer: integrate {타이포스타일} into the environment as LED signage, glass-panel UI, and dashboard labels, with clear hierarchy between title, event details, and small technical UI text.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: use Pretendard or Noto Sans KR for Korean text, and a clean sci-fi sans such as Eurostile or Orbitron for English accents; weights around 600–800 for titles and 400–600 for UI labels.
- Color palette: use deep charcoal and navy base tones with neon cyan #00E5FF, hot pink #FF4FD8, electric purple #8A5CFF, lime #B7FF4A, and white #FFFFFF.
- Border/shadow: thin translucent interface borders with subtle glow, plus soft drop shadows 4px y-offset, 14px blur, 18% opacity for panels, avatar separation, and holographic ticket cards.
- Detail density: fill the world with believable metaverse details such as portal signage, headset check-in kiosks, friend-list panels, mini profile cards, chat notifications, event countdowns, and decorative circuit patterns while keeping primary text legible.
- Korean text layout: align Korean text in clean rectangular panels or LED strips; avoid tiny dense paragraphs for important text, but allow small pseudo-UI microcopy around the edges.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: wide 24mm virtual camera look, slight isometric feel, deep perspective, f/4 equivalent for balanced sharpness across the scene.
- Lighting: studio-like neon illumination with main cyan light from upper-left, magenta rim light from the right, and faint underglow from the floor grid.
- Color grade: dark sci-fi base with neon cyan / pink / purple / lime highlights, crisp white UI accents, and controlled bloom around emissive edges.
- Rendering texture: polished game-key-art finish with glass reflections, brushed metal trim, semi-transparent hologram material, luminous grid lines, soft particle depth, and readable avatar material details.

[6. MOOD]
High-tech metaverse showcase — a cyberpunk exhibition render with the clarity of a futuristic game UI, the energy of a virtual launch event, and the polish of a premium VR product teaser.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Render the Korean title exactly as “{메인타이틀}” and the subtitle exactly as “{서브카피}”.
- Include visible Korean event details: “{행사일시}”, “{가상장소}”, “{티켓정보}”, and “{후원표기}”.
- Include metaverse UI text labels such as “{UI상태}”, “{월드코드}”, “{채널핸들}”, “입장 대기”, “월드 선택”, “아바타 라운지”, and “라이브 스테이지” without broken Korean characters.
- Composition invariants: wide virtual space + avatar + UI overlay + Korean promotional signage must all be present; maintain strong depth layering and readable focal hierarchy.
- Avoid realistic human deformation; if a human-like avatar appears, keep anatomy clean, stylized, and intentionally designed.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]

- Broken Korean characters

- Layout framing: editorial poster structure with a left-side headline/info stack and right-side lifestyle scene, using layered travel-magazine details such as issue label, date stamp, small captions, map-pin icons, divider rules, barcode area, and publisher credit.
- Add realistic lifestyle context: a half-finished iced coffee, local café menu board in the background, small table number, sunlight on the tabletop, faint outdoor scooter or palm silhouette through the window, and subtle paper grain / print texture.
- Use {도시}, {월 비용}, {일·시간}, {비주얼}, {컬러}, {발행처}, {비율} as the customizable text elements.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
- Top header band (upper 15%): set the title as a bold Korean masthead: “디지털 노마드 라이프”, centered or slightly left-aligned, with strong hierarchy and wide tracking. Add small magazine-style labels around it: “REMOTE WORK GUIDE”, “VOL.247”, “2026년 5월호”.
- City line (next 10%): place {도시} beneath the title as a concise destination descriptor, smaller than the masthead but still prominent. Add a small map-pin marker and short Korean subline such as “한 달 살아보기 도시 리포트”.
- Cost block (mid-upper 15%): present {월 비용} as a clear info line, with supporting micro labels such as “월 예상 생활비”, “숙소·카페·교통 포함”, and small divider rules in muted brown-gray.
- Daily routine block (mid 15%): show {일·시간} as a short schedule line, visually aligned with the cost block. Add two or three compact routine tags in Korean, e.g. “오전 집중 업무”, “오후 코워킹”, “저녁 로컬 산책”.
- Visual scene area (middle 30%): depict {비주얼} as the main lifestyle image, with the figure integrated naturally into the café setting and the laptop clearly visible. Include realistic café objects, tropical plants, window reflections, textured wall surfaces, and warm wooden furniture.
- Feature blurb strip (lower-mid 10%): include 2–3 short Korean editorial blurbs like “체류 예산 체크”, “카페 워크 루틴”, “주말 근교 여행”, styled as small travel-magazine cover lines.
- Palette cue and finish (lower-mid 10%): reflect {컬러} through the overall materials, wardrobe tones, furniture, foliage, small stickers, accent shapes, and warm atmosphere. Add a small label reading “COLOR NOTE: {컬러}”.
- Footer mark (bottom 5%): include {발행처} as a subtle publisher tag, like a magazine credit line. Add a small barcode block, “ISSN 2026-05”, “FORMAT {비율}”, tiny credit text “Photo essay / Nomad field note”, and a compact CTA such as “저장하고 다음 여행 준비”.
- The layout should feel structured like a modern travel/editorial poster, with believable publication details and lifestyle atmosphere rather than a flat ad banner.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: Pretendard or Noto Sans KR for the main body, Bold 800 for the title, SemiBold 600 for sublines, size hierarchy roughly 72–84 px title, 28–36 px supporting text, 18–22 px footer, and 12–16 px micro editorial labels.
- Color palette: beige, warm wood brown, natural leaf green, and amber accents; concrete neutrals and off-white paper tones should keep the layout airy but tactile. Suggested anchors: #F4E8D8, #B88A5A, #6E8B5B, #D9A15B, #F7F2EA.
- Border/shadow: modern editorial treatment with soft drop shadow 4px y-offset, 14px blur, 12% opacity; thin separator rules in muted brown-gray; add subtle paper grain, faint print registration marks, small rounded info cards, and warm translucent accent blocks.
- Graphic details: use restrained travel-guide decoration such as map-pin icons, tiny route lines, small sticker labels, café receipt fragments, page number “p.06”, and a barcode area without overpowering the main photograph.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: 35mm documentary-style café shot or 50mm f/1.8 environmental portrait, framed like a lifestyle magazine spread.
- Lighting: soft daylight from a large window on the left, gentle fill from the front, subtle warm bounce off wood surfaces, realistic highlights on coffee glass and laptop edge, no harsh flash.
- Color grade: warm cream + beige + sage green + amber, with slightly muted contrast and a clean travel-journal finish.
- Realism cues: natural skin texture, believable fabric folds, realistic laptop reflections, readable printed poster text, textured plaster wall, individual plant leaves, wood grain, and slight depth of field separating the figure from the café background.

[6. MOOD]
Premium digital nomad lifestyle editorial — a cross between Kinfolk travel spread, modern Nomad List social content, and a practical Korean city-guide poster. Polished, grounded, aspirational, and lived-in, as if documenting a real remote-work morning in {도시}.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: 반드시 아래 문구가 정확히 보여야 함: “디지털 노마드 라이프”, “{도시}”, “{월 비용}”, “{일·시간}”, “{비주얼}”, “{컬러}”, “{발행처}”, “{비율}”.
- Additional Korean text must be crisp and correctly rendered, including: “REMOTE WORK GUIDE”, “VOL.247”, “2026년 5월호”, “한 달 살아보기 도시 리포트”, “월 예상 생활비”, “숙소·카페·교통 포함”, “오전 집중 업무”, “오후 코워킹”, “저녁 로컬 산책”, “체류 예산 체크”, “카페 워크 루틴”, “주말 근교 여행”, “저장하고 다음 여행 준비”.
- Composition invariant: maintain the left-text / right-visual balance, with the café scene, laptop, nature elements, realistic travel details, and side-profile figure all present.

Designed to explain Notion, Zapier, and Bubble workflow basics for beginners, creators, and small teams, while looking like an actual workshop guide poster or downloadable resource cover.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Center layout: a tall poster composition with the main title in the upper 18%, a practical guide metadata strip below it, a three-tool visual cluster in the center 46%, and step boxes plus CTA details in the lower 26%.
- Background treatment: matte white base with subtle light-gray paper grain, faint folded-poster texture, thin charcoal divider lines, small accent blocks using {컬러}, tiny UI dots, arrows, connector lines, and sticker-like labels that support the workflow theme.
- Printed-poster details: add a small issue/date label such as "VOL.024", "2026년 5월호", a tiny barcode or QR-code area labeled "가이드 저장", and a publisher credit line using {발행처}.
- Information density: include short Korean feature blurbs, small section markers, tool labels, micro captions, and a footer info row so the image feels like a finished editorial guide rather than a blank mockup.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
- Header zone (top 18%): place the main title as a bold Korean masthead, with a smaller subtitle line directly beneath it using {도구}. Add small metadata around the masthead: "VOL.024", "2026년 5월호", "BEGINNER GUIDE", and "노코드 자동화 입문".
- Context line (top-mid 10%): set {활용 사례} as a compact descriptor in a lighter weight, supported by two or three short Korean blurbs such as "반복 업무 줄이기", "데이터 연결하기", "아이디어를 앱으로".
- Hero visual zone (mid 46%): show a 3-part cluster with stylized representations of Notion, Zapier, and Bubble, paired with a miniature screen mockup suggesting a workflow dashboard; include realistic dashboard details such as connected cards, small table rows, progress chips, calendar blocks, automation arrows, and labeled nodes reading "DB", "Trigger", "Action", "App". Keep the tools as editorial icon illustrations and UI cards, not copied brand artwork.
- Visual note area: place {비주얼} as a small caption tag near the dashboard, like a design annotation or sticky label.
- Step section (lower 26%): render {단계} as four evenly spaced rounded boxes or numbered chips, each with clear hierarchy and consistent spacing. Add short supporting labels inside or below the chips: "01 정리", "02 연결", "03 자동화", "04 배포".
- CTA and details band: add a narrow event/resource strip with "무료 체크리스트", "신청 QR", "소요 시간 30분", "권장 비율 {비율}" and a small ticket-style label reading "SAVE THIS GUIDE".
- Footer zone (bottom 8%): place {발행처} as a publisher mark or social handle, plus small spine/credit text such as "No-code Starter Series / Design notes / 2026" and a barcode-style block aligned to one corner.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: use Pretendard Bold for the title, Pretendard Medium for body labels, and Noto Sans KR Regular for small metadata; title size should feel poster-large, body text compact and highly legible.
- Color palette: matte white #FFFFFF, charcoal #222222, soft gray #E9E9E9, plus small accent touches pulled from {컬러}; include restrained Notion black-white, Zapier orange, and Bubble blue-inspired accents in tiny UI elements.
- Border/shadow: thin 1px charcoal rules, subtle card shadows with 0px x-offset, 4px y-offset, 10px blur, 12% opacity; add realistic paper edge softness and slight ink density variation.
- Graphic details: use arrows, dotted connector paths, numbered badges, tiny tabs, page markers, sticky-note shapes, sponsor/resource blocks, and compact caption labels to create a credible guide-poster layout.
- Text hierarchy: every headline and key label must remain readable at poster scale, while secondary metadata can be smaller like real printed editorial matter.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: 50mm standard editorial framing, front-facing graphic layout, no perspective distortion.
- Lighting: soft studio light from upper-left with even fill, gentle card shadows for separation, and realistic matte paper surface response.
- Color grade: clean white-and-charcoal base with selective signature accents from Notion, Zapier, and Bubble-inspired hues.
- Rendering: high-resolution printed poster realism, crisp vector-like typography, tactile paper grain, precise alignment, detailed UI micro-elements, and believable ink-on-paper texture.

[6. MOOD]

[7. CRITICAL]

[1. PURPOSE]
Korean AI tool comparison card for social media carousel, blog thumbnail, or newsletter feature image, presented as a polished vertical editorial infographic.
3-column comparison layout for ChatGPT, Claude, and Gemini with quick at-a-glance evaluation, practical notes, update metadata, and shareable card-news details.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Vertical poster composition: three equal columns across the page, each column occupying about 30% width with 5% gutters, framed by a refined thin outer rule and realistic printed-card edge treatment.
- Top headline band takes 14% of height, main comparison grid takes 72%, bottom recommendation strip takes 14%.
- Use {비교 도구}, {비교 항목}, {강점·약점}, {추천}, {비주얼}, {컬러}, {비율} as editable text content.
- Background should be crisp white with subtle paper grain, faint off-white editorial texture, charcoal dividers, and restrained accent colors per tool.
- Add realistic social-card metadata: top-left small label “AI TOOL GUIDE”, top-right “VOL.03 · 2026.05 업데이트”, a tiny handle “@ai.notes.kr”, and a slide marker “01 / 05” near the lower corner.
- Include small save/share/bookmark micro icons and hashtag-like footer text such as “#AI도구 #업무자동화 #생산성팁” while keeping the 3-column comparison dominant.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
- Header area (top 14%): set the main title as a bold Korean masthead, centered, with compact line spacing and strong hierarchy. Main headline must read “AI 도구 비교”; add a smaller subtitle line: “대화·코딩·이미지·긴 문맥까지 한 장으로 정리”.
- Comparison grid (middle 72%): build exactly 3 vertical cards side by side; each card contains one tool name at the top, a small circular or rounded-square icon area beneath, then 3–5 short bullet lines for strengths, weaknesses, and quick use-case notes.
- Above the cards, place {비교 도구} and {비교 항목} as readable supporting labels, styled like small category tabs: “비교 도구: ChatGPT · Claude · Gemini” and “비교 항목: 대화 / 코딩 / 이미지 / 가격 / 언어”.
- Tool 1 card: place ChatGPT content in the left column with green accent bars, checklist dots, a compact score row, and small Korean tags such as “다재다능”, “일상 질문”, “빠른 초안”; keep the card balanced and evenly padded.
- Tool 2 card: place Claude content in the center column with beige accent bars, document-style marks, a compact score row, and small Korean tags such as “긴 문맥”, “코딩”, “문서 분석”; match the same text hierarchy as the other cards.
- Tool 3 card: place Gemini content in the right column with blue accent bars, subtle sparkle/geometric marks, a compact score row, and small Korean tags such as “멀티모달”, “이미지”, “구글 연동”; maintain equal visual weight.
- In each card, add a tiny “BEST FOR” ribbon and short Korean line: ChatGPT “일상 업무·아이디어”, Claude “코딩·긴 문서”, Gemini “이미지·검색 연동”.
- Add a small row of evaluation chips inside each card for “대화”, “코딩”, “이미지”, “가격”, “언어” using dots, short bars, or 5-step markers rather than long paragraphs.
- Recommendation strip (bottom 14%): show {추천} inside a high-contrast bar or rounded label row, with the exact conclusion sentence “코딩 = Claude / 일상 = ChatGPT / 멀티모달 = Gemini”.
- Below the recommendation sentence, add a subtle CTA line: “저장해두고 상황별로 골라 쓰기” plus a tiny source/date note “업데이트 기준: 2026.05 · 개인 사용 시나리오 기준”.
- Use {비주얼}, {컬러}, and {비율} as small production-note labels in the lower metadata area or side note, integrated naturally without creating extra panels.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: use Pretendard or Noto Sans KR for all Korean text; headline weight 800–900, body weight 500–600, small labels 400–500. Keep letter spacing tight and clean.
- Color palette: white #FFFFFF, charcoal #1F1F1F, ChatGPT green #10A37F, Claude beige #D8C3A5, Gemini blue #4285F4, light gray #EAECEF for separators.
- Border/shadow: thin 1px charcoal rules, soft drop shadow 4px y-offset, 12px blur, 12% opacity for the cards; no heavy neon glow.
- Add editorial details such as hairline dividers, tiny page-number text, small corner brackets, check icons, rating dots, and lightly textured paper fibers to make the card feel like a finished magazine-style infographic.
- Icons should be simple original geometric marks inspired by each tool category, not official certification marks; brand names “ChatGPT”, “Claude”, and “Gemini” must remain clearly readable.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: clean editorial flat graphic layout, top-down poster design feel, simulated with crisp vector-like rendering rather than photographic depth.
- Lighting: even studio-like illumination with gentle contact shadows around the printed card edges, giving a realistic premium social-media graphic finish while keeping all text readable.
- Color grade: neutral white base with controlled accent saturation in green, beige, and blue; overall balanced and modern.
- Rendering quality: high-resolution digital editorial design, sharp typography, realistic paper texture, precise grid alignment, tactile card layering, and polished UI-thumbnail clarity.

[6. MOOD]
Practical editorial comparison sheet — like a polished Notion-style infographic mixed with a sharp product roundup from The Verge, upgraded into a saved-worthy Korean Instagram carousel card with useful real-world labels and decision cues.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: 반드시 정확히 보여야 하는 문자열 — “AI 도구 비교”, “ChatGPT”, “Claude”, “Gemini”, “대화”, “코딩”, “이미지”, “가격”, “언어”, “다재다능”, “긴 문맥”, “멀티모달”, “코딩 = Claude / 일상 = ChatGPT / 멀티모달 = Gemini”.
- Additional Korean microcopy must be clean and legible: “VOL.03 · 2026.05 업데이트”, “AI TOOL GUIDE”, “@ai.notes.kr”, “저장해두고 상황별로 골라 쓰기”, “#AI도구 #업무자동화 #생산성팁”.
- Layout invariant: exactly 3 columns, one tool per column, with equal visual weight and no extra fourth panel.
- All Korean text must be clean, correctly spelled, and fully legible.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]
- Fake official seals / certifications
- Broken Korean characters
- Celebrity composites / unauthorized likeness

Each card must include a number 01–05, one trend label from {트렌드목록}, one concise example from {사례문구}, and a simple icon.

6. Footer publishing strip (bottom 10%): Include {페이지표시}, {해시태그}, {출처문구}, and a CTA pill with {CTA}. Add tiny save/share micro icons and a subtle carousel cue, making it feel like a real Instagram card-news cover.

[4. STYLE RULES]

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: Clean graphic editorial layout, simulated top-down design presentation, like a contemporary magazine infographic rather than a photographed scene.
- Lighting: Bright even studio-like illumination with no harsh shadows; subtle contrast only, keeping white areas crisp and colored blocks vivid.
- Color grade: High-chroma contemporary palette with fresh social-media brightness, balanced by charcoal text, warm off-white panels, and vivid accent cards.

[6. MOOD]
Modern Korean trend-report editorial — feels like a smart Seoul youth-culture publication prepared for an Instagram carousel, with crisp infographic energy, practical insight, and a polished magazine-card finish.

[7. CRITICAL]
- 반드시 선명하게 렌더링할 한국어 텍스트: {주제}, {부제}, {트렌드목록}, {사례문구}, {발행처}, {채널핸들}, {호수}, {날짜}, {페이지표시}, {해시태그}, {CTA}.

studio:prompts3:ours-661.content:
[INPUT]
- language: Korean
- output_size: 1024x1536

[1. PURPOSE]
Instagram story music share card for a song post, designed as a vertical 9:16 visual with album-art-first composition, realistic social-story UI, and detailed playback information.
Create a shareable music moment that feels like a streaming app snippet captured inside an Instagram story, with atmospheric album-inspired background, tiny platform interface cues, and Korean caption details.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Center the main album artwork and artist image stack to occupy roughly 52% of the frame height, with the track title area above and playback controls below.
- Background treatment: dark blurred bokeh derived from the album art, with a deep charcoal-to-black gradient wash, soft vignette at the corners, faint light leaks, and subtle texture like a real phone-screen share graphic.
- Add a realistic Instagram story frame layer: top status time, thin story progress bar, profile handle area, tiny more/share icons, and a bottom reply pill, all secondary to the music card.
- Include social-card details around the central column: small Korean mood label, hashtag-style caption, save/share micro icons, and a subtle sticker tag that matches {컬러}.
- Use {곡·아티스트}, {앨범 자켓}, {재생 정보}, {배경}, {컬러}, {비율} as variable elements in a fixed music-card layout.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
1. Top platform zone (upper 8%): render an Instagram-story-like header with a thin segmented progress line, small circular profile thumbnail, handle text @daily.sound, timestamp 21:37, and tiny icons for sound, more, and share.
2. Top title zone (upper 18%): place {곡·아티스트} in crisp Korean-readable text, aligned center, with compact tracking and a strong hierarchy over the dark background; add a small label above it reading 오늘의 무드 and a tiny tag reading 지금 재생 중.
3. Central media zone (middle 42%): show {앨범 자켓} as the hero element, framed like a premium streaming-card preview with a soft glass reflection, realistic print texture, rounded corners, and depth shadow separating it from the blurred background.
4. Playback zone (lower-middle 16%): render {재생 정보} beneath the artwork, using a thin progress line, a filled progress segment, elapsed/remaining time marks such as 01:24 and 03:48, a pause icon button, previous/next controls, and small shuffle/repeat icons.
5. Social caption zone (lower 14%): add a bottom story reply pill reading 메시지 보내기, a small sticker-style caption reading 밤 산책 플레이리스트, hashtags #지금듣는노래 #플레이리스트, and tiny save/share micro icons.
6. Background zone (full frame): build {배경} using heavy blur, soft bokeh light specks, low-contrast gradient, faint album-color reflections, and subtle grain so the foreground card remains legible and cinematic.
7. Palette application: use {컬러} to drive the accent colors for the progress bar, title highlight, sticker outline, icon glow, and small interface details, while keeping the rest in dark neutral tones.
8. Ratio lock: maintain {비율} composition with all elements vertically stacked and centered for an Instagram story-friendly silhouette.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: Pretendard and Noto Sans KR, medium to bold weight, title around 54–68px, playback text around 24–28px, micro UI labels around 16–20px, with sharp anti-aliased Korean glyphs.
- Color palette: combine the album’s signature hues from {컬러} with near-black #111111, charcoal #1B1B1F, off-white #F3F3F1, muted gray #8A8A92, and dim translucent UI overlays.
- Border/shadow: apply a soft drop shadow with 4px y-offset, 14px blur, 18% opacity under the album artwork and controls; use subtle rounded glass panels and faint inner highlights for a real app-share feel.
- UI realism: include tiny status indicators, a story progress bar, profile handle, reply field, and micro icons, but keep them visually lighter than the album artwork and song information.
- Texture: add fine screen grain, faint compression glow around bright text, and soft bokeh blooming in the background to make the image feel like a real social-media music post.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: clean digital mockup look inspired by a 50mm f/1.8 product-style crop, as if a music card were photographed front-on and then refined into a UI poster.
- Lighting: low-key studio lighting with a softbox from upper-left at 45°, faint rim light from upper-right, and controlled falloff into the corners.
- Color grade: dark cinematic grade with deep blacks, slightly lifted midtones, and accent hues matching the album art; keep whites neutral, not warm.
- Rendering: high-resolution mobile-story design with realistic glass blur, layered shadows, subtle screen reflections, and polished Korean typography.

[6. MOOD]
Indie streaming-app editorial — refined like a Spotify story card meets a moody A24 music-promo poster, with the feeling of sharing a favorite song late at night.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: 반드시 아래 문자열이 정확히 보여야 함.
  - {곡·아티스트}
  - {재생 정보}
- Additional Korean text may appear and must be readable: 오늘의 무드, 지금 재생 중, 밤 산책 플레이리스트, 메시지 보내기, #지금듣는노래, #플레이리스트.
- The artwork must remain vertically centered and readable; progress bar, pause button, time marks, handle, reply pill, and text hierarchy must match a realistic Instagram music-share story layout.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]
- Fake official seals / certifications
- Broken Korean characters
- Celebrity composites / unauthorized likeness
