args.default: 앨범 자켓 흐릿한 보케 + 어두운 그라디언트

studio:prompts3:ours-660.content:
[INPUT]
- language: Korean
- output_size: {비율}

[1. PURPOSE]
SNS 좋아요·댓글 화면 mockup poster for social media presentation, showing a realistic mobile social post UI with engagement metrics, caption activity, comments, save/share controls, and platform-native micro details.
Designed as a vertical smartphone-screen style graphic for marketing mockups, portfolio samples, influencer campaign proposals, brand report thumbnails, or UI concept previews.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Center one large mobile SNS post screen in a 1024x1536 vertical frame, with the interface occupying most of the canvas like a premium screenshot presentation board.
- Use {플랫폼} as the platform-specific base UI, adapting top navigation, icon rhythm, reaction style, and tab/footer behavior to feel familiar for that platform.
- Build the screen from top to bottom: {상단 상태바}, platform title/navigation row, account header, main post image, engagement row, caption, comments preview, date/location metadata, and bottom interaction bar.
- Use {계정명} and {핸들} in the account row with a circular avatar, story-ring accent, follow/option affordance, and a small {프로필 라벨} descriptor.
- Place {게시물 이미지} as the main visual content area, sized large enough to read as a real post preview rather than a blank placeholder.
- Display engagement metrics prominently: {좋아요 수}, {댓글 수}, {공유 수}, plus save/share micro icons and small reaction indicators.
- Put {캡션} below the engagement row, followed by {해시태그} in a native social-caption style.
- Insert {댓글 목록} in the lower comment area as readable Korean comment lines, each with small avatar dots, usernames, timestamps, like hearts, and reply links.
- Add {날짜 위치} as compact metadata near the bottom, including a realistic date, time, and location label.
- Apply {UI 스타일} to interface accents, separators, buttons, story ring, active icon, and notification dots.
- Use {컬러 팔레트} for the UI palette, balancing white app surfaces, charcoal text, gray metadata, and platform accent color.
- Set {타이포그래피} throughout labels, counters, comments, timestamps, and icon labels with a crisp app-screen hierarchy.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
- Status/navigation area: show battery, signal, time, platform wordmark/title, search or DM icon, and a compact notification badge.
- Account header: circular profile image placeholder, {계정명}, {핸들}, {프로필 라벨}, location microtext, follow button, and three-dot menu arranged like a native SNS post.
- Main content block: a large square or portrait post preview occupying the upper-middle section, using {게시물 이미지} with realistic photo texture, crop marks from the app frame, and a subtle media carousel indicator if appropriate.
- Engagement row: reaction icons, like count {좋아요 수}, comment count {댓글 수}, share count {공유 수}, bookmark/save icon, and a tiny row of liked-by avatar circles.
- Caption block: {계정명} in bold followed by {캡션}, then {해시태그} in muted blue or platform accent.
- Comment preview: render {댓글 목록} as two to four stacked Korean comment lines with usernames, short replies, small heart icons, and timestamps such as 12분, 1시간, 어제.
- Metadata line: show {날짜 위치} in small gray text, including date, posting time, and location-style label.
- Footer controls: include home, search, upload, reels/media, profile icons or the equivalent for {플랫폼}, plus a bottom gesture bar for smartphone realism.
- Presentation frame: add a soft phone-screen shadow and a subtle blurred platform-color backdrop behind the UI so it reads as a designed mockup poster.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: use Pretendard or Noto Sans KR for interface text, with bold 700 for account name and counters, medium 500 for labels, regular 400 for comments, and metadata at 18–24 px equivalent.
- Color palette: platform-native accent tones from {컬러 팔레트} plus white #FFFFFF, charcoal #222222, soft gray #E9E9E9, muted divider gray #D6D6D6, and notification red #FF3B30.
- Border/shadow: thin 1px divider lines, rounded card corners 18px, soft drop shadow 0px 8px 24px rgba(0,0,0,0.08), and subtle inner separation between post sections.
- UI realism: include small touch-target spacing, native icon alignment, realistic text truncation only where app UIs naturally truncate account labels, and clear hierarchy between primary content and metadata.
- Korean copy: every visible Korean label, caption, comment, date, and hashtag must be spelled correctly and rendered as legible Hangul.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: flat editorial UI render, straight-on front view, simulated smartphone screenshot composition with no perspective tilt.
- Lighting: even studio-style screen illumination, no dramatic highlights, clean diffuse brightness across the interface.
- Color grade: platform-native clean white UI with charcoal text, lightly saturated accent color, and controlled contrast for readable small text.
- Render quality: high-resolution app mockup with sharp vector-like UI edges, crisp icons, realistic phone-screen density, and polished product-preview finish.

[6. MOOD]
Premium social-media UI mockup — lively, credible, and campaign-ready, like a polished Figma presentation slide, influencer report visual, or App Store preview board with real engagement energy.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Render readable Korean UI text including: 소담리뷰, @sodam.review, 좋아요 1,248개, 댓글 312개 모두 보기, 공유 58회, 저장, 답글 달기, 2026.05.01 · 서울 성수동.
- Caption example must remain crisp: 오늘 발견한 작은 취향 기록. 저장해두고 주말에 다시 보기 좋은 리스트예요.
- Comment examples must remain legible: 지민: 이거 진짜 미쳤음 ㅠㅠ / 하린: 어디서 샀어요? / 민수: 저장 완료, 친구한테 공유함.
- Include hashtag-style text such as #성수핫플 #오늘의발견 #리뷰그램 and keep all Hangul, numbers, and punctuation unbroken.
- Must preserve the visible SNS interface feel with readable counters, comment text, handle, date/location label, micro icons, and platform-like structure.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]
- Fake official seals / certifications
- Broken Korean characters
- Blurry, warped, or unreadable UI text
- Celebrity face composites or real person identity alteration

[INPUT]
- language: Korean
- output_size: 1536x1024

[1. PURPOSE]
Challenge before/after comparison graphic for fitness, dieting, or hairstyle transformation. Landscape social card with a split-screen progress story, designed to make change feel measurable, personal, and shareable like a real transformation post.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Main layout: strict 좌우 분할 50:50 composition, with {비포} on the left and {애프터} on the right, separated by a bold center divider and a small arrow pointing from left to right.
- Subject scale: each side should occupy about 42% of the frame width, leaving a narrow central lane for the arrow, stat badges, and challenge markers.
- Background treatment: bright editorial white and cool-gray base with realistic paper-card grain, faint measurement ticks, calendar marks, soft photo shadows, and small wellness-related visual cues that support the transformation theme.
- Framing direction: keep both sides aligned on the same baseline so body shape, hair silhouette, or pose change is easy to compare; preserve similar camera distance and crop between the left and right panels.
- Use {챌린지}, {기간 정보}, {비주얼}, {컬러} as the customizable text and layout directions.
- Add social-card realism: include a small profile strip, handle text “@daily_challenge”, slide number “01/03”, tiny save/share icons, and a compact date label “2026.05.01 기록”.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
1) Top header band: place the title text “챌린지 비포·애프터” across the upper 12–15% of the canvas in a clean editorial banner style, with a small issue-style label such as “WEEKLY PROGRESS NOTE” and “VOL.247”.
2) Social metadata row: under or beside the header, add “챌린지” as a category pill, the value {챌린지} as the challenge subtitle, “@daily_challenge”, “01/03”, and tiny micro icons for save/share/comment.
3) Left panel: render {비포} as a realistic everyday starting-point photo with honest natural lighting, casual posture, and context details appropriate to {비주얼} such as a gym mirror edge, bathroom scale, tape measure, comb, towel, water bottle, or calendar note.
4) Right panel: render {애프터} with visible improvement cues—sharper posture, cleaner styling, more defined shape, refreshed haircut finish, or more polished grooming depending on the challenge type—while keeping the same person, crop, and stance comparable.
5) Center connector: place a thick arrow or stacked chevrons in the middle lane, colored from {컬러}, with a raised stat badge beneath it reading “변화 기록” and a small numeric-style chip such as “DAY 01 → DAY 30”.
6) Progress text block: show {기간 정보} as a compact chip or footer label, aligned near the bottom center for quick readability; add a second small caption line in Korean such as “꾸준함으로 만든 변화”.
7) Panel labels: place bold labels “비포” and “애프터” at the top-left of each panel, plus small caption strips under each image such as “시작 사진” and “완료 사진”.
8) Footer details: include realistic fine-print style text along the bottom such as “운동 · 식단 · 헤어 루틴 기록”, “개인 변화 아카이브”, and “다음 슬라이드에서 루틴 공개”.
9) Visual balance: keep both panels visually equivalent in size and crop, but make the right side slightly more luminous, confident, and polished to reinforce transformation.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: use Pretendard Bold for the header, Pretendard SemiBold for labels, and Noto Sans KR Medium for the date/stat chips; header size should feel like 38–52 px equivalent in a 1536x1024 layout.
- Color palette: {컬러} should translate to crisp white #FFFFFF, charcoal #2B2B2B, lime green #B8E94E, and coral #FF6F61, with light gray #E9ECEF for separators, card surfaces, metadata rows, and caption strips.
- Border/shadow: use a thin charcoal divider line with a very soft shadow, plus a subtle 4px y-offset drop shadow on the center arrow badge at 15% opacity; add realistic photo-card shadows around each panel.
- Graphic treatment: use modern infographic shapes, sticker-like date chips, measurement-line accents, small check marks, progress dots, and editorial card layering; avoid excessive 3D, heavy blur, or glossy gradients.
- Text hierarchy: large readable title, medium panel labels, compact metadata, and tiny but legible footer microcopy; Korean text should feel like a real social transformation card rather than a blank template.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: studio editorial flat composition, equivalent to a 50mm standard lens look with controlled perspective distortion, optimized for comparison graphics rather than portrait drama.
- Lighting: even softbox lighting from upper-left at about 45°, with a gentle fill from the right so both sides remain readable and skin/hair/fabric detail stays natural.
- Color grade: high-key white base with charcoal contrast, lime-green progress accents, and coral highlights; keep saturation moderate and print-friendly.
- Realism cues: visible fabric texture, natural hair strands, subtle skin detail, realistic floor or wall hints inside the photo panels, and believable shadows under props and card layers.

[6. MOOD]
Modern wellness infographic — clean magazine explainer page feel, similar to a premium fitness editorial spread and an Instagram carousel cover with crisp before/after storytelling, practical progress labels, and motivational personal-record energy.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: the following strings must appear exactly as written in the rendered image: “챌린지 비포·애프터”, “챌린지”, “비포”, “애프터”, “기간 정보”.
- Placeholder fidelity: render the visible values of {챌린지}, {비포}, {애프터}, {기간 정보}, {비주얼}, {컬러}, and {비율} according to their meaning without changing the placeholder names in this prompt.
- Additional Korean text may include: “변화 기록”, “시작 사진”, “완료 사진”, “꾸준함으로 만든 변화”, “다음 슬라이드에서 루틴 공개”, “2026.05.01 기록”.
- Composition invariant: maintain exact 좌우 분할 50:50 with a centered arrow and compact stats area.
- Readability: all Korean text must be clean, fully formed, and free of broken characters.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]
- Fake official seals / certifications
- Broken Korean characters
- Celebrity composites or unauthorized likeness

studio:prompts3:ours-658.content:
[INPUT]
- language: Korean
- output_size: 1024x1536

[1. PURPOSE]
Vertical daily vlog intro screen for a personal lifestyle video, designed like a polished social-media opening card with a clear date, mood phrase, daily topic cue, and realistic lifestyle details.
Korean vlog thumbnail-style intro with a human hero, diary stickers, small agenda accents, channel-style micro text, and natural-light editorial atmosphere.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Center the {인물 결} hero portrait to occupy about 58% of the frame height, with natural headroom for the vlog title, date label, and small creator details.
- Place {오늘 날짜} near the upper-right quadrant as a bold, easy-to-scan date label, paired with a tiny weekday/time chip such as “AM 09:30” or “오늘의 기록”.
- Use {무드 텍스트} as a mid-lower text band, diary memo, or speech-card element, sized smaller than the date but still highly legible.
- Add realistic schedule-like visual cues around the hero area to support {주제}: small checklist notes, a tiny calendar scrap, coffee receipt, phone notification card, pen marks, or sticker labels that feel like a real vlog planning board.
- Background should feel like soft indoor daylight with a beige-toned wall, lived-in desk corner, fabric curtain, warm wood surface, mug, notebook, subtle plant shadow, or other everyday home-studio details.
- Build a cohesive vertical intro layout with layered paper cards, tiny tape pieces, doodle arrows, micro captions, and readable Korean text hierarchy.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
1. Hero area (center 58%): {인물 결} shown as the main subject, cleanly separated from the background, with a natural everyday pose, authentic skin texture, soft realistic shadowing, and a relaxed vlog-host presence.
2. Date label zone (upper-right 12–15%): {오늘 날짜} displayed as the most immediately readable anchor, using compact bold typography with an amber underline, rounded box, or small calendar-tab shape.
3. Vlog title and creator cue (upper-left / top band): include “데일리 vlog” as a bold Korean-English title, plus a small handle such as “@daily.zip” and a tiny label like “EP. 014” or “LIFE LOG”.
4. Mood text zone (mid-lower 15–18%): {무드 텍스트} placed in a rounded memo card, speech bubble, or handwritten-style strip, visually lighter than the date but still prominent.
5. Topic cue layer (around hero edges): {주제} translated into supporting diary details such as “오늘 할 일”, “장보기”, “편집하기”, “산책”, tiny checkboxes, subtle sticker tags, and compact bullet notes.
6. Lifestyle detail layer: add small real-world props and textures such as a ceramic cup, open planner, phone corner, washi tape, soft knit sleeve, receipt slip, window highlight, and paper grain so the intro feels photographed rather than synthetic.
7. Visual rhythm layer: {비주얼} should feel like a vlog cover page, with gentle layering, slight overlap, tactile paper elements, and clear hierarchy rather than a flat template.
8. Palette integration: {컬러} should control the background, text blocks, accent shapes, stickers, and prop tones so the entire frame reads as one cohesive morning-to-daytime diary aesthetic in {비율}.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: use Pretendard Bold for the date and title, Pretendard Medium for supporting labels, and a handwritten Korean font such as Cafe24 Ssurround Air or Nanum Pen Script for the mood phrase; date around 52–68px, support text around 24–32px.
- Color palette: apply beige, charcoal, and warm amber from {컬러}, with off-white paper-like neutrals, a soft cream base, muted brown shadows, and amber accent highlights.
- Graphic treatment: layered rounded memo cards, tiny tape strips, subtle sticker shapes, checkbox marks, small arrow doodles, and translucent highlight swashes; shadows should feel like real paper with 4px y-offset, 14px blur, 16% opacity.
- Include micro UI/details that fit a vlog intro: tiny save/share-style icons, a short location/date chip, “REC” dot, small caption line, and one or two decorative tags without overpowering the hero.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: 35mm or 50mm portrait-lifestyle look, equivalent to a Sony A7 IV with 50mm f/1.8 or Canon EOS R6 with 35mm f/1.4, shallow-to-moderate depth of field.
- Lighting: soft window light from upper-left at roughly 45°, with a gentle fill bounce from lower-right; daylight-balanced, no harsh flash, no hard shadow edges.
- Color grade: beige paper tones + warm amber highlights + softened charcoal contrast, with slightly lifted shadows and low saturation for a calm vlog-editorial finish.
- Texture realism: visible paper grain, natural fabric folds, soft skin detail, mild lens falloff, believable desk shadows, and gentle bokeh on background props.

[6. MOOD]
Indie lifestyle vlog opening — somewhere between a Kinfolk editorial spread, a cozy YouTube day-in-the-life cover, and a warm Korean diary app intro screen.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: 반드시 정확히 보여야 하는 문자열: "데일리 vlog", {주제}, {인물 결}, {오늘 날짜}, {무드 텍스트}, {비주얼}, {컬러}, {비율}.

[1. PURPOSE]

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Main layout: 7 full-body OOTD panels arranged in a balanced weekly lookbook grid, with each day clearly separated and easy to compare at a glance.
- Subject placement: each outfit panel should keep the model centered or slightly off-center, full-body visible from head to shoes, with consistent scale across all 7 cuts.
- Background treatment: use {배경} with believable floor contact, soft wall texture, street pavement, café window reflections, clothing rack hints, or natural city details that support the fashion story.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
1) Title zone: place the main headline “{메인타이틀}” at the top in a bold magazine-style Korean masthead, with “7 DAYS OOTD EDIT” and “LOOKBOOK VOL.247 · {날짜}” as small editorial subtext.
2) Profile meta strip: show {인플루언서핸들}, {장소}, a tiny circular profile thumbnail placeholder, and micro UI icons so the design reads as a realistic influencer style card.
3) Weekly grid: build the 7-day sequence as separate outfit cards, each one showing a distinct full-body look based on {주간룩} with clear day labeling.
4) Day labels and captions: each panel should include Korean weekday tags such as “월 MON”, “화 TUE”, “수 WED”, plus short item captions like “니트 + 와이드 데님”, “블레이저 셋업”, or “운동복 레이어드”.
5) Outfit presentation: each panel should show {구도}, such as mirror selfie stance, street-style walking pose, café entrance pose, or fashion lookbook stance, always keeping shoes, bag, accessories, silhouette, and proportions readable.
6) Styling annotations: add small decorative tags near selected panels, such as “출근룩”, “카페룩”, “데이트룩”, “주말 산책”, “오늘의 포인트”, using {컬러팔레트} as accent colors.
7) Visual consistency: retain a uniform editorial tone across all 7 panels so the page reads as one curated influencer lookbook, while allowing each day to have distinct styling, accessories, and background details.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: use Pretendard Bold for the title at large size, Noto Sans KR Medium for weekday labels, and a small clean sans-serif English subtitle in 12–16px range.
- Color palette: follow {컬러팔레트}; beige #D8C7B2, charcoal #3A3A3A, coral #F28C7D, warm off-white #F7F4EF, with small accent stickers and label bars.
- Grid treatment: thin soft gray dividers, editorial card edges, subtle drop shadows about 4px y-offset, 12px blur, 15% opacity, and magazine-like alignment for the 7 outfit cards.
- Graphic details: add realistic influencer-post elements such as tiny hearts, bookmark icon, share arrow, hashtag chips, day-number badges, small dotted guide lines, and caption labels without covering the clothing.
- Text hierarchy: {타이포스타일} should make the main title dominant, weekday labels instantly readable, and smaller captions clearly secondary.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: editorial fashion photography look, 50mm to 85mm lens equivalent, f/4–f/5.6 for sharp outfit detail and balanced full-body framing.
- Lighting: bright studio softbox from upper-left with gentle fill on the right, or daylight street lighting under soft overcast conditions for even skin and fabric rendering.
- Color grade: neutral cream base with beige and charcoal anchors, slightly warm coral accents, mild contrast, and clean magazine-style color separation.
- Material realism: render believable fabric texture, denim weave, knit softness, leather bag sheen, sneaker soles, coat seams, jewelry highlights, and natural hair movement.

[6. MOOD]
Korean fashion magazine editorial — approachable influencer lookbook with the organized feel of a modern street-style spread, practical weekly styling, and a save-worthy social post layout.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: the rendered image must clearly show “{메인타이틀}”, “월 MON / 화 TUE / 수 WED / 목 THU / 금 FRI / 토 SAT / 일 SUN”, “{인플루언서핸들}”, “{날짜}”, “{장소}”, and “{해시태그}” without broken characters.

- Visible realistic copy examples to include: “LOOKBOOK VOL.247”, “01 / WEEKLY LOOKBOOK”, “저장하고 내일 뭐 입을지 확인하기”, and short Korean item captions for each day.
- {주제}, {주간룩}, {구도}, {배경}, {컬러팔레트}, {타이포스타일}, {CTA} must be reflected faithfully in the design and layout.

- Color palette: {컬러팔레트} with marble whites, muted neutral highlights, charcoal text, and restrained gold accents for dividers, icon strokes, or a small decorative tag.

Premium luxury unboxing editorial — a Kinfolk-meets-Aesop product still-life with a boutique brand gift aesthetic, warm sponsored-review sincerity, and Instagram-ready polish.

Vertical studio class poster for a meditation/yoga class announcement, designed as a calm social-media and print-friendly promo card with a warm real studio atmosphere, editorial hierarchy, and practical class-registration details.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Main subject: a serene yoga pose figure placed slightly left of center, occupying about 45% of the frame height, photographed in a real bright studio setting with natural posture, relaxed expression, soft cotton activewear, and grounded body alignment.
- Secondary information stack: {강사·시간} and {장소} arranged in a clear vertical text block on the right-lower side, with class details, registration notes, and small icon-like markers aligned to a subtle editorial grid.
- Background treatment: bright natural-light studio interior with soft off-white wall, pale wood floor, linen curtain texture, rolled yoga mats, a low wooden bench, ceramic diffuser, folded towels, and leafy plants near the edges to create a believable wellness studio environment.
- Overall framing: tall poster layout with clear hierarchy, a premium wellness-brand feel, layered real-world details, and enough readable spacing for the headline and class information.
- Use {수업}, {비주얼}, {컬러}, {타이포}, {비율} as the customizable content anchors.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
1) Hero area (top 55%): a yoga posture figure rendered with clean, graceful body lines, framed from head to mid-leg, lit by daylight from the left, with a soft shadow falling to the lower right; include tactile studio details such as a woven mat edge, pale wood floor seams, and soft linen curtain folds.
2) Title zone (upper center): set the main headline in refined Korean serif typography, large and elegant, with the subtitle in smaller English beneath it: "Mind & Movement"; add a small season/date label above the title such as "SPRING MORNING CLASS · 2026".
3) Schedule block (mid-lower right): place {강사·시간} in smaller sans-serif text, with date/time separated by a thin divider rule for clarity; include small Korean detail text nearby such as "정원 8명 · 초보자 환영" and "준비물: 편한 복장, 개인 물병".
4) Location block (lower right): place {장소} below the schedule, aligned left, using slightly bolder weight than the schedule line; add a smaller address/contact style line such as "서울 마포구 포은로 00 · 예약 @mindflow.studio".
5) Event details and CTA: add a lower information band with practical poster content: "체험권 ₩25,000", "4주 클래스 등록 가능", "예약 마감: 수업 전날 18:00"; include a small ticket-style rectangle or QR reservation placeholder labeled "RESERVE" without claiming official certification.
6) Visual accents: add soft botanical shadows, translucent sage-green circular shapes, thin amber divider rules, small moon/sun breathwork icons, and subtle paper-like grain around the edges to keep the composition airy, organic, and print-realistic.
7) Sponsor / studio area: near the bottom margin, add a small studio credit line such as "Hosted by Mindflow Studio · Yoga / Meditation / Sound Healing" and tiny social handle text "@mindflow.studio".
8) Background balance: maintain a calm vertical poster rhythm while allowing realistic studio props, textures, and decorative editorial elements to support the yoga class theme.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: use a high-contrast Korean serif for the main title, such as Noto Serif KR or Sandoll Myeongjo, bold 700 for headline, 300–400 for supporting lines; English subtitle in a clean sans-serif like Pretendard or Inter, medium weight; micro-details use compact Pretendard with careful tracking.
- Color palette: follow {컬러} with beige #E8DDCF, sage green #A8B9A5, warm amber #D9A15B, and charcoal #2F2F2F; use cream paper tones, pale wood browns, muted plant greens, and warm sunlight highlights.
- Border/shadow: very soft drop shadow under the figure, 4px y-offset, 14px blur, 12% opacity; use delicate printed-card edge depth, soft contact shadows from props, and faint sunlight gradients.
- Layout styling: use thin separator rules, refined editorial spacing, registration-card modules, small icon labels, and restrained modern wellness branding with realistic print texture.
- Poster content styling: Korean class information must look like an actual studio announcement, including date/time, teacher name, venue, fee, booking note, small credit text, and a reservation placeholder.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: 50mm lens look, f/2.8, clean studio portrait framing with gentle depth separation; composition should feel like a lifestyle editorial poster rather than a fitness ad.
- Lighting: soft daylight from a large window on the left at about 45°, with light bounce fill from the right and a faint rim highlight on the figure’s shoulders and hair.
- Color grade: muted beige and sage with warm amber highlights, slightly lowered contrast, natural skin tones, and a calm matte finish.
- Material realism: visible cotton fabric texture, natural skin detail, matte paper grain, subtle floor reflections, plant leaf veins, linen curtain weave, and ceramic diffuser surface texture.

[6. MOOD]
Premium wellness studio editorial — calm, tactile, warm, slow-living, and inviting, with the atmosphere of a real neighborhood yoga studio preparing for a morning class.

1. Upper area: place the main roofline, layered 기와, eaves, and silhouetted temple structure first so the viewer immediately recognizes a Korean Buddhist temple setting.
2. Mid area: show {장면} with clear separation between carved wooden beams, dancheong patterns, courtyard stones, lantern strings, old trees, and mountain greenery.

6. Mood layering: keep {분위기} dominant through slow visual rhythm, quiet human absence, natural textures, and the feeling of early temple stillness.
7. Composition finish: use {구도} to create a contemplative editorial poster presentation with precise architectural clarity and a small Korean caption area.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: include a tasteful Korean editorial title block using Pretendard SemiBold or Noto Sans KR Medium. Main title 54–72px, subtitle 26–34px, date/location label 20–26px, all fully legible.
- Text placement: place {제목문구}, {부제문구}, {날짜}, and {위치라벨} in the lower third or along a quiet side margin, aligned cleanly with the temple geometry.
- Caption detail: add a small travel-note line using {하단캡션}, like a magazine or meditation poster imprint, without covering key architectural details.
- Color palette: dancheong red, antique gold, hanji beige, charcoal gray, temple wood brown, muted forest green from {컬러}; typography may use warm ivory or charcoal depending on background contrast.
- Depth and print finish: use subtle paper-grain texture, natural lens depth, soft atmospheric haze near the roofline, and gentle shadowing where text overlays stone or wood.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]

- Lighting: {조명} with soft directional illumination, low-angle sun grazing eaves and stone surfaces, no blown highlights.
- Color grade: restrained warm earth tones with balanced red-gold temple accents, gentle green foliage, and slightly muted contrast for meditative calm.
- Material realism: detailed 기와 ridges, carved brackets, aged 단청 paint, stone courtyard seams, dry leaves, incense smoke diffusion, and natural wood grain.

[6. MOOD]
Quiet Korean temple editorial — like a contemplative travel spread in National Geographic Traveler or a still frame from a slow Korean art film. The image should feel like a real dawn visit to a mountain temple, calm but richly observed.

[7. CRITICAL]

- Editorial realism: if adding lantern tags, small signboards, or caption plates, keep them plausible for a Korean Buddhist temple and ensure every Korean character is correctly formed.

Add realistic poster components: sponsor/host area near the bottom, small QR-ticket or registration block, venue note, and a fine-print credit line.

- Add realistic data-publishing details: “POST GAME REPORT”, “DATA DESK”, “MATCH CENTER”, page number “P.01”, date label “2026.05.01”, and a small QR/barcode-style information block in the lower corner.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]

7. Visual hierarchy support: keep {비주얼} consistent with a scoreboard infographic, ensuring the top result, middle charts, and lower MVP all read in one glance while adding believable sports-media details.

[1. PURPOSE]
Marathon finish-line emotional editorial image, wide landscape composition for sports recap cover or social post.
Create a rich, real-looking finish-line moment with a celebratory runner, packed crowd atmosphere, race infrastructure, visible timing details, bib number, photographers, volunteers, course barriers, sponsor-board texture, and clear race signage.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Main subject placement: runner(s) occupy the central 45–55% of the frame, crossing the finish line from left-to-right or slightly toward camera, with the finish banner spanning the upper third.
- Background treatment: stadium or city road-race setting with layered spectators, flags, course barriers, media photographers, volunteers in vests, hydration tables, confetti scraps, and distant cheering signs fading into warm atmospheric depth.
- Spacing and framing: compose the finish marker prominently so {결승선 표시} reads clearly while surrounding it with believable race-day details: overhead truss, LED timer, safety cones, sponsor placards, lane tape, and a timing mat on the road.
- Scene logic: {장면} should feel like the decisive final moment, while {인물 결} gives the emotional and physical condition of the runner; sweat, salt marks, flushed skin, taped knees, swinging medal ribbon, and a crumpled paper cup on the asphalt may reinforce realism.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
1. Foreground hero: place the runner in the lower-center area with a strong forward stride or raised arms, sweat visible, face showing relief and triumph; include a pinned race bib with realistic small numerals such as “BIB 0472” and tiny Korean race text.
2. Finish line anchor: render {결승선 표시} across the race tape or overhead banner in large, crisp typography with a visible timing display beside it, such as “02:58:41”, plus a small date label “2026.05.10” and location label “서울 잠실 구간”.
3. Race environment layer: add the finish arch truss, timing mat stripes, barricades, sponsor logo panels, medical staff vest details, photographers kneeling near the barrier, scattered confetti, water cups, reflective road markings, and a few waving national or club flags.
4. Crowd layer: place {관중} behind the main action as dense cheering forms with raised hands, phones, foam sticks, homemade signs, caps, banners, and realistic depth blur; keep the runner and finish text as the visual priority.
5. Light shaping: apply {조명} to create a golden edge on shoulders, hair, sweat, race tape, banner fabric, metal truss, and airborne dust/confetti, with natural shadow falloff across the asphalt.
6. Color balance: unify the scene with {컬러}, keeping the finish zone bright and emotionally lifted without oversaturating skin, bib paper, timing display, or signage.
7. Format discipline: maintain the exact landscape sports-photo framing implied by {비율}, with the subject centered enough for a cover crop but still dynamic and full of credible marathon finish-line context.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: use bold condensed sans styles similar to DIN Condensed or Pretendard ExtraBold for {결승선 표시}, sized large enough for instant readability, with compact timing text beneath in Noto Sans KR Regular.
- In-image Korean micro text: add realistic event details in small but legible places, such as “서울 국제 마라톤”, “결승 지점”, “완주를 축하합니다”, “기록 확인”, “2026년 5월 10일”, and “잠실 올림픽로”.
- Race signage: include a barcode-like bib strip, lane marker numbers, LED timer digits, sponsor-board blocks, media pass tags, and a small course board reading “42.195km”.
- Color palette: use warm amber, grass green, clean white, and soft asphalt gray; suggested accents #D98B3A, #6F8F4E, #F7F4EE, #4B4B4B.
- Texture and material realism: show woven banner fabric, matte bib paper with safety pins, sweat-darkened athletic fabric, rubber shoe soles, painted asphalt, metal barricades, vinyl sponsor boards, and soft dust particles in the backlight.
- Border/shadow: subtle soft shadow under the runner and banner fabric, 6px y-offset, 14px blur, 18% opacity; avoid hard cutout edges.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: 70–200mm sports telephoto at 135mm, f/2.8, fast shutter look, compressed background perspective.
- Lighting: golden hour natural sunlight from low rear-left, slight front fill from reflected ground light, soft shadows with bright rim highlights.
- Color grade: warm amber highlights, fresh grass-green secondary tones, clean white banner contrast, moderate cinematic saturation.
- Photoreal detail: editorial sports-photo realism with natural motion tension, crisp runner silhouette, shallow depth of field, believable crowd blur, readable finish-line text, and small documentary details that reward close viewing.

[6. MOOD]
Sports editorial triumph still — like a Nike campaign finish-line photo crossed with a Reuters sports feature, emotional but grounded. The mood should feel exhausted, human, celebratory, and specific to a real marathon finish, with public cheering energy and a believable race-day atmosphere.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: the following Korean strings must appear exactly and without broken characters where used: “서울 국제 마라톤”, “결승 지점”, “완주를 축하합니다”, “2026년 5월 10일”.
- Preserve all placeholder-driven content exactly in meaning: {장면}, {인물 결}, {결승선 표시}, {관중}, {조명}, {컬러}, {비율}.
- All runner anatomy must be natural and anatomically correct, with accurate stride pose and realistic hand/finger count.
- The finish-line typography, LED timing display, bib number, and Korean event labels must remain sharp, legible, and horizontally aligned.
- Do not invent an official certification seal; sponsor-style panels and realistic event graphics are acceptable.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]
- Broken Korean characters
- Fake official seals / certifications
- Celebrity composites or unauthorized likeness

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Main subject placement: the player occupies the central-to-lower 55% of the frame in a low-angle dramatic jump, with the ball and shooting hand pushed into the upper third for maximum vertical tension.

- Framing direction: wide horizontal action framing, with strong diagonal motion from lower-left to upper-right, visible rim/backboard area when appropriate for {장면}, and realistic court depth lines.
- Poster information layer: integrate event-promo details around the action without covering the athlete: short Korean headline, date/time/venue, ticket info, sponsor strip, small credit line, and decorative motion graphics such as speed lines, halftone dots, court-diagram arcs, or light streaks.
- Use {장면}, {선수 결}, {코트}, {조명}, {컬러}, {구도}, {비율} as the editable scene controls.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
- Hero action zone (center 60%): show {장면} at peak suspension, with the torso twisted naturally, knees bent or extended depending on the move, and the ball held clearly in the action path.
- Athlete rendering: {선수 결} with sharp muscle definition, realistic fabric folds, sweat highlights, compression gear seams, taped fingers or wristband detail, and authentic basketball shoe traction visible on the lifted foot.
- Court environment: {코트} with glossy reflections on the hardwood, painted lane markings, three-point arc fragments, baseline typography blur, basket support padding, out-of-focus arena lights, LED ad-board color glow, and sideline hints such as towels, camera lenses, staff silhouettes, or bench figures.
- Lighting composition: {조명} with a defined key light on the player’s upper body, deeper shadow under the legs, a mild rim edge to separate the silhouette from the background, and small specular highlights on sweat, ball texture, and polished floor.
- Color design: {컬러} applied as the dominant palette, with team accents on jersey trims, ball details, scoreboard glow, LED signage, court reflections, and graphic overlays, while keeping the arena background darker for contrast.
- Event poster text layout: set bold Korean title text in a strong sports-poster position: “농구 슛 모먼트”; add secondary blurbs such as “파이널 쿼터 집중”, “승부를 가르는 한 방”, “LIVE GAME NIGHT”; include realistic details: “2026.05.18 SAT 19:30”, “잠실 아레나”, “TICKET ₩35,000~”, “입장 18:30”, and a small sponsor/partner strip reading “SPONSOR · HOOP LAB · SEOUL SPORTS · ARENA CREW”.
- Micro details: include a small player credit near the lower edge such as “PLAYER CREDIT: KIM JIWON #23”, a tiny photo credit “PHOTO BY COURTSIDE STUDIO”, and a subtle QR/ticket block or barcode-style ticket mark labeled “예매 정보”.
- Camera language: low-angle sports editorial perspective, 70-200mm telephoto feel at around 135mm, f/2.8 look, freezing motion with crisp subject edges and slight background blur.
- Final framing: {구도} with enough headroom for the jump arc, hands and ball fully readable, arena ceiling lights and scoreboard glow supporting the vertical height, and the poster information arranged in readable zones around the action.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: use Pretendard Bold or Noto Sans KR Bold, 42–64px for title-scale text, 20–32px for event details, and 10–16px for micro credits; use tight kerning, strong sports-poster alignment, and high-contrast text blocks that remain legible over motion blur.
- Color palette: use {컬러} as the core scheme, anchored by deep charcoal #1E1E24, hardwood amber #A66A3F, off-white highlights #F4F1EA, and one saturated team accent.
- Graphic elements: add dynamic but believable sports-design layers such as diagonal score-line bands, transparent court diagrams, shot-clock numerals, dust/sweat particles, light flares from arena fixtures, and subtle halftone texture in the background.
- Border/shadow: subtle 10–18px soft shadow under the player body, 20% opacity, plus a faint vignette around the corners for arena depth; allow poster-style edge gradients, ticket-stub blocks, and sponsor-strip panels when they support the event-promo design.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]

- Lighting: studio-style arena key light from upper-left at 45°, controlled fill from front-right, and a slight rim from the back to carve out the athlete from the crowd.
- Color grade: contrasty broadcast sports grade with dark navy shadows, warm wood tones, vivid team-color accents, realistic skin tones, crisp jersey texture, and glossy court reflections.

[6. MOOD]
High-energy arena sports editorial — ESPN / NBA game-night poster feel with a cinematic action freeze, packed with real event atmosphere, crowd tension, court sound, and playoff-night intensity.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: “농구 슛 모먼트”, “파이널 쿼터 집중”, “승부를 가르는 한 방”, “2026.05.18 SAT 19:30”, “잠실 아레나”, “TICKET ₩35,000~”, “예매 정보”, “입장 18:30” must render cleanly and legibly.
- Scene logic: the player must be in a believable basketball action pose with anatomically correct limbs, exactly 5 fingers per hand, and a physically plausible jump arc.

8) Sports graphic layer: add a clean editorial overlay with a main Korean title, short match metadata, and small stat chips; place text where it does not cover the ball or primary facial expression.
9) Real-world details: include subtle elements such as jersey numbers, captain armband, referee in the background, corner flag, white touchline paint, blurred fans holding scarves, camera operators, and a thin lower-third highlight label.

[1. PURPOSE]

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Main subject: {디저트} fills about 65–75% of the frame, cropped tightly so the texture, {결}, filling, glaze, cream, crust, or crumb structure becomes the visual focus.
- Framing: centered hero composition with slight handcrafted asymmetry; show the dessert from a close three-quarter macro angle so the front cut surface and top garnish are both visible.
- Background: {배경} as a lived-in café tabletop scene with stone, wood, ceramic, linen, parchment, faint coffee ring marks, a dessert fork, and a softly blurred cup or saucer in the distance.
- Space planning: integrate {타이포} into a small menu-label area, a tiny paper tag, or a subtle printed card near one edge while keeping the dessert visually dominant.
- Color handling: {컬러} should guide dessert tones, plate color, napkin, tag paper, and small garnish accents, with warm café neutrals supporting the palette.
- Ratio: maintain {비율} as a square social/menu cover crop with rich macro detail from corner to corner.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
- Hero dessert area: {디저트} rendered as a hyper-detailed macro still life, showing frosting peaks, cocoa dust, sugar crystals, cream layers, fruit glaze, flaky pastry layers, shell texture, or moist crumb depending on the dessert type.
- Texture emphasis: make {결} visible through realistic pores, cut marks, air bubbles, toasted edges, powdered sugar residue, cream swirls, and tiny imperfect handmade details.
- Surface layer: place the dessert on a ceramic plate, clean stone slab, or wood board from {배경}; include natural crumbs, chocolate shavings, tiny herb leaves, fruit seeds, powdered sugar specks, or sauce droplets that match the dessert.
- Café context: add a folded linen napkin, a vintage dessert fork with gentle reflections, a small parchment menu card, a blurred espresso cup or tea glass, and a few background highlights to create a believable premium café setting.
- Text placement: add {타이포} as a refined menu-cover label. Include short Korean menu details such as “시그니처 디저트”, “오늘의 결”, “₩7,500”, “2026.05 시즌 메뉴”, “@cafe_signature”, and a tiny caption line “한입마다 깊어지는 달콤함”.
- Decorative details: use subtle café editorial elements such as a small round price sticker, fine divider lines, handwritten-style garnish note, tiny save/share micro icons, and a small barcode-like menu code area on the paper tag.
- Light falloff: use {조명} to create a bright highlight on the top plane and a soft gradient into the shadow side, preserving shape, depth, and edible realism.
- Overall finish: maintain an editorial café product-photo look with crisp focus on the nearest texture plane, creamy bokeh on distant props, and natural imperfections that make the food feel freshly plated.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: Pretendard or Noto Sans KR, regular to semibold weight, 18–34px equivalent for the main label, 10–16px equivalent for tiny menu details, clean Korean letterforms and accurate spacing.
- Color palette: {컬러} plus off-white #F6F1E8, warm beige #D8C3A5, muted cocoa #6B4E3D, soft amber #C98B4A, toasted brown #8A5A38, and cream highlight #FFF4DF.
- Text hierarchy: “시그니처 디저트” should be the clearest Korean title; supporting text like price, season label, and café handle should appear smaller on the tag/card.
- Shadow and contact realism: soft natural shadow under the dessert, about 4px y-offset, 14px blur, 18% opacity; include realistic occlusion where plate, crumbs, fork, and paper meet the tabletop.
- Material behavior: cream should look whipped and soft, pastry should look flaky or moist as appropriate, glaze should have controlled edible shine, and ceramic/metal/linen should each have distinct real-world texture.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: full-frame macro look, 100mm macro lens at f/4, extremely shallow depth of field but enough sharpness to preserve dessert texture.
- Lighting: {조명}; warm side light from upper-left, natural window quality with a gentle fill from the right; highlights should feel soft and edible, not glossy plastic.
- Color grade: warm cream + amber + cocoa, with slightly lifted highlights and low-contrast shadows for a café editorial finish.
- Focus behavior: sharpest focus on the front bite/cut surface, garnish, cream ridge, or crumb edge; gradual blur toward background cup, napkin folds, and tabletop details.
- Rendering quality: realistic macro photography with fine grain, natural lens falloff, subtle bokeh circles, true-to-life food texture, and a premium Korean café menu mood.

[6. MOOD]
Premium dessert editorial — a warm Korean café still life with tactile handmade detail, quiet luxury, soft afternoon light, and the feeling of a freshly served signature menu item.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: the following Korean text must appear exactly as rendered: “시그니처 디저트”, “한글 정확”.

- Maintain the square 1:1 framing, macro-focused composition, {비율}, and the same signature dessert subject throughout.

- Fake official seals / certifications
- Broken Korean characters

- Right panel (mid-right 40%): show a yield chart or bar/line comparison using {수익정보}, {수익률계산}, and {레버리지비교}. Include axis labels "월 임대료", "연 환산 수익", "실수익률", green highlight callout "핵심 수익률" and a small scenario chip "대출 조건: {대출조건}".
- Lower third table: present a compact financial summary table with rows for "매입가", "보증금", "월세", "관리비", "공실률", "연 수익률", "레버리지 후", using {매입가}, {보증금}, {월세}, {관리비}, {공실률}, {수익률계산}, and {레버리지비교} in a structured spreadsheet-like layout.
- Risk memo strip: add three small badges reading "임대수요", "금리민감도", "공실 리스크" with short Korean notes, plus a caption box showing "계산 기준: {수익정보}".
- Footer note strip (bottom 8%): place {면책문구}, a small source label "자료: 실거래가·임대시세 참고", a QR-style placeholder block, and a final CTA pill reading "{CTA}".

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: Pretendard or Noto Sans KR for all body text, bold 700–800 for headings, medium 500 for labels, 11–14px-equivalent for table text, 22–30px-equivalent for title, and 9–10px-equivalent for footer notes.
- Color palette: white #FFFFFF, charcoal #2B2F33, deep gray #4B5563, trust green #2E8B57, muted sage #DCE8DF, light border gray #E5E7EB, pale yellow #FFF7D6 for caution badges.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: realistic architectural/editorial capture, 35mm lens for property image panel, flat infographic rendering for chart elements, crisp print-layout composition.
- Lighting: soft overcast daylight or diffused window light from upper-left, even exposure, low contrast, readable text areas, natural property-photo depth.
- Color grade: neutral white base with controlled green accents, charcoal text, slightly cool-gray balance for a financial-report aesthetic.

[6. MOOD]
Premium real-estate investment memo — resembles a clean institutional property analysis sheet with practical investor annotations, believable market-note details, and a calm data-driven tone.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: 반드시 다음 문구가 정확히 보여야 함: "부동산 임대 수익 분석", "{매물명}", "{수익정보}", "{수익률계산}", "{레버리지비교}", "{분석일자}", "{지역라벨}".
- 표 안의 핵심 값은 반드시 다음처럼 읽혀야 함: "매입가 {매입가}", "월세 {월세}", "보증금 {보증금}", "관리비 {관리비}", "공실률 {공실률}".
- All numbers and percentage values must be cleanly legible, aligned, and consistent across the chart/table.
- The composition must preserve a left property visual + right performance chart + lower financial table layout.
- Footer에는 반드시 "{면책문구}"와 "{CTA}"가 작게 표시되어야 함.

[1. PURPOSE]
Korean stock analysis infographic card, editorial finance layout, social-media shareable portrait.
Designed to summarize one listed stock with chart, valuation metrics, market context, key risk notes, and a clear investment opinion in a realistic brokerage-report card format.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Portrait finance card with a strict three-part vertical flow: top stock header occupies 18% of frame, center chart zone 52%, bottom metrics and opinion zone 30%.
- Use {종목·티커} as the primary headline in the top band, aligned left with a compact ticker tag style; add {현재가·등락} as a price chip on the right.
- Background is a deep dark-charcoal finance-board surface with subtle matte texture, faint grid lines, small data ticks, market-session marks, and restrained glow accents.
- Include realistic editorial metadata: {분석일시}, {자료출처}, {채널핸들}, slide marker {슬라이드번호}, and a small save/share micro-icon row suited for an Instagram or card-news post.
- Maintain balanced inner padding, clean dividers, and a dense data-card framing direction that feels like a premium brokerage research note.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
1. Header area (top 18%): place {종목·티커} as the dominant title, with supporting Korean labels such as “종목 심층 분석”, “장마감 기준”, “관심종목”, and {분석일시}; place {현재가·등락} in a right-side market-status capsule.
2. Market chart area (middle 52%): render {차트} as the central visual, with a dark trading-screen panel, visible candles, moving averages, volume bars, RSI subline, axis labels, price markers, and a small caption line “6개월 추세 / 거래량 / 모멘텀”.
3. Market context strip: add {거래정보} as compact badges near the chart, such as 시가총액, 거래대금, 52주 범위, 외국인 수급, 기관 수급.
4. Metrics block (bottom 30%): present {지표} in a structured table grid with clear row separation, aligned numeric columns, colored change arrows, and high-contrast readability.
5. Opinion callout: position {의견} as a concise highlighted note near the lower section, using an accent box labeled “애널리스트 코멘트”.
6. Insight and risk notes: include {투자포인트} and {리스크} as two short bullet groups, visually separated with small icons, badges, and thin dividers.
7. Footer card-news utility: include {채널핸들}, “저장하고 다음 리포트 보기”, “공유 · 저장 · 알림”, page indicator {슬라이드번호}, and {자료출처} in small but legible text.
8. Overall layout cue: {비주얼} should be expressed as a professional market-research card rather than a sales advertisement, with all added UI elements supporting the financial data hierarchy.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: Pretendard and Noto Sans KR, bold 700 for the title, semibold 600 for price and section labels, medium 500 for table labels, regular 400 for supporting text; title size should feel like 48–60px equivalent in a 1024x1536 canvas.
- Color palette: {컬러} with deep charcoal #1E1F22, near-black #111214, alert red #E25252, positive green #2DBE60, muted gray #A7ADB6, off-white text #F2F4F7, subdued blue #4C8DFF for neutral data chips.
- Border/shadow: thin 1px divider lines in muted gray, soft drop shadow 0 4px 12px rgba(0,0,0,0.28), subtle inset highlight on chart panels, small rounded capsules for metadata and risk badges.
- Table design: numeric values must align on a shared baseline; Korean labels should not overlap; red and green must be used consistently for loss/gain or bearish/bullish signals.
- Social card details: add small micro-icons for 저장, 공유, 댓글, and 알림 using simple line-style symbols; include a realistic footer disclaimer “투자 판단의 책임은 투자자 본인에게 있습니다.”

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: straight-on graphic poster render, equivalent to a 50mm normal-perspective editorial product shot look, no distortion, no wide-angle exaggeration.
- Lighting: controlled studio-softbox feel with even front illumination, a refined upper-left highlight, soft panel depth, and enough contrast to keep every table cell and chart label legible.
- Color grade: cool graphite finance palette with restrained red/green market accents, high contrast but not neon, clean institutional tone.
- Surface realism: crisp screen-like data panels, subtle paper-report texture in the background, tiny grid ticks, and polished editorial spacing suitable for a premium Korean finance channel.

[6. MOOD]
Premium Wall Street research-note editorial — Bloomberg Terminal / Financial Times data card aesthetic, adapted for a Korean Instagram card-news finance account.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: must appear exactly as rendered text for {종목·티커}, {분석일시}, {현재가·등락}, {차트}, {거래정보}, {지표}, {의견}, {투자포인트}, {리스크}, {채널핸들}, {슬라이드번호}, and {자료출처}.
- Required rendered Korean labels include: “종목 심층 분석”, “장마감 기준”, “현재가”, “거래량”, “PER”, “PBR”, “ROE”, “배당수익률”, “투자포인트”, “리스크 체크”, “애널리스트 코멘트”, “저장하고 다음 리포트 보기”, “투자 판단의 책임은 투자자 본인에게 있습니다.”
- Layout invariants: top header, center chart, bottom metric table must remain in the same vertical order with clear separation.
- All numbers, tickers, arrows, Korean words, chart labels, footer captions, and page indicators must be sharp, fully legible, and correctly spaced.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]
- Fake official seals / certifications
- Broken Korean characters
- Celebrity composites or unauthorized person likeness
- Fake exchange approval marks or forged regulatory stamps

[1. PURPOSE]
Korean finance-card-news poster introducing 5 side jobs for office workers, designed as a vertical carousel cover page with a 5-box grid, editorial metadata, realistic print texture, and compact visual annotations.
Social-media-friendly finance editorial layout for quick reading and saving, focused on side-income ideas, estimated earnings, required skills, and practical after-work action cues.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Main subject: a structured 5-panel grid occupying about 72–78% of the canvas height, with each box clearly separated and styled like a printed card-news page.
- Header zone: top 16% contains the title, publisher tag, issue label, date label, and slide indicator, arranged with strong hierarchy and centered editorial balance.
- Add realistic card-news details: small label chips reading "VOL.247", "2026년 5월호", "01/06", a tiny bookmark/share icon row, and a short note such as "퇴근 후 2시간으로 시작".
- Background treatment: warm cream paper-like base with subtle grain, faint ledger lines, small sticky-note shapes, charcoal text blocks, and accent pops in lime green and coral.
- Use {5가지 부업}, {각자 수익 예상}, {필요 기술}, {비주얼}, {컬러}, {발행처}, {비율} placeholders exactly where variable content is needed.
- Keep the layout highly readable while allowing useful editorial micro-elements such as page markers, divider labels, small captions, and CTA badges.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
1) Header area (top 16%): set the main title in large bold Korean type, with a short subtitle beneath in smaller weight; include "VOL.247", "2026년 5월호", "직장인 머니노트", and page indicator "01/06" as small editorial labels.
2) Grid area (middle 68%): arrange 5 equal boxes in a tidy card-news grid, each box containing one side job, one earnings line, one skill line, and a tiny practical cue chip.
3) Per-box structure: each box should show a recognizable icon at the upper-left, the side-job label as the primary line, estimated monthly income as a colored badge, required skill as a compact bottom line, plus a tiny caption such as "시작 난이도", "퇴근 후 가능", or "초기비용 체크".
4) Visual treatment: use editorial flat icons with small realistic print imperfections, thin charcoal dividers, subtle paper shadow, mini highlight stickers, and consistent spacing so every box reads as part of the same finance-card system.
5) Footer area (bottom 8%): place {발행처} as a small but legible channel mark, add "저장하고 퇴근 후 다시 보기", "다음 장: 시작 비용 체크", and tiny save/share micro icons aligned with the overall layout.
6) Content mapping: populate the 5 boxes with {5가지 부업}, show {각자 수익 예상} as the income row, and {필요 기술} as the skill row, all rendered in Korean with exact spacing.
7) Ratio and visual reference: apply {비율} for the vertical card-news format, reflect {비주얼} in the icon/illustration language, and use {컬러} as the main accent palette while preserving cream, charcoal, lime green, and coral harmony.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: Pretendard or Noto Sans KR for the main title in ExtraBold, secondary text in Medium and Regular; title size should dominate, with compact but readable box text and clear Korean line breaks.
- Color palette: cream #F4EEDF, charcoal #2B2B2B, lime green #B8D94A, coral #FF6F61; use accent colors for icons, badges, page indicators, highlight underlines, and small CTA chips.
- Border/shadow: 1px charcoal outline around each card, soft shadow 4px y-offset, 10px blur, 12% opacity, with slight printed-paper depth and gentle edge texture.
- Add editorial details: tiny section label "SIDE JOB LIST", small chart-like dots, divider tabs, bookmark/share icons, and handwritten-style micro captions while keeping all essential Korean text crisp.
- Korean text should be sharp, evenly aligned, and natural, with no awkward wrapping inside the small cards.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: top-down photographed printed card-news sheet, Canon EOS R5 with RF 50mm f/2.8 Macro, orthographic editorial composition with slight paper curl and realistic ink-on-paper texture.
- Lighting: soft even studio illumination with gentle natural paper shadows, preserving uniform readability across the entire poster.
- Color grade: warm cream base with restrained high-contrast charcoal text and bright lime/coral accents, similar to a contemporary Korean fintech carousel saved from a social feed and printed as an editorial reference card.
- Surface realism: subtle paper grain, faint halftone ink texture, tiny registration-like marks, and tactile sticker labels that make the infographic feel like a real designed finance card rather than a sterile mockup.

[6. MOOD]
Practical, energetic Korean finance editorial — similar to a well-produced 매거진 카드뉴스 page for office workers planning realistic after-work income, with a modern startup-finance aesthetic and useful save-worthy details.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: 반드시 다음 문자열이 정확히 보여야 함: "직장인 부업 5가지", "블로그 / 유튜브 / 온라인 강의 / 중고거래 / 외주 디자인", "월 30만 / 월 100만 / 월 200만 / 월 50만 / 월 80만", "글쓰기 / 영상 / 강의 / 협상 / 디자인", "재테크 카드뉴스 채널".
- Also render short Korean editorial elements clearly: "VOL.247", "2026년 5월호", "01/06", "퇴근 후 2시간으로 시작", "저장하고 퇴근 후 다시 보기", "다음 장: 시작 비용 체크".
- The 5 boxes must remain evenly spaced and consistently styled, with each income badge and skill chip aligned to its corresponding side job.
- Keep all icon shapes aligned with their corresponding text and make every Korean string sharp enough to read at social-media thumbnail size.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]
- Fake official seals / certifications
- Broken Korean characters

- Top utility strip: show {카테고리}, {슬라이드번호}, and {발행일} in small editorial labels, with a lime-green dot marker and a thin divider.

- Mid-page stacked process area: display {단계목록} as a compact roadmap, then show five vertical step cards using {단계상세}; each card has a number pill, tiny icon, action keyword, and a short maker-style note.
- Add realistic card-news UI details: {페이지표시} near the lower-right, small “저장 · 공유 · 팔로우” micro icons near the footer, and a sticky-note callout containing {다음장예고}.
- Lower support area: a laptop/browser-window illustration, tiny revenue chart, checklist ticks, cursor arrow, calendar chip, and tool badges based on {추천도구}.
- Bottom footer strip: {발행처} aligned left, {해시태그} aligned right, and {CTA} placed as a bold end-card call-to-action bar.
- Background treatment: matte off-white paper base with subtle light-gray grid texture, faint notebook ruling, small lime annotation marks, and soft editorial card shadows.
- Use {비주얼} as the central illustration language, with flat infographic elements mixed with tactile paper stickers and dashboard snippets.
- Use {컬러} for the overall palette and accent hierarchy.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
1) Utility zone (top 6%): place {카테고리} on the left, {발행일} centered or right-aligned, and {슬라이드번호} inside a small lime-outlined capsule. Add a tiny “VOL.01” editorial mark if it fits the rhythm.
2) Header zone (top 20%): render “사이드프로젝트 가이드” as a small uppercase-style Korean series label, then set {주제} in a bold sans-serif masthead style with tight leading and high contrast. Put {부제} underneath as a practical promise line.
3) Step roadmap zone (middle 43%): present {단계목록} as a slim summary rail, then build five stacked rounded rectangles for {단계상세}. Each step card should include: 01–05 number marker, a compact icon, one bold Korean keyword, and a one-line action memo.
4) Tool and proof zone (middle-lower 13%): place {추천도구} as compact pill badges, plus a small mock dashboard card showing “목표 ₩1,000,000”, “첫 고객 10명”, and a rising lime mini-chart.
5) Visual support zone (lower 11%): integrate {비주얼} as a laptop anchor, cursor, sticky notes, small calendar label, checklist marks, and chart accents that reinforce the side-project process.
6) Footer / CTA zone (bottom 7%): place {발행처}, {해시태그}, {페이지표시}, “저장 · 공유 · 팔로우” micro icons, and a strong CTA bar with {CTA}.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: Pretendard or Noto Sans KR, title in ExtraBold 54–64px, series label in Bold 22–26px, step labels in SemiBold 24–28px, microcopy in Medium 16–20px, footer in Medium 18–20px.
- Color palette: use white #FFFFFF / warm off-white #FAFAF7, charcoal #222222, and lime green #A6E22E from {컬러}, with pale gray #E9ECEF for dividers, cards, and grid marks.
- Border/shadow: thin 1.5px charcoal outlines, lime accent strokes, soft drop shadow 0px 6px 18px at 10% opacity on step cards, tactile paper sticker edges, and flat editorial vector styling.
- Icons and UI: simple line icons for lightbulb, chat bubble, cube/MVP, rocket, megaphone, plus save/bookmark/share symbols sized like real Instagram card-news micro UI.
- Text hierarchy: every Korean label must be readable at mobile size; keep headline dominant, steps scannable, and CTA visually separated with a lime highlight bar.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: top-down editorial flat-lay look, 35mm equivalent with slight orthographic feel, crisp infographic rendering.
- Lighting: even studio lighting from above with soft short shadows, clean high-key exposure, gentle paper texture visibility, and precise edges on text and cards.
- Color grade: neutral white base with charcoal typography and lime green accent pops, modern fintech / indie startup palette.
- Rendering: polished vector-editorial card news mixed with realistic printed-paper texture, subtle sticker overlays, dashboard mini-cards, and social carousel UI details.

[6. MOOD]
Practical indie startup editorial — Notion template, YC-style launch playbook, and Korean maker newsletter feel.
Useful, energetic, and save-worthy, like a carousel post someone would bookmark before building on the weekend.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: 반드시 아래 문구가 정확히 보여야 함:
  - 사이드프로젝트 가이드

  - 아이디어 / 검증 / MVP / 런칭 / 마케팅
  - 01 아이디어: 반복되는 불편 찾기 / 02 검증: 10명에게 문제 확인 / 03 MVP: 주말에 핵심 기능만 제작 / 04 런칭: 랜딩페이지와 결제 연결 / 05 마케팅: 후기와 지표로 반복

[INPUT]
- language: Korean

[1. PURPOSE]
크리스마스 굿즈 4종을 한 화면에 정리한 평면 mockup 콜라주 포스터. 온라인 스토어 상세페이지 헤더, SNS 프로모션 배너, 시즌 상품 소개용으로 바로 쓸 수 있는 구성이며, 실제 시즌 기획전처럼 상품명·가격·출시일·구매 혜택·작은 바코드/QR 스타일 요소까지 포함한다.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- 전체 화면은 16:10 가로 비율의 정돈된 편집 디자인으로 구성하고, 중앙에 4종 굿즈가 균형 있게 배치된 콜라주가 프레임의 약 70%를 차지하게 한다.
- 상단 14~16%에는 브랜드명, 시즌 타이틀, 출시일 배지를 배치하고, 중앙 56%에는 굿즈 묶음과 각 상품 라벨, 하단 14~16%에는 가격·혜택·구매 안내·웹주소가 들어가게 한다.
- 배경은 따뜻한 화이트 또는 옅은 크림 톤의 종이 보드 위에 은은한 페이퍼 그레인, 얇은 리본 조각, 작은 전나무 가지, 별 모양 컨페티, 금색 실 장식이 자연스럽게 놓인 스튜디오 flat lay로 만든다.
- {컨셉}에 맞춰 전체 분위기를 정하고, {굿즈구성}이 한눈에 구분되도록 각 아이템은 개별 상품 카드와 작은 라벨 스티커를 함께 가진다.
- {디자인모티프}는 각 굿즈 표면의 작은 그래픽 패턴, 스티커 시트, 키링 참, 머그컵 전면 인쇄, 양말 자수 디테일에 반복 적용한다.
- {컬러팔레트}는 메인 팔레트로 사용하되, 빨강과 다크 그린은 상품 인쇄와 헤드라인에, 골드는 가격 배지·리본·작은 별 장식에 집중한다.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
- Header zone (top 15%): 좌측 상단에 {브랜드명}, 중앙에 {타이포스타일} 기반의 큰 타이틀 "Merry Christmas"와 한글 서브타이틀 "크리스마스 굿즈 풀세트"를 배치한다. 우측에는 둥근 배지로 "{출시일}"과 "HOLIDAY DROP"을 넣어 실제 시즌 프로모션처럼 보이게 한다.
- Main collage zone (center 56%): {굿즈구성}을 좌우 2x2 균형 배열로 놓고, 각 아이템 아래에 상품 라벨을 붙인다. 라벨 문구는 "01 니트 양말", "02 세라믹 머그", "03 아크릴 키링", "04 스티커 시트"처럼 번호와 이름이 선명하게 읽히게 한다.
- Item 1: 양말은 좌상단에 두고, 부드러운 니트 조직과 발목 리브, 작은 자수 패치가 보이게 하며 발목 부분에 {디자인모티프}를 아기자기한 자수 느낌으로 넣는다.
- Item 2: 머그컵은 우상단에 두고, 정면에 가까운 각도로 배치하되 손잡이는 오른쪽 3시 방향으로 보이게 한다. 컵 전면에는 "크리스마스"와 작은 산타 아이콘, 컵 안쪽에는 코코아 색감과 미니 마시멜로 느낌의 디테일을 넣는다.
- Item 3: 키링은 좌하단에 두고, 금속 링과 투명 아크릴 참의 반사광을 자연스럽게 표현한다. 참에는 산타 모자, 눈사람, 작은 선물 상자 그래픽이 겹겹이 인쇄된 실제 굿즈처럼 보이게 한다.
- Item 4: 스티커 시트는 우하단에 두고, 여러 개의 작은 스티커가 네모 그리드 안에 촘촘히 들어가도록 만든다. 스티커에는 "JOY", "NOEL", "눈 오는 밤", "선물 도착" 같은 짧은 문구와 {디자인모티프}가 섞인다.
- Footer zone (bottom 15%): 왼쪽에는 가격 배지 "{세트가격}", 중앙에는 혜택 문구 "{구매혜택}", 오른쪽에는 "온라인 단독", "{웹주소}", 작은 바코드 스타일 그래픽과 QR 코드 스타일 사각 패턴을 배치한다. 하단 가장자리에는 얇은 제품 코드 라인 "SET NO. XMAS-1225 · GIFT READY"를 넣는다.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: Pretendard ExtraBold for Korean headline, Noto Sans KR Medium for supporting text, 영문 "Merry Christmas"는 세리프 계열 또는 둥근 산세리프를 섞어 festive하게 처리한다.
- 글자 크기: 메인 타이틀은 화면 폭의 18~22%, 보조 텍스트는 메인 대비 35~45% 크기, 상품 라벨은 작지만 굵고 선명하게 읽히는 크기로 설정한다.
- Color palette: {컬러팔레트}를 기본으로 하되, 배경은 #F8F7F2 또는 #FFFDF7, 그림자는 #C7B299 계열의 부드러운 톤, 골드 장식은 #C8A24A 계열로 따뜻하게 표현한다.
- Border/shadow: 각 굿즈 카드에는 4px y-offset, 12px blur, 14% opacity의 부드러운 드롭 섀도를 넣고, 테두리는 1px의 얇은 라인으로 정돈한다. 가격 배지와 출시일 배지는 둥근 스티커 형태로 약간의 종이 두께와 접착 라벨 질감이 느껴지게 한다.
- Graphic details: 리본, 별 컨페티, 전나무 잎, 작은 선물 태그, 바코드 스타일 요소는 상품 정보를 보조하는 장식으로 배치하고, 전체는 실제 촬영된 굿즈 세트와 디지털 편집 포스터가 결합된 느낌으로 완성한다.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: top-down flat lay look, Canon EOS R5 with 35mm lens at f/8, crisp product-layout clarity with minimal perspective distortion.
- Lighting: studio softbox overhead + gentle fill from upper-left, shadow edge soft and even, reflections controlled like a professional e-commerce catalog shoot.
- Color grade: clean holiday editorial grade with bright white balance, saturated red and deep green accents, restrained gold highlights, no neon shift.

[6. MOOD]
Seasonal product catalog spread — a warm boutique holiday goods layout with festive stationery details, premium e-commerce packaging mockup aesthetics, and the cheerful realism of a Christmas pop-up store display.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: 반드시 정확히 보여야 하는 문구: "Merry Christmas", "크리스마스 굿즈 풀세트", "{브랜드명}", "{출시일}", "{세트가격}", "{구매혜택}", "{웹주소}".
- 상품 라벨은 "01 니트 양말", "02 세라믹 머그", "03 아크릴 키링", "04 스티커 시트"로 선명하게 렌더링한다.
- 모든 굿즈는 서로 다른 4종으로 명확히 구분되어 보여야 하며, 각 아이템의 형태·재질·인쇄 그래픽이 실제 판매 상품처럼 설득력 있게 보여야 한다.
- 한글 문자는 깨짐 없이 선명하게 렌더링되어야 하며, 가격·출시일·상품 번호·짧은 홍보 문구가 실제 온라인 스토어 배너처럼 읽혀야 한다.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]
- Fake official seals / certifications
- Broken Korean characters
- Celebrity composites or real-person identity transformations
- Misleading government, medical, or legal endorsement marks

[1. PURPOSE]
Korean white Christmas home interior poster for a newlywed couple's home, composed like a premium seasonal home magazine cover. The image should combine a realistic editorial room-styling hero scene with visible magazine-cover information, feature headlines, and small publishing details.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Main scene: wide living-room hero composition filling about 70% of the frame, with {공간} as the primary setting and the decorated Christmas zone centered slightly lower than mid-frame.
- Magazine cover layer: place {매거진명} near the upper area as a clean masthead, with {이슈번호}, {발행일}, and {가격} placed as small editorial metadata; add a barcode block using {바코드번호} near the lower-right corner.
- Main cover text: render {표지제목} as the main Korean cover title over a bright readable area, with {부제} as a smaller subtitle below it.
- Feature headlines: add 2–3 Korean feature headlines — {헤드라인1}, {헤드라인2}, {헤드라인3} — arranged along the side or lower third, integrated like a lifestyle magazine cover rather than floating stickers.
- Interior styling: include natural home details such as a woven rug, linen cushions, knitted throw blanket, wrapped gifts, ceramic mugs, a small tray, pine garland, books, photo frame, and subtle fabric textures so the room feels realistically lived-in.
- Surface and background: bright white walls, soft beige textile surfaces, warm wood furniture grains, gentle shadow corners, clean home interior depth, visible floor texture, and small seasonal reflections on ornaments.
- Framing: maintain an airy portrait magazine composition with the decorated tree and main furniture forming the visual anchor; keep readable zones for cover text while allowing realistic home objects and seasonal textures to remain visible.
- All styling elements should follow {데코}, {가구}, {컬러}, {조명}, and {비주얼} while preserving a natural interior-photo layout.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
1. Hero room area: stage the full Christmas interior in {공간}, with the decorated tree, sofa, table, rug, window glow, and main furniture anchored in a cohesive newlywed-home vignette.
2. Decor layer: place {데코} across the room in a refined, warm way — tree as the tallest focal point, stockings and candles as low-level warmth accents, gold ornaments catching light, and small wrapped gifts near the tree base.
3. Furniture layer: integrate {가구} so the scene reads as a realistic Korean couple's home setup, with sofa, table, cushions, throw blanket, books, mugs, and a small tray creating everyday domestic detail.
4. Magazine layer: add the masthead {매거진명}, issue metadata {이슈번호}, {발행일}, {가격}, a spine credit {스파인크레딧}, and a barcode labeled {바코드번호}; keep all text aligned to a polished editorial grid.
5. Feature text layer: include {표지제목}, {부제}, {헤드라인1}, {헤드라인2}, and {헤드라인3} in accurate Korean, sized with clear hierarchy and placed so they do not cover the Christmas tree face or key decor details.
6. Color harmony: apply {컬러} throughout textiles, ornaments, typography accents, ambient highlights, candlelight, and evergreen details, keeping the whites creamy and the amber glow soft rather than orange-heavy.
7. Lighting layer: use {조명} as visible practical lights, with gentle reflections on ornaments, candle glass, glossy gift ribbon, and surrounding furniture surfaces.
8. Visual framing: follow {비주얼} by emphasizing a broad interior hero shot with supporting detail emphasis, as if photographed and designed for a premium seasonal lifestyle magazine cover.
9. Final finish: keep the composition polished and realistic, with crisp object edges, soft shadow separation, legible Korean typography, tactile fabrics, wood grain, ceramic surfaces, and believable holiday styling.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: use Pretendard Bold, Pretendard Medium, or Noto Sans KR Bold for all Korean cover text; masthead 64–90px, main title 48–64px, feature headlines 26–36px, metadata 16–22px.
- Typography color: warm charcoal, ivory, muted gold, and deep green; use subtle translucent text panels only where needed for readability while keeping the photographic interior visible.
- Cover details: include issue number, date, price, barcode, page-like editorial hierarchy, and a thin vertical spine credit along one edge using {스파인크레딧}.
- Color palette: {컬러} with off-white #F7F4EE, warm beige #D8C7B3, gold #C9A35C, amber #D88A3D, deep green #2F4B35.
- Border/shadow: soft natural shadowing under furniture, decor, and text panels, with 12px blur and 15% opacity; maintain a printed editorial cover feel rather than a cutout collage.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: full-frame interior photography look, 24mm wide-angle lens at f/4.5, straight-on room shot with mild perspective depth.
- Lighting: warm practical lighting from {조명}, plus soft window daylight from upper-left at 45°, creating layered glow and gentle ambient reflections.
- Color grade: creamy white balanced with warm amber highlights, muted gold accents, slightly deepened evergreen contrast, realistic paper-cover polish, and tactile fabric detail.

[6. MOOD]
Premium Christmas home styling — Kinfolk and House & Garden interior editorial feel, with a calm newlywed couple-home holiday atmosphere, cozy winter textures, and polished Korean lifestyle magazine-cover sensibility.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: all on-image Korean typography must be perfectly rendered and readable, including “{매거진명}”, “{표지제목}”, “{부제}”, “{헤드라인1}”, “{헤드라인2}”, “{헤드라인3}”, “{이슈번호}”, “{발행일}”, “{가격}”, and “{스파인크레딧}”.
- Required visible cover text examples: “{표지제목}”, “{부제}”, “{헤드라인1}”, “{헤드라인2}”, “{헤드라인3}”.
- Barcode detail: include a realistic small barcode box with the readable number “{바코드번호}” near the lower-right corner.
- Composition invariants: maintain a bright white Christmas interior, a large hero room scene, premium magazine-cover layout, and realistic home styling details without changing the overall portrait format.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]

- Broken Korean characters or unreadable Hangul
- Celebrity composites or lookalike endorsement

studio:prompts3:ours-634.content:
[INPUT]
- language: Korean
- output_size: 1024x1536

[1. PURPOSE]
Korean year-end greeting card for office colleagues, family, friends, or clients. Vertical social card with an elegant holiday still-life editorial feel, suitable for sincere seasonal thanks and New Year wishes. The image should feel like a real printed premium greeting card photographed on a festive tabletop, with tactile paper, warm candlelight, tasteful seasonal objects, and polished Korean typography.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Main composition: a refined holiday still life fills the lower 60% of the frame, while the greeting title, date label, and message block occupy the upper 40% as a designed printed card surface.
- Background treatment: deep matte charcoal-to-dark green backdrop with subtle paper grain, velvet-like fabric texture, warm candle bokeh, and a dark wooden tabletop edge for realism; keep all text highly legible.
- Framing direction: centered vertical layout with a slightly asymmetrical still-life balance for a premium editorial look; include realistic card edges, layered paper, envelope corner, ribbon, pine sprigs, and small gift details.
- Target-specific text areas use {대상}, {메시지}, {타이포}, {비주얼}, {컬러}, {비율 결}, and {비율} as customizable content anchors.
- Add small printed stationery details: a date label, sender/recipient cue, tiny seasonal caption, subtle decorative tag, and small footer credit line so the card feels authentic rather than empty.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
1. Top date label area (upper 8%): add a small refined label such as "2025.12.31  YEAR-END GREETINGS" and a tiny Korean caption "겨울의 끝에서 전하는 마음" in warm gold or muted white.
2. Top header area (upper 18%): place the main Korean greeting text "올해도 함께해서 감사했습니다 — 좋은 한 해 되세요" in bold traditional serif styling, centered and large enough to dominate the first read.
3. Secondary title line: set the English phrase from {타이포} beneath the Korean heading in smaller uppercase lettering, tracking slightly expanded for a refined finish.
4. Central message block (mid 22%): display {메시지} in clear, high-contrast Korean text with comfortable line spacing, aligned to the visual center; include a small recipient cue such as "To. {대상}" or "{대상}에게".
5. Decorative note details: add subtle printed micro text like "따뜻한 마음을 전합니다", "새해 복 많이 받으세요", and a tiny footer credit "Winter Card 2025 · with gratitude" near the lower text area.
6. Still-life hero area (lower 45%): render {비주얼} as a composed holiday arrangement with candles, wine glass highlights, pine leaves, dried orange slices, brass bells, red berries, ribbon, small wrapped gift, folded envelope, handwritten tag, and textured paper card pieces arranged on a dark surface, lit like a luxury magazine still life.
7. Color and ratio integration: let {컬러} guide the accent palette while preserving the gold, dark green, white, and charcoal base; preserve the vertical card feel implied by {비율} and {비율 결}.
8. Footer zone (bottom 8%): include a small elegant sign-off line, for example "마음을 담아 · 2025 겨울", plus tiny decorative divider dots or a fine foil line.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: use Noto Serif KR or Nanum Myeongjo Bold for Korean headline text, 42–58px equivalent; use Pretendard or Inter for English subtitle, 18–24px equivalent, medium weight, expanded tracking.
- Color palette: gold #C9A24A, dark green #14281D, white #F5F2EA, charcoal #232326; accents may include muted brass highlights, warm candle amber, deep berry red, pine green, and cream paper tones.
- Paper and finish: realistic thick matte card stock with slight embossing, subtle foil-stamped gold accents, visible paper fibers, gentle edge shadow, and layered envelope texture.
- Object depth: use soft realistic drop shadows 4px y-offset, 12px blur, 15% opacity under objects and text elements for depth; candles and glass should cast believable warm reflections.
- Decorative elements: include refined dividers, small tag stickers, ribbon curls, pine needles, dried citrus, berries, and gift-wrap textures while keeping the greeting message readable.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: 85mm f/1.8 editorial product-photo look, straight-on framing with slight top-down bias for the still life.
- Lighting: studio softbox from upper-left at 45° with a gentle fill from lower-right, plus warm candle glow accents; keep highlights controlled and elegant with natural specular highlights on glass, wax, foil, and brass bells.
- Color grade: warm gold accents against cool dark green and charcoal, with slightly desaturated whites for a premium holiday print aesthetic.

[6. MOOD]

Include realistic kindergarten details such as cubbies with name stickers, picture books, attendance name tags, soft floor mats, toy baskets, low tables, crayon drawings on the wall, indoor shoes by the door, handwashing sign, snack tray, and a small teacher-note board.

Each mini-cut should include a tiny child-safe action, such as waving at the teacher, stacking blocks, eating fruit, reading a picture book, putting away toys, or preparing a blanket.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]

[6. MOOD]
Premium maternity editorial moodboard — like a Kinfolk-inspired lifestyle spread mixed with a refined hotel lookbook, modern self-studio reference page, and warm pregnancy keepsake scrapbook.
