- Use {테마} as the visual theme direction, {디저트구성} as the dessert arrangement logic, {데코} as the decorative layer stack, {컬러} as the palette foundation, {타이포} as the text styling direction, and {비주얼} as the framing approach.
- Include realistic poster information: child name, age, date/time, venue, reservation/contact, ticket or package note, sponsor area, hashtag-style caption, and small decorative labels integrated into the party design.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
1. Header zone (top 16%): place the main title in rounded Korean typography, centered and highly legible, with a small English subtitle {영문부제}, a date pill {행사일}, and a playful sticker badge reading “BIRTHDAY PARTY”.
2. Event info strip (upper-mid 10%): add compact invitation details such as “{아이이름}의 {나이}번째 생일”, “{행사시간}”, “{장소}”, and “{티켓정보}” on rounded cards or ribbon tags.
3. Backdrop layer (upper 32%): build a pastel balloon arch behind the table, paired with a shaped backdrop panel, fabric folds, hanging mini flags, illustrated stars/clouds matching {테마}, and small sponsor panel text {스폰서문구} near the lower side of the backdrop.
4. Hero cake area (center 28%): show the birthday cake as the tallest focal point, topped with a cute cake topper matching {테마}; topper text should read “{아이이름} HAPPY BIRTHDAY” with crisp acrylic or paper-cut edges, icing texture, sprinkles, and themed figurine details.
5. Dessert row (mid-lower band): arrange {디저트구성} across the table, using cupcakes, candy jars, macarons, cake pops, jelly cups, cookies, and small pedestal trays as supporting accents on both sides of the cake.
6. Table styling layer (lower 20%): cover the table with a neatly draped tablecloth, add small food labels {푸드라벨}, a mini price/package card, reservation/contact card “문의 {예약문의}”, and tiny save/share icon-style graphics like a modern social poster.
7. Decorative accents: add {데코} around the sides, rear edges, table corners, and header area so the scene feels like a real birthday setup with balloons, ribbons, confetti, paper toppers, character cutouts, and themed dessert picks.
8. Color integration: apply {컬러} across balloons, topper details, labels, ribbons, plates, and small trims while keeping the cream beige base visible as a warm party-planner catalog foundation.
9. Typography application: use {타이포} for the visible text treatment, with rounded forms, thick strokes, friendly hierarchy, and strong legibility for a kid-friendly birthday event poster.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: rounded Korean display fonts such as Pretendard ExtraBold or Noto Sans KR Bold for the main title, with a smaller English subtitle in clean sans-serif at 24–32 px equivalent; letterforms should be thick, friendly, and highly readable.
- Color palette: {컬러} plus supporting cream #F6F1E8, warm white #FFFDF8, pastel pink #F7C8D0, mint #BFE7D4, sky blue #B9D9F3, soft butter yellow #F6E7A7, and tiny coral accents for sticker highlights.
- Graphic details: use rounded stickers, scallop-edge labels, mini pennant flags, confetti dots, sparkle icons, cupcake picks, translucent acrylic sign cards, and paper-cut themed shapes that feel handmade but professionally styled.
- Border/shadow: subtle soft drop shadow 4px y-offset, 12px blur, 15% opacity under the cake, trays, label cards, and jars; use soft rounded card panels and light dimensional layering rather than hard outlines or glossy neon effects.
- Text hierarchy: main title largest, child birthday line second, event details third, and micro information such as contact, sponsor, hashtags, and package note as small but still readable poster text.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: 50mm lens, f/5.6, slight elevated front angle, studio product-shot framing with enough depth to show the full dessert table and backdrop.
- Lighting: diffused studio softbox from upper-left at 45°, gentle fill from right, soft natural shadow contrast, clean commercial catalog illumination with warm highlights on icing, acrylic toppers, and glass candy jars.
- Color grade: pastel party palette with soft cream base, slightly warm highlights, controlled saturation, and gentle cyan-pink balance reminiscent of modern event styling photography.
- Material realism: buttercream ridges, fondant topper pieces, glossy candy surfaces, paper label grain, satin ribbon sheen, matte balloon texture, translucent acrylic stands, and cotton tablecloth folds should be visible.

[6. MOOD]
Premium kids birthday event styling — polished party-planner catalog meets a playful family celebration set, with the presentation quality of modern editorial product photography and the practical information density of a real birthday party poster.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: 반드시 다음 한국어 문자열이 정확하게 보여야 함: “키즈 생일 디저트 테이블”.
- Poster title and event copy should include these readable Korean strings: “{아이이름}의 {나이}번째 생일”, “날짜 {행사일}”, “시간 {행사시간}”, “장소 {장소}”, “문의 {예약문의}”, “{티켓정보}”.
- Food labels should include clean Korean text such as “딸기 컵케이크”, “별사탕 젤리”, “무지개 마카롱”, “생일 쿠키”, plus the customizable label set {푸드라벨}.
- Add small realistic poster microcopy: “포토존 운영”, “케이크 토퍼 포함”, “예약 제작 가능”, “{해시태그}”, and sponsor/support line “{스폰서문구}”.
- The cake topper, labels, backdrop graphics, and dessert arrangement must all feel consistent with {테마}; keep the hero cake as the tallest focal point and maintain a polished symmetrical party-table layout.
- All visible text must be cleanly rendered in Korean without broken characters, warped glyphs, or unreadable spacing.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]
- Fake official seals / certifications
- Broken Korean characters or warped glyphs
- Celebrity face composites or unauthorized lookalikes

studio:prompts3:ours-629.content:
[INPUT]
- language: Korean
- output_size: 1536x1024

[1. PURPOSE]
돌잔치 풀세트 광고/소개용 리얼리스틱 평면 콜라주. 백드롭, 답례품 라벨, 케이크 토퍼, 식순지를 실제 제작 샘플처럼 한 테이블 위에 펼쳐 놓고, {아이·일자}, {굿즈 4종}, {컨셉}이 한눈에 전달되는 따뜻한 베이비 파티 브랜딩 이미지로 구성. 완성된 행사 패키지 소개 이미지처럼 {패키지명}, {행사시간}, {장소}, {부모명}, {문의}, {패키지가격}, {제작크레딧}까지 작은 인쇄 정보로 자연스럽게 포함한다.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- 화면은 가로형 1536x1024, {비율} 감각의 top-down flat lay 구성으로, 중앙에 4종 굿즈가 브랜드 패키지처럼 배치된 현실적인 제품 촬영 콜라주.
- 메인 시선은 가운데 60% 영역의 백드롭 샘플과 식순지로 모이고, 답례품 라벨과 케이크 토퍼가 좌우에 자연스럽게 겹치며 실제 촬영된 종이·아크릴·리본 질감이 느껴지게 한다.
- 배경은 크림 톤 린넨 테이블보와 매트한 종이 보드가 섞인 정물 스타일이며, 파티 준비 현장처럼 얇은 리본, 작은 꽃잎, 골드 컨페티, 미니 봉투, 실링 스티커, 샘플 컬러칩, 작은 주문 메모 카드가 주변에 놓인다.
- 상단에는 {아이·일자}를 메인 타이틀처럼 읽히게 하고, 하단에는 “첫 번째 생일”, “초대합니다”, “Thank you gift”, “DOLJANCHI SET”, “제작 문의 {문의}”, “{제작크레딧}” 같은 보조 문구와 제작 크레딧이 작게 들어간다.
- 오른쪽 아래에는 실제 상품 상세컷처럼 “SET 구성”, “행사일 {행사시간}”, “장소 {장소}”, “부모 {부모명}”, “패키지 {패키지가격}”가 적힌 작은 안내 카드와 QR 형태의 장식 코드를 배치한다.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
- Background layer: 크림색 린넨 패브릭 위에 아이보리 카드지와 살짝 비치는 트레이싱지, 종이결이 살아 있는 샘플지를 겹쳐 실제 스튜디오 촬영 같은 깊이를 만든다. 모서리에는 파스텔 리본, 말린 안개꽃, 작은 진주 장식, 골드 조각 컨페티, 봉투 안에 반쯤 들어간 초대장, 금박 샘플 스와치를 배치한다.
- Hero arrangement: 4종 굿즈를 한 세트처럼 보이게 배치한다. 백드롭 인쇄 샘플을 가장 큰 면적으로 상단/중앙에 두고, 답례품 라벨이 붙은 작은 유리병 또는 미니 박스, 케이크 토퍼 샘플, 식순지 카드를 주변에 크기 차이를 두어 정렬한다. 각 샘플에는 동일한 {컬러}, {타이포}, {컨셉} 요소가 반복되어 맞춤 제작 세트처럼 보인다.
- Backdrop area: {컨셉} 분위기가 가장 먼저 보이도록 아치형 백드롭 샘플에 메인 패턴과 문구를 크게 배치한다. 문구 예시는 “{아이·일자}”, “첫 번째 생일”, “우리 아기의 돌잔치에 초대합니다”, “오늘의 주인공”이며, 파스텔 핑크와 소프트 골드 포인트를 사용한다. 하단 작은 줄에는 “{행사시간} · {장소}”를 인쇄해 실제 행사 백월 시안처럼 만든다.
- Invitation and event card area: 접힌 초대장 카드 한 장을 추가로 보이게 하며, 상단에 “돌잔치 초대장”, 본문에 “소중한 첫 생일에 함께해 주세요”, “아빠·엄마 {부모명}”, “장소 안내 {장소}”, “문의 {문의}”를 읽을 수 있게 넣는다. 카드 하단에는 지도 아이콘, 주차 안내 아이콘, 작은 RSVP 체크박스가 인쇄된 것처럼 표현한다.
- Favor label area: 답례품 라벨은 원형 스티커, 직사각 태그, 미니 감사 카드가 함께 보이게 한다. 라벨에는 “답례품”, “감사합니다”, “Thank you”, “{아이·일자}”, “작은 마음을 담았어요”를 선명하게 넣고, 작은 리본이 묶인 유리병·쿠키 봉투·캔들 박스 위에 실제로 부착된 느낌을 준다. 태그 뒷면에는 “유통기한 2026.06.30”, “핸드메이드 쿠키” 같은 작은 실사용 문구를 더한다.
- Cake topper area: 얇은 막대형 케이크 토퍼는 골드 미러 아크릴 또는 매트 골드 종이 재질로 표현한다. “첫돌”, “Happy 1st Birthday”, 아이 이름이 들어갈 자리로 {아이·일자}를 보여주며, 아래에는 우드 스틱, 투명 받침, 작은 크림 케이크 일부와 딸기·블루베리 장식을 보이게 배치한다. 토퍼 옆 작은 포장 라벨에는 “Cake Topper · Gold Acrylic · 1ea”가 적혀 있다.
- Agenda sheet area: 식순지는 두꺼운 카드 한 장과 접힌 안내지 한 장으로 구성한다. 상단에는 “돌잔치 식순”, “TODAY’S PROGRAM”, “12:00 입장”, “12:20 성장영상”, “12:40 돌잡이”, “13:00 식사 및 인사”, “13:30 포토타임”처럼 짧은 한국어 일정이 들어가고, 하단에는 “장소 안내”, “가족 인사”, “Page 01”, “진행 도우미 안내” 같은 작은 정보 줄을 넣는다.
- Product information card: 한쪽 작은 카드에는 “{패키지명}”, “{굿즈 4종}”, “SET 구성”, “Backdrop · Favor Label · Cake Topper · Agenda Card”, “Designed for {아이·일자}”, “옵션: 컬러 변경 / 문구 수정 / 인쇄 수량 상담”, “패키지 금액 {패키지가격}”, “상담 {문의}”를 넣어 광고/소개 이미지로서 상품 구성이 분명히 보이게 한다.
- Accent details: 구름, 보헤미안, 우주, 동물 친구 중 선택된 {컨셉}의 아이콘을 백드롭, 라벨, 식순지, 토퍼, 초대장, 포장 스티커에 반복해 통일감을 만든다. 작은 스티커에는 “LOVE”, “D-1”, “BABY PARTY”, “SPECIAL DAY”, “SAVE THE DATE”, “우리 가족의 첫 축하”를 넣어 실제 굿즈 세트처럼 보이게 한다.
- Texture and finish: {결}에 맞춰 평면 mockup 콜라주이지만 실제 촬영된 정물처럼 종이 섬유, 잉크 농도, 금박 반사, 유리병 굴절, 리본의 새틴 결, 케이크 크림의 부드러운 표면이 서로 다르게 보이도록 한다.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: 한글은 Noto Serif KR 또는 본명조 계열의 세리프, 영문은 부드러운 손글씨 스크립트와 작은 산세리프를 섞는다. {타이포}의 조합이 명확히 보이도록 메인 이름은 굵고 우아하게, 일정·가격·설명·문의 텍스트는 작은 크기로 정돈한다.
- Color palette: {컬러}를 기준으로 크림 #F7F1E8, 파스텔 핑크 #F7C9D8, 소프트 골드 #D8B56A, 연한 베이지 #E9DDCF를 함께 사용하고, 종이 그림자에는 따뜻한 브라운 톤을 아주 약하게 더한다.
- Border/shadow: 각 굿즈 아래에 4px 정도의 아래쪽 오프셋과 12px 블러, 15% 불투명도의 부드러운 드롭 섀도우를 적용한다. 종이 가장자리는 미세한 두께와 섬유감이 보이도록 하고, 아크릴 토퍼와 유리병에는 작은 하이라이트를 만든다.
- Print detail: 인쇄물에는 재단선 느낌의 작은 모서리 라운딩, 은은한 금박 포인트, 반투명 트레이싱지 레이어, 스티커 광택 차이를 표현한다. 모든 문구는 실제 인쇄된 것처럼 평면에 붙어 보이며, 종이 질감과 잉크 농도가 자연스럽게 보인다.
- Realistic production cues: 출력 샘플 옆에 컬러 교정용 작은 칩, “시안 확인 완료” 메모, 수량 체크박스, 포장용 투명 OPP 봉투 일부를 배치해 실제 돌잔치 굿즈 제작 납품 전 촬영컷처럼 만든다.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: top-down flat lay 느낌의 50mm 표준 렌즈, f/5.6, 얕지 않은 선명도와 종이 질감이 살아나는 제품 촬영 스타일.
- Lighting: 상단 왼쪽에서 들어오는 부드러운 창문광, 오른쪽에서 아주 약한 보조광을 더해 리본, 유리병, 금박 토퍼의 하이라이트와 종이 그림자가 현실적으로 보이게 한다.
- Color grade: warm cream + pastel pink + muted gold의 저채도 편집톤, 밝고 따뜻한 스튜디오 무드. 화이트 밸런스는 크림빛을 살리고, 금색 포인트는 과한 노랑이 아니라 은은한 샴페인 골드로 표현한다.
- Material realism: 매트 카드지, 린넨 패브릭, 트레이싱지, 리본 새틴, 골드 미러 아크릴, 유리병, OPP 포장지, 스티커 코팅, 작은 케이크 크림의 재질 차이가 분명히 보이도록 한다.

[6. MOOD]
Korean first-birthday party stationery editorial — a refined lifestyle product spread with the calm polish of Kinfolk and modern baby-party branding, but styled as a real event preparation table with tactile paper goods, keepsakes, sample tags, pricing cards, and warm family celebration details.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: 반드시 정확히 보여야 하는 문구는 “{아이·일자}”, “{굿즈 4종}”, “{컨셉}”, “{컬러}”, “{타이포}”, “{결}”, “{비율}”, “{패키지명}”, “{행사시간}”, “{장소}”, “{부모명}”, “{문의}”, “{패키지가격}”, “{제작크레딧}”.

The image should look like a finished portrait-studio concept sheet with a baby portrait, tasteful set props, soft editorial text labels, date/location details, and subtle decorative tags.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Main subject placement: infant hero occupies the center 45–55% of the frame, with parents optionally flanking in side profile at lower left and lower right; allow a single-hero version with the baby centered and slightly elevated.
- Background treatment: {배경} as a studio-ready stage using hanji paper texture, seamless white cyclorama, natural wood paneling, soft fabric drape, or luxury suite-inspired wall details, with realistic natural-light falloff.
- Foreground styling: {주요 소품} arranged in a gentle semicircle around the baby, including tactile details such as folded hanbok fabric, small flower clusters, brass tray, wooden blocks, silk ribbon, rice-cake plate, or a modern linen cushion when appropriate to {컨셉}.
- Framing direction: portrait orientation, gentle symmetry, elegant top and bottom spacing, with a realistic studio floor plane and soft contact shadows grounding the props.
- Layout flexibility: {구도} should read clearly even when switching between family-side composition and isolated hero composition.
- Text and card elements: include a small premium studio label near the top, a date/location label, one short Korean caption, tiny decorative tags or sticker-like accents, and a discreet photographer/studio credit integrated into the layout.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
- Top zone (10–15%): refined title area like a premium studio sample board. Include Korean title text “백일 사진관”, small English subline “100 DAYS PORTRAIT”, and a small date tag such as “2026.05.01”.
- Center hero zone (45–55%): infant presented according to {구도}, with calm, centered emphasis, realistic skin tone, soft baby hair detail, natural expression, and crisp silhouette separation from the background.
- Prop zone (lower-middle 20–25%): {주요 소품} placed with intentional rhythm so each object remains identifiable; show believable materials such as matte wood grain, hanji paper fibers, linen weave, silk sheen, porcelain, dried flowers, or polished brass.
- Information zone (lower 8–12%): add small editorial details such as “Seoul Studio · Room 03”, “Concept: {컨셉}”, “Color: {컬러}”, and a tiny caption “우리 아기의 첫 100일”.
- Background zone (entire frame): {컨셉} reflected in the environment through fabric, wood, hanok-inspired curves, hotel-suite textures, or luxury-studio cues, enriched with believable depth and layered surfaces.
- Color mapping: {컬러} used consistently across props, textile accents, flowers, ribbons, title text, and small decorative labels, with the dominant tone anchored by the background.
- Finish zone: {비주얼} rendered as a polished photography-studio concept board with realistic shadows, controlled highlight rolloff, tactile surfaces, and premium editorial finishing.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: Korean lettering should use Pretendard SemiBold or Noto Sans KR Medium, clean sans-serif, medium-large title size with crisp anti-aliased edges; small labels may use lighter Noto Sans KR Regular.
- Required visible Korean/English layout text examples: “백일 사진관”, “100 DAYS PORTRAIT”, “우리 아기의 첫 100일”, “촬영 컨셉”, “서울 스튜디오”.
- Color palette: {컬러} with specific tonal control such as warm beige #D8C3A5, soft gold #C9A86A, deep red #B13A2E, off-white #F7F2EA, natural wood brown #8B6B4F.
- Border/shadow: soft studio shadow under props, 4px y-offset, 14px blur, 18% opacity; use gentle card-like layering for text tags if needed, avoiding hard outlines or glossy sticker effects.
- Surface detail: use subtle paper grain, linen weave, silk texture, floral detail, matte wooden texture, porcelain highlights, and delicate fabric folds depending on {컨셉}, avoiding plastic sheen.
- Decorative details: allow tasteful Korean celebration motifs such as bojagi folds, tiny gold dots, ribbon knots, dried baby’s-breath, peony accents, moon-jar silhouette, or modern hotel stationery details, scaled small so the baby remains the hero.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: full-frame studio portrait look, 85mm f/1.8 or 50mm f/1.4, shallow but controlled depth of field, clean subject separation.
- Lighting: soft diffused key light from upper-left at 45°, gentle fill from front-right, faint rim from back-right; if traditional mood is selected, add warm amber bounce; if white-luxury mood is selected, keep lighting neutral and high-key.
- Color grade: cream + beige + gold for traditional themes, or bright white + natural wood + muted champagne for modern luxury themes; preserve skin tone accuracy and smooth highlight transitions.
- Realism cues: visible but delicate fabric weave, natural baby skin softness, slight shadow under cheeks and hands, realistic prop scale, authentic studio floor contact, and depth in background layers.

[1. PURPOSE]

Content-rich side-by-side analysis card with table-like structure, compact mini charts, editorial labels, realistic housing-context details, and clear recommendation cues.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Vertical poster with a strong top header occupying about 15% of the frame, central comparison body taking 70%, and a compact recommendation footer around 15%.
- Main comparison split into two equal columns with a clear center divider; left side for {비교 대상} as apartment, right side for the officetel side of the comparison.
- Background should feel like a polished Korean real-estate editorial print card: warm white paper base, subtle light-gray grid texture, faint city-map contour lines, and soft paper grain while keeping all text highly readable.
- Add contextual housing visuals: small apartment tower icon on the left, compact officetel building icon on the right, tiny subway-pin and school-pin markers, simple money/tax/loan pictograms, and a small source-note strip.
- Use {비교 대상}, {비교 항목}, {장단점}, {추천}, {비주얼}, {컬러}, {비율} as the editable content fields.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
- Header area (top 15%): Set the title “아파트 vs 오피스텔 비교” in a bold modern Korean headline, centered, with thin divider lines beneath it.
- Add an editorial metadata row near the title: “REAL ESTATE GUIDE · VOL.247 · 2026년 5월호” on the left and “저장용 비교표” on the right in small Korean text.
- Subheader line: Place {비교 대상} directly under the title in smaller medium-weight text, acting as the main context line.
- Add two small pill labels under the subheader: “실거주 관점” and “투자·대출 체크” with navy/coral accents.
- Comparison body (middle 45%): Build a two-column table with {비교 항목} listed as row labels down the center-left, and the two property types compared across left/right cells.
- Table rows should include visible Korean row labels such as “가격”, “관리비”, “세금”, “입주 자격”, “대출”; add tiny matching icons inside each row for quick recognition.
- Pros/cons block (middle-lower 20%): Present {장단점} as concise bullet points with small check, caution, and minus icons, keeping each side visually balanced.
- Add realistic editorial side notes: a small callout tag reading “체크포인트” beside the pros/cons area, a tiny caption line “지역·면적·금리 조건에 따라 달라질 수 있음”, and a thin page-marker label “PAGE 01 / 03”.
- Mini chart cluster: Include {비주얼} as a small bar chart or donut chart cluster near the lower-middle area, using the same color family as the table accents; label chart segments with short Korean tags like “초기비용”, “월고정비”, “환금성”.
- Add a compact ratio badge using {비율}, styled like a finance dashboard indicator, with a tiny legend using {컬러}.
- Recommendation footer (bottom 15%): Display {추천} inside a highlighted rounded rectangle, with strongest contrast and slightly larger type for decision emphasis.
- Footer should also include a brief decision line: “신혼 → 아파트 / 1인 직장인 → 오피스텔”, plus tiny save/share micro icons and a small handle-style credit “@realestate.note”.
- Overall layout should feel like a structured editorial infographic, with careful alignment, equal spacing, clear hierarchy, and readable content density.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: Use Pretendard or Noto Sans KR for all Korean text; title in Bold 42–52px, section labels in SemiBold 22–28px, body text in Regular 18–22px, recommendation in Bold 24–30px.
- Color palette: White background, charcoal #2B2B2B, navy #1F4E79, coral #FF6B6B, and soft neutral gray #E9EDF2 for lines and table fill; allow warm off-white #FAFAF7 and pale blue-gray #F3F6FA for realistic paper/card depth.
- Border/shadow: Thin 1px charcoal or gray rules, subtle card shadows like 0px 4px 10px rgba(0,0,0,0.08), plus delicate divider ticks, tab labels, and chart outlines.
- Use {컬러} as the main accent family while maintaining navy/coral contrast between the apartment and officetel columns.
- Include fine editorial details such as section labels, caption rules, page indicator dots, miniature legend boxes, and small credit text without reducing legibility.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: Flat graphic layout, top-down infographic presentation, no photographic perspective; if any rendered objects appear, keep them as clean vector-style shapes.
- Lighting: Even studio-like illumination with crisp screen-print style contrast and very soft printed-paper depth.
- Color grade: Clean white-canvas infographic grading with navy/coral accent balance, cool neutral grays, and a lightly textured editorial print finish.
- Render as a realistic Korean social-media real-estate card rather than a blank template: visible microcopy, chart numbers, grid rules, building icons, location pins, and source/caption strips should make the poster feel complete.

[6. MOOD]
Practical Korean real-estate editorial infographic — like a Naver Finance / The New York Times comparison card blended with a polished Korean property newsletter, precise, trustworthy, and easy to scan.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: 반드시 정확히 표시해야 하는 문구: “아파트 vs 오피스텔 비교”, “가격”, “관리비”, “세금”, “입주 자격”, “대출”, “아파트: 가족·학군”, “오피스텔: 단신·역세권”, “신혼 → 아파트 / 1인 직장인 → 오피스텔”.
- Additional Korean text that should appear naturally in the image: “REAL ESTATE GUIDE · VOL.247 · 2026년 5월호”, “실거주 관점”, “투자·대출 체크”, “체크포인트”, “초기비용”, “월고정비”, “환금성”, “PAGE 01 / 03”, “@realestate.note”.
- All comparison rows must remain in a clean two-column alignment; do not swap the left/right structure.
- Typography must stay crisp, fully legible, and free of broken Korean characters.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Main scene: a home-office corner composition with a desk hero taking about 62% of the frame height, surrounded by readable editorial text blocks, item callouts, small price tags, and a bottom checklist strip.
- Space treatment: {공간} is staged as a lived-in but polished interior nook with matte painted wall, subtle floor texture, baseboard detail, cable tray, a nearby window edge or curtain, and realistic corner perspective.
- Key objects: {필수아이템} arranged as functional essentials on and around the desk, including small everyday details such as a notebook, charging cable, mug, keyboard, mouse pad, pen tray, sticky notes, and one personal decor item.
- Furniture emphasis: {추천가구} should appear as the main practical upgrade elements, positioned so the viewer can compare ergonomic desk height, chair support, monitor placement, and storage efficiency at a glance.
- Lighting setup: {조명} should be represented as layered workspace lighting with believable daylight, task light, warm accent glow, and visible light direction on the wall, desktop, and chair.
- Color direction: {컬러} should dominate room surfaces, furniture finishes, textile accessories, plant leaves, cable color, and small stationery accents.
- Visual framing: {비주얼} with small Korean furniture labels placed near key objects, plus a title header, date stamp, room-size badge, budget note, and mini floor-plan icon integrated into the poster.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
1. Header editorial zone: at the top, place the main Korean title “{포스터제목}”, subtitle “{부제}”, and issue/date line “{발행정보}” in a clean magazine-poster style; include a small vertical spine credit on the left edge reading “ROOM GUIDE / REMOTE WORK”.
2. Background and room base: build a realistic interior backdrop using {공간} with matte wall, baseboard, subtle floor grain, curtain or window-edge highlight, and gentle shadows that show real scale.
3. Desk hero zone: place a compact or medium desk in the lower-middle area, styled with {필수아이템}; the working surface should look usable and inhabited, with tidy stationery, device cables, a water glass or mug, and a small paper note.
4. Furniture highlight zone: feature {추천가구} as the most prominent upgrade items; show the chair angled slightly toward the desk, motion desk legs visible, monitor arm joint clear, and a small under-desk cable tray or footrest.
5. Lighting layer: render {조명} as a believable combination of side daylight, desk task light, and ambient lamp glow; add soft contact shadows below monitor, keyboard, chair wheels, plant pot, and storage items.
6. Color and material pass: apply {컬러} across wall tone, wood grain, desktop, chair mesh or fabric, plant leaves, lamp finish, organizer trays, and small accessories; finishes should feel tactile, matte, and residential.
7. Label and info treatment: integrate {비주얼} with neat Korean callout labels near desk, chair, monitor arm, lamp, plant, cable tray, and storage box; add small pill-shaped tags such as “높이 조절”, “눈높이 모니터”, “간접 조명”, “케이블 정리”.
8. Practical poster details: add a bottom information strip containing “공간 크기 {공간크기}”, “예산 {예산}”, “체크리스트 5”, and a save/share icon row; include a tiny barcode-like catalog mark and page number “P.03” as editorial decoration.
9. Final crop logic: keep the vertical 1024x1536 composition grounded with the desk and chair occupying the main visual weight, while text badges and callouts wrap naturally around the furniture without hiding key objects.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: Pretendard and Noto Sans KR, medium to semi-bold weight, high Korean readability for title, labels, captions, and small guide text.
- Color palette: cream, wood brown, charcoal, plant green, soft gray, muted black, and one small accent color from {강조색}; align with {컬러} and keep the palette warm and editorial.
- Poster graphics: use thin dividers, rounded label pills, small numbered dots, transparent overlay cards, barcode-style catalog mark, and tiny save/share micro icons suitable for Korean social media interior content.
- Shadows and depth: very subtle soft drop shadows under desk objects and furniture, 4px y-offset, 12px blur, 15% opacity; use natural contact shadows and ambient occlusion for realism.
- Text hierarchy: title largest, subtitle second, callouts medium, checklist and metadata small but legible; Korean spacing and punctuation must be clean.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: 35mm full-frame interior photo look, f/5.6, straight-on three-quarter room view with moderate depth and crisp furniture edges.
- Lighting: soft daylight from a side window at upper-left, supplemented by a desk LED from front-right and a warm ambient lamp near the back, with realistic shadow falloff.
- Color grade: creamy neutral base with warm wood, charcoal accents, and fresh green plant notes, similar to a premium Scandinavian workspace editorial.
- Rendering detail: realistic fabric/mesh chair texture, fine wood grain, matte wall surface, ceramic mug, paper fibers on notes, soft plant leaf variation, small cable shadows, and believable scale between monitor, chair, and desk.

[6. MOOD]
Premium home-office editorial — a calm Scandinavian apartment feature with the practical clarity of an IKEA catalog spread, the tactile warmth of a lived-in Seoul apartment, and the polished restraint of Kinfolk styling.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: 반드시 아래 한국어 문자열이 정확히 보여야 함: “홈오피스·재택 인테리어”.
- Render these Korean poster elements clearly: “{부제}”, “{발행정보}”, “공간 크기 {공간크기}”, “예산 {예산}”, “체크리스트 5”, “높이 조절”, “눈높이 모니터”, “간접 조명”, “케이블 정리”, “P.03”.
- Layout invariant: desk hero, chair, monitor arm, light, and plant must all read as a coherent work zone, with realistic interior scale and no distorted furniture proportions.
- Text rendering: all Korean labels must be clean, legible, correctly spaced, and placed as part of the designed poster rather than floating randomly.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]

- Broken Korean characters
- Celebrity composites or unauthorized public-figure likeness mashups

- Keep labels and visual blocks aligned to a professional grid, but allow realistic collage depth: overlapping paper cards, clipped photos, washi tape, corner labels, fabric edges, and grounding shadows.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
- Top title band (12-15%): large Korean headline centered: "신혼 침실 무드보드", with small editorial metadata around it such as "ROOM GUIDE VOL.05", "2026년 5월호", "PROJECT: 우리 둘의 첫 침실", and a refined thin divider line.

- Concept comparison area: present the 5 style directions as distinct columns or stacked panels, labeled "MOOD 01 호텔 럭셔리", "MOOD 02 자연 보헤미안", "MOOD 03 북유럽 미니멀", "MOOD 04 한옥 모던", "MOOD 05 핑크 로맨틱"; each panel includes a color strip, furniture photo, textile/material sample, lamp reference, and 1-line Korean style note.
- Material detail band: include fabric swatches, wood texture chips, rug samples, metal finish chips, ceramic tray details, curtain fabric, bedding close-ups, dried flowers, candle jar, framed art thumbnail, and small handwritten-style arrows pointing to important materials.
- Add catalog-like micro information: "예산 가이드", "소재 샘플", "침구", "패브릭", "수납", "벽지", "조명 계획", plus compact item tags and tiny item numbers such as "A-01", "B-02", "LAMP-03".
- Bottom annotation area (10-15%): compact Korean labels and short descriptors for each concept, aligned consistently and easy to read, with a small barcode/QR-style reference box, designer credit "디자인 큐레이션: 신혼집 스타일팀", and date stamp "2026.05".
- Use {비주얼} as the organizing principle for every panel so the collage feels like a professional interior design presentation board with believable photographed objects.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: Pretendard or Noto Sans KR for all Korean text, bold 700 for the title, semibold 600 for concept names, medium 500 for labels, 22-34px title scale and 12-16px label scale; micro captions may be 8-10px but still sharp.
- Color palette: derive each set from {컬러 팔레트}, using specific tones such as deep charcoal #1F1F1F, antique gold #B08D57, taupe #B8A89A, moss green #7C8A63, soft blush #E8C2C7, and warm ivory #F4F0E6.
- Border/shadow: thin white borders around each photo tile, subtle soft drop shadow with 4px y-offset, 12px blur, 15% opacity; fabric and material samples should cast slightly stronger contact shadows.
- Make the collage feel printed and photographed: paper fibers, slight ink texture, matte photo paper, soft tape translucency, visible fabric weave, wood grain, rug pile, ceramic glaze, brushed metal, and paper thickness.
- Korean captions should be short, readable, and theme-specific, for example: "차분한 호텔식 침실", "햇살과 라탄 포인트", "밝은 우드와 린넨", "목재 격자와 여백감", "크림 핑크 침구".

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: editorial interior photography look, 35mm lens for room shots and 85mm lens for detail cutouts, f/4 depth for the collage source images.
- Lighting: indirect ambient lighting combined with {조명}, bedside lamp glow, ceiling downlights, window-filtered daylight, and soft diffusion with gentle shadow separation.
- Color grade: warm ivory, muted beige, charcoal, and accent gold for the hotel concept; taupe, moss, and earthy sand for the bohemian concept; clean white, pale oak, and cool gray for the Nordic calm concept labeled "북유럽 미니멀"; ink black, warm wood, and restrained neutral tones for the hanok modern concept; soft pink, cream, and muted rose for the pink romantic concept.
- Texture realism: visible linen wrinkles, quilted bedding seams, velvet cushion nap, woven basket fibers, rattan details, ceramic candle holders, matte wall paint, oak veneer, brass lamp bases, paper tape, and printed photo grain.
- Layout realism: objects should sit on the board with believable perspective, small overlaps, anchored shadows, and consistent top-down editorial poster geometry.

[6. MOOD]
Premium interior design presentation board — like an Architectural Digest bedroom concept collage mixed with a Kinfolk-style moodboard spread, enriched with real studio samples, practical shopping notes, and warm newlywed home details.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: 반드시 정확히 보여야 하는 문구: "신혼 침실 무드보드", "호텔 럭셔리", "자연 보헤미안", "북유럽 미니멀", "한옥 모던", "핑크 로맨틱", "침대", "베드프레임", "협탁", "스탠드", "러그", "쿠션", "캔들", "식물", "아트 포스터".
- Additional readable Korean micro text to include: "ROOM GUIDE VOL.05", "2026년 5월호", "프로젝트: 우리 둘의 첫 침실", "예산 가이드", "소재 샘플", "침구", "패브릭", "수납", "벽지", "조명 계획", "디자인 큐레이션: 신혼집 스타일팀", "2026.05".
- Layout invariants: 5가지 컨셉이 한 장 안에서 비교 가능해야 하며, 모든 패널은 동일한 그리드 규칙과 정돈된 정렬을 유지해야 함.
- Realism invariants: 각 패널은 실제 신혼 침실에 있을 법한 가구, 조명, 패브릭, 장식 소품, 소재 샘플을 포함하고, 모든 컷아웃과 샘플에는 자연스러운 접지 그림자가 있어야 함.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]
- Fake official seals / certifications
- Broken Korean characters

studio:prompts3:ours-624.content:
[INPUT]
- language: Korean
- output_size: 1024x1536

[1. PURPOSE]
1-2 English lines: realistic vertical apartment room-tour infographic for a single-person Korean studio, designed like a shareable interior magazine / Instagram save-card.
Concrete: 1인 가구 자취방 룸투어 showing compact living flow, furniture zoning, storage tips, budget cues, and small lifestyle details that make the room feel genuinely lived-in.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Main room diagram occupies about 68–72% of the frame, with a top editorial title band at 12%, a slim metadata strip, and a bottom budget / save note band at 8–10%.
- {평수·결} describes the apartment scale and interior tone as the primary context label, displayed near the title as a small Korean subtitle chip.
- {가구 구성} should be distributed into clear zones: sleep, work, dining, cooking prep, entry, and storage, separated by thin floor-plan lines, small rugs, lighting pools, and subtle label tags.
- {수납 팁} appears as a callout cluster near cabinets, under-bed storage, pegboard hooks, wall shelving, rolling cart, and entryway shoe storage, with neat arrows pointing to the relevant furniture.
- {비주얼} defines the main rendering method, using a polished room diagram, 3D isometric mockup, or flat-plan presentation with readable Korean labels and believable household objects.
- Background treatment: warm off-white paper base with light cream grid texture, faint notebook crease, tiny measurement ticks, and soft editorial card shadows for a realistic printed-room-tour feel.
- Add social content details: small handle “@onehome_log”, date label “2026.05 ROOM TOUR”, save/share micro icons, page indicator “01 / 04”, and short hashtag line “#원룸인테리어 #자취방정리 #수납루틴”.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
1. Header band: set the main title as a bold Korean room-tour headline, centered near the top: “1인 가구 자취방 룸투어”. Add small editorial labels such as “VOL.024”, “2026년 5월호”, and “한글 정확 체크” in compact side text.
2. Main layout panel: show the room as a compact apartment overview with bed, desk, chair, small dining table, plant, wardrobe, low cabinet, laundry basket, lamp, rug, curtain, books, mug, laptop, cushions, framed print, slippers, charging cable, and entry mat placed logically for a realistic single-person flow.
3. Storage highlight panel: emphasize under-bed boxes, wall shelves, stackable fabric bins, S-hooks, vertical file holders, pegboard, and multipurpose dining table drawers with small Korean label tags and pointer lines.
4. Visual mode layer: render {비주얼} as an editorial presentation style with crisp furniture outlines, soft natural shadows, tactile wood / fabric / paper textures, and easy-to-read furniture annotations.
5. Color system: apply {컬러} as the full palette across walls, furniture, labels, textiles, rugs, lamps, and accent props so the interior looks cohesive, practical, and lived-in.
6. Budget note band: place {예산} in a compact footer block styled like a small receipt / cost summary card, with Korean lines such as “가구 예산”, “수납템”, “조명·패브릭”, and “총정리 메모”.
7. Proportion note: include {비율} as the final framing reference for a tall portrait layout, ensuring the composition fills the full vertical canvas with readable room details.
8. Extra editorial microcopy: include 2–3 short Korean blurbs around the layout, such as “침대 아래 2단 박스”, “책상 옆 30cm 틈새장”, “식탁은 작업대로 겸용”, and a small caption “오늘의 자취방 기록”.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: Pretendard or Noto Sans KR, bold for title 700, medium for labels 500, small note text 400; title around 52px, labels around 22px, note text around 16px, micro metadata around 12–14px.
- Color palette: use {컬러} plus supporting neutrals like #F6F1E8, #E7DED1, #4A4A4A, muted botanical green, warm oak brown, soft linen beige, and small charcoal accent marks.
- Border/shadow: thin 1px charcoal rules, soft drop shadow 4px y-offset, 10px blur, 12% opacity for cards and labels; add tiny pin marks, dotted guide lines, and subtle divider rules.
- Texture detail: show believable oak grain on desk and shelves, cotton texture on bedding, woven rug fibers, matte ceramic mug, paper label stickers, and faint scuffs on storage boxes.
- Label style: use rounded rectangular Korean tags, tiny arrow leaders, numbered markers ① ② ③, and consistent spacing so every furniture zone feels like a real room-tour annotation.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: clean top-down interior layout with a 35mm architectural perspective feel, or a 24mm flat-lay presentation if drawn as a plan-style poster.
- Lighting: soft diffused daylight from upper-left, low-contrast fill from the right, gentle shadows under bed, desk, shelves, chair, bins, and plant leaves, with evenly readable surfaces.
- Color grade: warm cream + oak wood + charcoal + plant green, slightly desaturated for a calm practical apartment-documentary look.
- Realism cues: include small everyday items without cluttering legibility — phone charger, folded throw, tiny calendar, laundry mesh bag, sticky notes, book stack, rice cooker corner, water bottle, and slippers near the entry.

[6. MOOD]
Modern Scandinavian Korean studio editorial — cozy, practical, magazine-like room-tour card with realistic daily-life traces, smart storage, warm daylight, and a save-worthy social media layout.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: 반드시 다음 문구가 정확히 보여야 함: “1인 가구 자취방 룸투어”, “한글 정확”, “평수·결”, “가구 구성”, “수납 팁”, “비주얼”, “컬러”, “예산”, “비율”.
- Also render the following Korean microcopy clearly where appropriate: “VOL.024”, “2026년 5월호”, “오늘의 자취방 기록”, “침대 아래 2단 박스”, “책상 옆 30cm 틈새장”, “식탁은 작업대로 겸용”, “#원룸인테리어”.
- All room labels, notes, handle text, page indicator, and budget text must be fully legible Korean with no broken syllables or mistranslated characters.
- Keep furniture arrangement realistic for a single-person room, with clear zoning, believable walking paths, and no impossible overlaps.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]
- Fake official seals / certifications
- Broken Korean characters
- Celebrity composites / unauthorized likeness

studio:prompts3:ours-623.content:
[INPUT]
- language: Korean
- output_size: 1536x1024

[1. PURPOSE]
셀프 인테리어 전후 비교용 편집형 이미지. 원룸·거실·주방·욕실 리모델링 사례를 한 장에서 바로 이해하는 Before/After 비교 포스터 스타일로, 실제 집을 촬영한 듯한 생활감, 시공 기록, 비용 메모, SNS 저장용 정보 요소가 함께 보이게 한다.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- 전체 구도는 {비율}을 반영한 좌우 2분할 비교 레이아웃으로, 왼쪽 50%는 {비포}, 오른쪽 50%는 {애프터}가 차지하게 배치한다.
- 상단에는 공간 설명 영역을 12~15% 높이로 두고, "셀프 인테리어 기록", {날짜}, {프로젝트번호}, {위치}, {계정}, {공간} 제목이 함께 보이게 한다.
- 각 패널은 동일한 카메라 높이와 시점으로 맞춰, 바닥선과 벽면 수평이 정확히 일치하게 구성한다.
- 왼쪽 {비포} 패널에는 기존 벽지, 낡은 조명, 노출된 멀티탭, 택배 박스, 임시 수납, 오래된 커튼, 바닥 흠집, 생활 먼지, 문고리 스크래치 같은 현실적인 디테일을 포함한다.
- 오른쪽 {애프터} 패널에는 {컬러} 톤의 페인트 벽, 우드 가구, 패브릭 러그, 식물, 액자, 간접 조명, 정돈된 선반, 세라믹 트레이, 책, 쿠션, 바구니 수납과 텍스처가 자연스럽게 보이도록 연출한다.
- 하단에는 {비용기간}과 {팁}을 캡션 카드 형태로 넣고, 작업 체크리스트, 사용한 컬러칩, 작은 영수증 느낌의 가격 라벨, DIY 난이도 표시, 저장/공유 아이콘, 해시태그 라인을 함께 배치한다.
- 모든 비교 요소는 {공간}을 중심으로 실제 셀프 인테리어 전후 변화가 직관적으로 보이게 정리한다.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
1. Header zone (top 14%): {공간}을 큰 제목처럼 배치하고, 작은 라벨로 "BEFORE / AFTER", "셀프 인테리어 기록", {날짜}, {프로젝트번호}, {위치}, {계정}을 넣어 포스터형 기록지와 SNS 저장 카드가 섞인 느낌을 만든다.
2. Left panel (49%): {비포} 상태의 공간을 실제 실내 사진처럼 보여주되, 흰 벽·기본 가구·약간 어수선한 생활감·낡은 손잡이·전선·스티커 자국·청소 도구·벽면 못 자국·구겨진 커튼이 읽히도록 한다. 패널 상단에는 작은 탭 라벨 "비포"와 짧은 캡션 "처음 상태"를 넣는다.
3. Right panel (49%): {애프터} 상태의 공간을 크림 벽, 우드 가구, 식물, 따뜻한 스탠드 조명, 패브릭 쿠션, 책과 트레이, 벽면 아트 프린트, 작은 방향제, 라탄 바구니가 보이도록 연출하고, 전후 차이가 즉시 느껴지게 한다. 패널 상단에는 작은 탭 라벨 "애프터"와 짧은 캡션 "완성 후"를 넣는다.
4. Center comparison marker: 두 패널 사이에 얇은 세로 구분선과 작은 원형 배지 "전후 비교"를 배치하고, 바닥재·조명·수납 변화가 한눈에 이어져 보이게 한다. 구분선 주변에는 "조명 교체", "러그 추가", "식물 배치" 같은 손글씨 화살표를 붙인다.
5. Bottom info strip (bottom 12%): {비용기간}은 작은 라벨 박스에, {팁}은 따옴표가 포함된 강조 문구로 배치한다. 옆에는 "작업 체크: 페인트 / 조명 / 러그 / 식물", "난이도 ★★★☆☆", "총비용 메모", "재료 리스트: 페인트 2L · 전구 2개 · 러그 1장", "저장해두고 주말에 따라하기" 같은 마이크로 정보를 넣는다.
6. Palette and finish: {컬러}를 기반으로 전체 톤을 맞추고, off-white 배경 위에 컬러칩, 줄자 눈금, 작은 메모 스티커, 얇은 다이어리 라인, 미니 평면도, 영수증 조각, 해시태그 "#원룸꾸미기 #셀프인테리어 #전후비교"를 더한다.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: Pretendard 또는 Noto Sans KR, 제목은 SemiBold~Bold 36~48px, 보조 문구는 Regular 18~24px, 숫자 정보는 Medium으로 또렷하게 정리한다. 작은 라벨과 체크리스트는 12~16px 수준의 실제 편집물 같은 마이크로 타이포그래피로 구성한다.
- Color palette: off-white #F6F1E8, beige #D8C7B2, warm wood brown #A7784E, soft gray #D9D9D9, deep charcoal #2E2A27, muted green #7E8F78, plus {컬러} accent swatches.
- Border/shadow: 카드형 캡션에 1px warm gray border, soft drop shadow 0px 6px 18px 12% opacity, 패널 분리는 아주 얇은 neutral divider.
- Graphic details: small date stamp, tape-like label, handwritten-style arrow marks, tiny ruler ticks, price memo sticker, material swatch chips, before/after arrow icon, bookmark/save icon, share icon, small QR-style project note graphic을 자연스럽게 포함한다.
- Interior realism: 벽지 결, 목재 무늬, 패브릭 직조감, 러그 파일, 식물 잎의 질감, 조명 그림자, 바닥 반사, 사용감 있는 가구 모서리, 케이블 정리 전후 차이, 손때와 청소 후 광택이 실제 촬영처럼 보이게 한다.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: Canon EOS R5 with RF 35mm f/1.8 Macro IS STM, eye-level interior photography, f/4 느낌의 선명한 공간 컷.
- Lighting: 자연광이 창문 쪽에서 부드럽게 들어오고, 전후 모두 같은 방향의 확산광을 유지해 비교 일관성을 확보한다. 애프터 쪽에는 은은한 웜톤 간접 조명과 작은 그림자를 더한다.
- Color grade: warm beige + cream + light wood + muted green, 약한 매거진 편집 톤으로 정돈한다.
- Rendering quality: realistic interior photo composite with editorial poster layout, crisp Korean typography, accurate perspective, believable furniture scale, visible material textures.

[6. MOOD]
Kinfolk 스타일의 따뜻한 홈 리모델링 편집 화보 느낌 — 실제 셀프 시공 기록, 생활감 있는 Before, 완성도 높은 After, 비용과 팁이 함께 읽히는 인테리어 매거진 페이지이자 저장하고 싶은 SNS 전후 비교 카드.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: 반드시 아래 문구가 한글 깨짐 없이 정확히 보여야 한다.
  - {공간}
  - {비포}
  - {애프터}
  - {비용기간}
  - {팁}
  - {날짜}
  - {프로젝트번호}
  - {위치}
  - {계정}
  - "셀프 인테리어 기록"

- Use {라벨} as style tags in the upper-right corner of each panel, aligned consistently, with a small style number marker such as 01, 02, 03, 04.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]

2. Top-left panel: render the room in {4종 스타일} first style, using {각 스타일 컬러} for the palette and a clean daytime interior editorial look. Include believable room contents such as sofa or bed depending on {공간}, side table, rug, framed wall art, curtains, plant, books, ceramics, and warm material accents.

Keep the same major furniture footprint but use a clearly different mood and color balance.

Bottom-left panel: render the same room as the third style, emphasizing distinct materials, silhouette choices, layered decor, natural surface textures, and decorative tone while keeping the layout matched. Add realistic details such as cushions, throw blanket, art frame, floor lamp, coffee-table objects, and visible fabric weave.
5. Bottom-right panel: render the same room as the fourth style, with richer contrast, upscale surfaces, refined lighting, metallic or stone accents where suitable, and a polished hospitality-inspired arrangement. Keep it believable and lived-in with selected accessories, not empty.
6. Labeling: place the style name from {라벨} in each panel’s upper-right corner in consistent Pretendard-style text, paired with a small Korean caption line such as '톤앤무드', '주요 마감', or '가구 제안'.

8. Add small per-panel material swatches near each label or along the panel bottom edge: 3-4 tiny rectangles/circles showing wood, fabric, wall color, metal, stone, or accent color. Use {각 스타일 컬러} and {컬러} as the guiding palette.

[4. STYLE RULES]

- Color palette: build each panel around {컬러} while preserving an overall restrained interior-design editorial palette; use neutral whites, warm wood, beige, taupe, terracotta, dark charcoal, muted gold, soft olive, stone gray, linen ivory, and style-specific accent colors as appropriate.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Overall layout: vertical 1024x1536 poster, strict 좌우 분할 composition with a centered comparison table bridging both sides.
- Left side occupies 42% of frame: 신축 visual panel, brighter modern apartment complex photo treatment with glass balcony lines, clean exterior walls, landscaped entrance, street trees, and subtle reflected daylight.

- Use {비교 대상}, {비교 항목}, {장단점}, {비주얼}, {컬러}, {발행처}, {비율} placeholders as the exact user-editable content anchors.
- Background should use crisp white and subtle off-white paper texture with faint editorial grid marks, small section labels, a tiny map-pin motif, and light data-card accents that support the comparison theme.
- Spacing must feel like a professional finance/editorial card, with structured columns, clear gutters, readable labels, and a realistic card-news publishing rhythm.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
1. Top header area (15%): bold title line introducing 신축 vs 구축 comparison, with {비교 대상} displayed prominently in the main headline zone. Add small metadata above the title: SLIDE 01, VOL.247, 2026년 5월호, 데이터 기준 2026.05.
2. Subheader line (5%): {비교 항목} in smaller but highly legible text, separated by a thin divider rule. Include a small page indicator 1/6 and a compact tag line: 실거주·투자 체크리스트.

Render the Korean row header exactly as 가격 / 평형 / 학군 / 입주 연도 / 관리비, with small arrow badges ↑ ↓ = and navy highlight chips for key differences.
5. Pros/cons strip (12%): {장단점} shown as short contrast bullets, using directional arrows, simple house/coin/wrench/school icons, and a small summary pill: 한 줄 결론. Keep the text concise and editorial.
6. Footer area (8%): {발행처} placed at the bottom in small publisher-credit style, aligned with the grid and separated by a thin line. Add carousel CTA and micro UI details: 저장하고 비교하기, 다음 장: 대출·세금 체크, @rebuilder_kr 부동산 카드뉴스, tiny save/share icons, and a discreet page progress bar.

- Lighting: soft overcast daylight style, even exposure across both panels, slight cool highlight on the new-build side and slightly flatter diffuse tone on the old-building side.

Professional Korean real-estate editorial card-news — like a trusted finance magazine comparison spread with newsroom clarity, real apartment context, practical data cues, and shareable Instagram carousel energy.

[1. PURPOSE]
1-2 English lines: i2i vintage film tone conversion for a portrait, preserving the original person while recreating a specific era-inspired film look. Square-format social portrait with authentic analog texture, period-accurate color grading, and believable real-world details around the subject.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Center the subject from {원본 인물} as the main focus, keeping the original framing and facial identity intact, with the face occupying about 45-55% of the frame.
- Maintain the original pose implied by {자세·의상}; do not change body angle, crop style, or camera distance beyond the vintage-film reinterpretation.
- Use {배경} as the contextual setting, enriching it with plausible era-matched details such as worn walls, curtains, café tables, street signs, film-era furniture, window reflections, photo-album shadows, or everyday objects that naturally fit the scene.
- Apply {시대 결} to guide the overall era feel, while {필름 결} and {컬러 톤} define the final film texture and palette.
- If the source composition allows it, include a subtle analog-photo artifact such as an orange date stamp, small lab-scan numbering, or handwritten album-note feel near an edge, without covering the face.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
- Base image preservation: keep the same person, same expression, and same composition framing from the reference, with only the film styling transformed.
- Subject treatment: render {원본 인물} with natural skin texture, fine pores, flyaway hair, realistic fabric detail, slight film softening, and subtle analog halation around highlights; avoid beauty-filter smoothing.
- Era styling layer: translate {시대 결} into a convincing period-specific snapshot look, matching the implied decade through wardrobe feel, background cues, lighting behavior, surface aging, and tonal response.
- Texture layer: apply {필름 결} with visible film grain, mild color shift, gentle exposure roll-off, faint dust specks, tiny scratches, scan noise, faded edges, slight gate weave, and realistic lab-scan imperfections where appropriate.
- Setting layer: depict {배경} as a believable environment from the selected era, including tactile surfaces like wallpaper, brick, wood grain, vinyl flooring, curtain fabric, old posters, café menus, street pavement, or household objects when they fit the source.
- Color layer: grade according to {컬러 톤}, keeping skin tones coherent and avoiding modern digital saturation.
- Optional photo-memory details: add a tiny timestamp such as “1998.05.01”, “서울”, or “봄 오후” only if it feels like a real film-camera imprint or album annotation; keep it small, imperfect, and peripheral.
- Final finish: output a square 1024x1024 vintage film i2i result with preserved identity, period authenticity, layered analog texture, and a lived-in photographic mood.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: no headline typography; only tiny authentic photo artifacts are allowed, such as an orange camera timestamp, film-lab scan number, or a small album-note style mark. If Korean appears, render it accurately, e.g. “서울”, “봄 오후”, or “추억”.
- Color palette: derive from {컬러 톤}; favor era-specific muted amber, faded cyan, soft yellow, washed sepia, oxidized green, warm indoor tungsten, or gentle pastel shifts rather than modern vivid colors.
- Film border/shadow: allow realistic film-scan edge darkening, light leaks, corner fading, soft vignette, uneven exposure, or a subtle printed-photo edge if it suits {필름 결}.
- Detail density: include natural environmental texture and era-specific background cues while keeping the subject visually dominant and recognizable.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: 35mm film snapshot look, 50mm f/2.0 or compact point-and-shoot equivalent, with mild focus softness and realistic analog grain.
- Lighting: preserve the reference lighting style as closely as possible; if rebuilding, use soft ambient room light, window daylight, tungsten practical lamps, or overcast street light with gentle contrast and period-realistic highlight bloom.
- Color grade: period-authentic vintage grading matched to {시대 결}, with filmic blacks, softened highlights, uneven color response, subtle shadow tint, and the palette direction from {컬러 톤}.
- Material realism: keep fabric weave, hair strands, skin texture, glass reflections, wall texture, paper aging, and dust visible enough to feel like a real scanned photograph.

[6. MOOD]
Authentic analog portrait conversion — like a well-preserved family album scan, a 35mm street snapshot from a vintage photography archive, or a rediscovered personal photo with real atmosphere and tactile film history.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: if any tiny date/location/album mark is rendered, it must be legible Korean or numeric text such as “서울”, “봄 오후”, “추억”, or “1998.05.01”; do not add large captions.
- Preserve the exact subject identity from {원본 인물}; do not alter facial structure, age, gender expression, or recognizable features.
- Keep the original composition framing and subject placement as closely as possible while changing only the film-era styling and surrounding analog atmosphere.
- Maintain believable vintage texture: grain, slight color fade, dust, small scratches, halation, and analog imperfections are encouraged; AI-smooth skin is not.
- Match {비율} as a square social portrait result while preserving the 1024x1024 output size implication.

[INPUT]

[1. PURPOSE]
Anime illustration conversion from an input portrait/photo into a Japanese-style i2i character image. Preserve the original person’s identity and pose while translating the scene into a warm, content-rich anime still with polished 셀 셰이딩, believable environment detail, and a lived-in cinematic atmosphere.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Main subject: {원본 인물} is the clear focal point, occupying about 60% of the vertical frame, with the face and upper body kept closest to the camera perspective from the source image.
- Pose and expression: preserve {자세·표정} from the reference photo, keeping the head angle, shoulder line, gaze direction, and hand placement consistent with the original composition.
- Background treatment: replace the source background with {배경 결}, rendered as a softly painted anime environment with layered depth, recognizable everyday details, and natural atmosphere behind the subject.
- Environmental richness: include subtle real-world anime details that fit {배경 결}, such as warm window reflections, potted plants, a distant bicycle, cafe stools, soft street signage, utility wires, falling leaves, light dust particles, or blurred passersby far in the background.
- Color direction: apply {컬러 팔레트} across clothing accents, skin shading, sky/land tones, signage accents, props, and atmospheric highlights for a cohesive animated look.
- Framing: maintain a portrait-oriented composition with natural headroom and balanced depth, using foreground bokeh or soft environmental layers to make the portrait feel like a captured anime scene rather than an isolated character cutout.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
- Subject pass: redraw {원본 인물} as a faithful anime character while preserving facial identity, hairstyle silhouette, eye spacing, jawline impression, and recognizable features from the source.
- Pose pass: lock in {자세·표정} so the final illustration matches the original body language instead of creating a new pose.
- Line and shading pass: use crisp clean linework, soft 셀 셰이딩, and gentle gradient transitions on cheeks, hair strands, eyelids, hands, and clothing folds.
- Clothing/material pass: translate the source outfit into anime form while retaining its recognizable shape, fabric weight, seams, collars, buttons, accessories, and small highlights from {컬러 팔레트}.
- Background pass: build {배경 결} with simplified but atmospheric anime scenery, including perspective lines, light reflections, small props, believable surfaces, and soft background characters or objects only where they support the scene.
- Detail pass: add cinematic micro-details such as reflected sky color on hair edges, tiny highlights in the eyes, soft blush, fabric creases, rim-lit flyaway hairs, and dust or pollen catching the light.
- Color pass: blend {컬러 팔레트} into skin highlights, shadow edges, environmental accents, and background props, keeping the overall palette warm and harmonious.
- Final conversion pass: enforce {anime 결} as the dominant visual finish, with a polished Japanese anime illustration feel rather than a realistic photo filter.
- Aspect pass: keep the final output in {비율} without cropping important facial features, hands, hairstyle, or defining outfit details.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: no main title overlay; if background signage naturally appears, keep it short and legible in Korean, such as “카페”, “오늘의 메뉴”, or “봄 산책”, integrated into the environment rather than placed as graphic design text.
- Color palette: use {컬러 팔레트} with soft warm amber highlights, pastel sky tones, natural greens/blues where applicable, and slightly desaturated shadows for anime readability.
- Environment style: background objects should feel hand-painted and cohesive with the character, with enough detail to suggest a real place while staying secondary to the portrait.
- Line quality: clean anime contour lines on the face and hair, slightly lighter lines on clothing and background, with controlled variation in line weight around eyes, chin, fingers, and hair tips.
- Border/shadow: if a subject separation effect is needed, use natural rim light and ambient occlusion from the scene rather than a graphic outline halo.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: portrait-photo base translated as if shot on a 85mm f/1.8 lens, shallow depth of field, then stylized into anime line art while preserving the original framing.
- Lighting: soft diffused daylight from upper-left at roughly 45°, with a gentle fill from the opposite side, mild rim light to separate hair from the background, and tiny specular accents on eyes and hair.

- Hero vehicle layer: {차종} modeled as a highly detailed 3D render with sharp panel edges, refined glass transparency, realistic tire tread, brake calipers, wheel lug details, headlamp internals, grille depth, door gaps, windshield reflections, and premium surface reflections.
- Finish layer: {결} applied to bodywork and trims as a polished CGI material treatment, balancing mirror-like highlights with visible micro-detail on the paint, metal parts, rubber tires, glass, chrome, carbon fiber, or brushed aluminum accents where appropriate.
- Environment layer: {배경} designed to support the vehicle silhouette with rich but controlled context: cinematic urban night ambience, luxury studio architecture, dramatic mountain road, tunnel lighting, coastal highway, or futuristic showroom elements that make the scene feel physically present.
- Lighting layer: {조명} set to carve out the vehicle shape with strong specular highlights on hood, roof, shoulder line, grille, and side panels, plus realistic shadow falloff underneath and reflected light sources visible on paint and glass.
- Color layer: {컬러 톤} used as a signature palette cue, combining the car’s identity with a dark surround, graphite surfaces, reflective metallics, and one focused accent color for premium contrast.
- Format layer: {비율} maintained as a wide advertising composition with balanced left-right tension, strong hero emphasis, and enough environmental storytelling to feel like a finished campaign key visual.
- Detail layer: include realistic road grit near tires, faint water droplets or floor polish streaks when appropriate, soft bokeh highlights in the distance, subtle lens flare from practical lights, and physically accurate reflections that follow the vehicle geometry.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: allow refined automotive campaign microcopy only if it enhances realism; keep it secondary to the car. Suggested Korean text elements: headline “나다운 주행의 기준”, small line “2026 시그니처 에디션”, background event note “프리뷰 나이트 05.24”, or plate text “서울 12가 3456”.
- Color palette: {컬러 톤} supported by charcoal black, deep graphite, electric accent hues, reflective glass highlights, warm practical lights, and restrained metallic highlights; use near-black tones like #0B0D10 and #12161D for depth.
- Shadow and depth: soft contact shadows under all four tires, realistic occlusion in wheel wells and grille cavities, layered reflections on floor or road surface, gentle atmospheric perspective in the far background, and a subtle cinematic vignette that focuses attention on the vehicle.
- Environment detail: add believable premium ad set elements such as architectural pillars, LED light bars, painted road lines, puddle reflections, glass panels, small wayfinding signs, distant traffic bokeh, or studio rig reflections, scaled naturally and never competing with the vehicle.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: full-frame cinematic CGI look, equivalent to an 85mm lens at f/2.8 for a compressed premium perspective, or a 35mm low-angle beauty shot when the composition needs more environment.
- Lighting: studio-quality key light from upper-left at 45°, strong rim light from rear-right, controlled fill to preserve body contour, practical light reflections from the scene, and soft shadow grounding the tires.
- Color grade: luxury automotive ad grade with deep blacks, cool graphite midtones, vivid accent reflections, selective warm highlights, realistic specular rolloff, and a slightly desaturated background so the vehicle remains dominant.
- Rendering quality: ray-traced reflections, physically based materials, clean anti-aliased edges, realistic glass refraction, accurate tire rubber roughness, and high-resolution texture detail on the vehicle and surrounding surfaces.

[6. MOOD]
Premium automotive campaign visual — Hyundai / Genesis CGI commercial aesthetic with cinematic showroom intensity, dynamic road presence, and museum-level product presentation. The final image should feel like a real launch campaign still: polished, expensive, tactile, and emotionally aspirational.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: if any Korean appears, render it cleanly and legibly, such as “나다운 주행의 기준”, “2026 시그니처 에디션”, “프리뷰 나이트 05.24”, or “서울 12가 3456”; do not garble Hangul.
- Composition invariants: the vehicle must remain the single hero subject, fully intact, with precise proportions, realistic reflections, correctly aligned wheels, consistent perspective, and no distortion.
- Realism invariants: preserve believable scale between car, tires, floor, road markings, signage, light sources, and background architecture; reflections must match the scene and not float randomly.
- Render quality: clean CGI realism, no plastic-looking surfaces, no accidental blur on the car body, no extra wheels, no malformed lights, no duplicated vehicle parts, and no impossible panel geometry.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]
- Fake official seals / certifications
- Broken Korean characters

[INPUT]
- language: Korean
- output_size: 1024x1024

[1. PURPOSE]
3D food render poster for social media and portfolio use, with a polished magazine-food aesthetic that can swap between sushi, pizza, dessert, ramen, chicken, or fruit.
Render the food as an appetizing hero object with miniature stylization, combining realistic surface detail, clay-like softness, and a lived-in premium tabletop scene suitable for a square editorial menu post.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Main subject placement: {음식} occupies the central 62% of the frame as the hero, slightly lifted above the ground plane or plated on a low dish so the cast shadow is visible and readable.
- Background treatment: {배경} as a tactile studio tabletop scene with believable surface texture, gentle color variation, and food-appropriate context such as a ceramic plate, parchment sheet, lacquer tray, linen napkin, sauce dish, crumbs, herbs, sesame, fruit slices, or steam accents depending on {음식}.
- Framing and spacing: keep the hero food dominant in a square poster layout, with supporting details arranged around it to create a realistic editorial food set rather than an empty product mockup.
- Surface treatment: place the subject on a premium tabletop, plate, tray, or small plinth with realistic contact shadows, tiny crumbs, glaze marks, sauce streaks, moisture beads, or powder dusting where appropriate.
- Poster information layer: add small editorial menu-poster details around the food, including a top date label, short Korean title line, tiny price or volume tag, and a small social handle, integrated as tasteful printed or overlay typography.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
- Hero object (center 62%): {음식} modeled as a refined 3D food render with glossy highlights, tiny texture imperfections, appetizing volume, clean edge definition, and visible ingredient layering; keep the form stylized but rich enough to feel like premium food advertising.
- Material pass: apply {결} to the food surface, mixing soft specular reflections with micro-detail such as toasted edges, rice grain definition, melted cheese pull texture, cream swirls, fruit gel shine, crispy crust pores, sauce thickness, or powder granules as appropriate to {음식}.
- Base environment: build the scene around {배경} with layered tabletop objects that naturally belong with the food: a plate or tray, small garnish pieces, crumbs, sauce droplets, folded napkin, chopsticks, fork, cup, menu slip, or small ingredient fragments, all scaled to support the hero food.
- Light behavior: shape the scene with {조명} so the shadow falls softly and the highlights wrap naturally around the food, emphasizing rounded forms, moist surfaces, crispy textures, and dimensional 3D depth.
- Color emphasis: guide the palette using {컬러 톤}, ensuring the food remains the highest-contrast element while the surrounding props, tabletop, and typography harmonize with the same palette.
- Format control: maintain a square composition using {비율}, with the subject centered, fully readable, and supported by balanced editorial details around the frame.
- Micro text elements: include short Korean poster copy such as "오늘의 메뉴", "셰프 추천", "한입의 즐거움", "₩12,900", "VOL.03", "2026.05", and "@render_kitchen"; keep text small-to-medium except for one clear headline.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: use Pretendard SemiBold or Noto Sans KR Medium for visible Korean food-poster typography. Set one bold Korean title near the lower or upper third, such as "오늘의 메뉴" or "셰프 추천 {음식}", plus smaller support text like "2026.05", "VOL.03", "₩12,900", and "@render_kitchen".
- Color palette: use food-specific signature colors from {컬러 톤}, supported by tactile neutrals such as warm ceramic, muted pastel paper, wood grain, stone, brushed metal, linen, or charcoal depending on {배경}; allow vivid food color accents where appetizing.
- Border/shadow: use a soft drop shadow with 4px y-offset, 14px blur, and 16% opacity for the main object or typography accents; avoid harsh outlines while allowing subtle printed-poster depth, small labels, decorative dividers, and soft graphic shapes.
- Decorative graphic system: add small editorial elements such as thin divider lines, a circular price tag, tiny corner index marks, ingredient icon dots, or a small menu-card strip; these should feel like a designed social food poster, not a sterile catalog render.
- Texture realism: preserve visible texture in the food and set dressing, including glaze, crumbs, grains, bubbles, char marks, sauce sheen, condensation, ceramic speckles, paper fibers, or wooden pores where relevant.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: studio product photography look, equivalent to a 85mm macro-style lens at f/8 for crisp food detail and shallow scene clutter.
- Lighting: soft diffused natural light with a warm amber fill, key light from upper-left at about 45°, subtle rim light from upper-right, and gentle shadow falloff.
- Color grade: premium editorial food grade with clean neutrals, warm highlights, and slightly enriched food tones; keep the background supportive while allowing tactile props, typography, and garnish details to make the poster feel real and content-rich.
- Render quality: physically based 3D render with global illumination, realistic subsurface hints for soft ingredients, believable roughness variation, high-resolution texture maps, and gentle ambient occlusion in contact areas.

[6. MOOD]
Premium 3D food editorial — like a high-end Blender food render for a boutique café menu campaign, with playful miniature realism, appetizing surface detail, warm studio lighting, and designed Korean social-poster information.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: render all on-image Korean text cleanly and legibly. Recommended text strings include "오늘의 메뉴", "셰프 추천", "한입의 즐거움", "신선한 재료", "₩12,900", "2026.05", "VOL.03", and "@render_kitchen".
- Composition invariant: keep the main food subject centered, dominant, and fully readable in a square frame while surrounding it with believable food styling, tabletop texture, and small editorial menu details.
- Style invariant: preserve the 3D food render look with a mix of realistic detail and clay-like softness; do not turn it into flat illustration or photographic real food.
- Content richness: include food-appropriate contextual details such as garnish, sauce, crumbs, steam, utensils, dishware, napkin, menu label, or ingredient fragments when they naturally match {음식}.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]
- Fake official seals / certifications
- Broken Korean characters
- Celebrity composites / unauthorized likeness

studio:prompts3:ours-612.content:
[INPUT]
- language: Korean
- output_size: 1024x1024

[1. PURPOSE]
Isometric 3D city neighborhood illustration, square composition for poster-style sharing and thumbnail use.
Miniature diorama-like urban scene with a friendly handcrafted editorial finish, detailed enough to feel like a real lived-in neighborhood block with shops, signage, daily routines, and small civic details.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- 전체 프레임은 1024x1024 정사각형 캔버스 안에 35° 아이소메트릭 시점으로 구성하고, 중앙 동네 블록이 화면의 약 70%를 차지하도록 배치한다.
- {동네 콘셉트}은 도시/동네의 성격을 정하는 핵심 설정이므로, 한옥+모던 혼합 또는 유럽·일본·미국풍 중 하나가 자연스럽게 읽히는 거리 구조, 지붕 형태, 창문 비례, 간판 배치를 유지한다.
- 배경은 부드러운 하늘 그라데이션과 아주 옅은 원거리 건물 실루엣으로 처리하고, 바닥은 밝은 시멘트/석재 타일, 보도블록, 작은 맨홀, 배수구 라인, 점자블록, 도로 가장자리 경계석을 넣어 아이소메트릭 구조가 또렷하게 보이게 한다.
- 길의 흐름은 대각선으로 시선을 끌고 가도록 구성하며, 모서리에는 횡단보도, 코너 화단, 버스 정류장 표지, 동네 안내 지도, 작은 전단 게시판이 자연스럽게 이어지게 한다.
- {구성 요소}는 건물, 길, 자동차, 인물, 나무, 가로등, 꽃집, 카페가 한 화면 안에서 층층이 읽히도록 배치하고, 각 요소가 실제 동네의 생활 장면처럼 연결되게 한다.
- 화면 안 텍스트는 간판·생활 안내·거리 표지 위주로 넣는다: 꽃집 간판 “오늘의 꽃”, 카페 간판 “골목카페”, 거리 배너 “봄 산책길”, 버스 정류장 “동네입구”, 골목 표지 “느티나무길 12”, 게시판 포스터 “주말 플리마켓”.
- 작은 포스터처럼 공유해도 읽히도록 상단 한쪽의 거리 배너나 벽면 포스터에 {동네 타이틀}을 작게 넣고, 하단 안내판에는 {동네 태그라인}을 넣어 장면의 장소성을 강화한다.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
- Base plane: 밝은 베이지 톤의 바닥 평면 위에 도로와 보도를 분리해 배치하고, 도로에는 얇은 차선, 횡단보도, 자전거 표시, 빗물받이, 맨홀 커버, 미끄럼 방지 패턴, 작은 공사 콘 1~2개를 넣어 실제 거리 질감을 만든다.
- Main buildings: 3~5채의 건물을 화면 중앙과 좌우에 분산 배치하되, 가장 큰 건물 하나는 화면 중간 35% 영역에 두고 나머지는 20~25% 규모로 리듬 있게 배치한다. 1층에는 카페, 꽃집, 작은 서점, 식료품점 같은 상가를 넣고 2층 이상에는 창문, 커튼, 발코니 화분, 실외기, 우편함, 우유 배달함, 작은 주소판을 배치한다.
- Storefront details: 카페는 어닝, 테라스 의자 2개, 원형 테이블, 메뉴 입간판 “오늘의 메뉴”, 문 앞 매트 “어서오세요”를 갖추고, 꽃집은 바구니 꽃, 물뿌리개, 꽃 가격표 “튤립 ₩3,000”, 작은 배달 박스를 갖춘다. 서점 창문에는 책 더미, 추천 문구 “이달의 책”, 운영 시간 “OPEN 10:00”을 붙인다.
- Street life: 길 위에 작은 자동차 1~2대, 자전거 1대, 전동 스쿠터 1대, 보행자 3~6명, 반려견을 산책시키는 인물 1명, 카페 앞에서 음료를 기다리는 인물 1명을 넣어 스케일감을 준다. 모두 아이소메트릭 각도에 맞게 정렬하고 과장된 원근 왜곡은 피한다.
- Greenery and props: 나무, 가로등, 꽃집 화분, 카페 테라스 의자, 파라솔, 메뉴 입간판, 분리수거함, 벤치, 우체통, 택배 보관함, 작은 노점 카트, 자전거 거치대, 전봇대와 얇은 전선, CCTV, 소화전 같은 소품을 건물 전면과 코너에 붙여 넣어 동네의 생활감을 강화한다.
- Signage and micro text: 간판과 안내문은 짧고 읽기 쉬운 한국어로 구성한다. 예: “신선마켓”, “작은서점”, “오늘의 메뉴”, “아메리카노 ₩4,500”, “OPEN 10:00”, “1번 출구”, “골목 지도”, “느티나무길 12”, “택배함”, “분리배출”. 텍스트는 오브젝트 면에 맞춰 아이소메트릭 각도로 자연스럽게 붙인다.
- Neighborhood information layer: 버스 정류장 표지에는 “동네입구 04-128”, 작은 시간표에는 “마을버스 07:20 / 07:45”, 지도판에는 “산책 코스 800m”, 벽보에는 “주말 플리마켓 5.18 토 11:00”처럼 실제 동네에서 볼 법한 생활 정보를 넣는다.
- Signature accents: {컬러 팔레트}에서 하나의 액센트 컬러를 간판, 창문 프레임, 작은 차체, 꽃 장식, 거리 배너 중 2~3곳에 반복적으로 사용해 동네 전체가 통일되어 보이게 한다.
- Atmosphere: {시간대}에 맞춰 그림자 길이와 하이라이트 색을 조절한다. 밤 설정이면 창문 불빛, 가로등, 카페 내부 조명, 작은 네온 간판 “OPEN”, 젖은 보도에 비친 간판 반사가 부드럽게 반짝이도록 처리한다.
- Story details: 카페 테이블 위 컵, 꽃집 앞 물뿌리개, 서점 창가의 책 더미, 배달 상자, 빨래가 걸린 발코니, 코너에 붙은 작은 포스터 “주말 플리마켓”, 강아지 물그릇, 아이가 들고 가는 풍선, 창가의 고양이, 반쯤 열린 카페 문처럼 한 번 더 들여다보고 싶은 디테일을 넣는다.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: 화면 내 텍스트는 Pretendard SemiBold 또는 Noto Sans KR Medium, 18~28px 수준의 깔끔한 UI 느낌으로 사용하되, 간판·버스 표지·메뉴판·벽보·주소판처럼 실제 거리 요소에 자연스럽게 배치한다.
- Color palette: {컬러 팔레트}를 기반으로 베이지 #E8DCC8, 우드 브라운 #A97B50, 세이지 #A9B89A, 따뜻한 앰버 #D89A4B, 그리고 한 가지 액센트 컬러를 조합한다.
- Border/shadow: 오브젝트 아래에 10px y-offset, 18px blur, 18% opacity의 부드러운 그림자를 넣고, 가장자리는 얇은 1px 내외의 정돈된 윤곽으로 마감한다.
- Surface finish: 과도한 광택 없이 매트한 종이 모형/클레이 모형 질감으로 정리하되, 벽돌, 목재, 유리창 반사, 보도블록, 나뭇잎, 꽃송이, 금속 가로등, 플라스틱 버스 표지, 종이 포스터의 재질 차이가 가까이 보면 느껴지도록 한다.
- Detail density: 중심 블록에는 풍부한 생활 디테일을 배치하고, 외곽으로 갈수록 크기와 명도를 낮춰 주인공 거리 장면이 명확히 보이게 한다.
- Shape language: 건물과 소품은 둥근 모서리와 정돈된 모듈형 비례를 사용하되, 손으로 만든 미니어처처럼 약간의 비대칭, 작은 칠 벗겨짐, 화분마다 다른 높이, 간판별 다른 두께를 넣어 자연스럽게 보이게 한다.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: 35mm equivalent wide view, orthographic-like isometric render, f/8 depth consistency, clean miniature city model framing.
- Lighting: Daytime uses diffused light from upper-left at 45 degrees; golden hour uses low warm side light with longer soft shadows; night uses window glow, street lamps, and small neon accents with soft cinematic falloff.
- Color grade: Warm beige, sage, and amber low-saturation grade; cream highlights, gentle gray-brown shadows, and one controlled accent color repeated across signage and props.
- Rendering finish: Handcrafted 3D editorial illustration with realistic miniature textures, soft ambient occlusion in corners, tiny contact shadows under people and street props, crisp but warm object edges.
- Material detail: Matte clay-paper surfaces, subtle rough plaster, tiny brick seams, warm wood grain, translucent glass reflections, painted metal posts, cloth awnings, and paper poster fibers visible at close inspection.
- Composition finish: Square poster-ready isometric diorama, balanced object rhythm, readable micro signage, and clear layered depth from foreground curb to rear rooftops.

[6. MOOD]
손으로 만든 동네 모형을 정갈하게 내려다보는 따뜻한 아이소메트릭 도시 일러스트. 작은 가게들이 열려 있고 사람들이 천천히 오가며, 간판·포스터·버스 표지·화분·테라스 소품이 실제 생활의 흔적처럼 쌓인 안전하고 다정한 동네 산책 풍경으로 보이게 한다. {분위기}가 색감, 조명, 인물 행동, 가게 디테일에 자연스럽게 반영되어야 한다.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: 화면에 들어가는 한글은 “오늘의 꽃”, “골목카페”, “작은서점”, “신선마켓”, “봄 산책길”, “동네입구”, “아메리카노 ₩4,500”, “OPEN 10:00”, “주말 플리마켓”, “느티나무길 12”, “마을버스 07:20”, “분리배출”, “{동네 타이틀}”, “{동네 태그라인}”처럼 짧고 정확하게 렌더링해야 하며 글자 깨짐이 없어야 한다.
- Isometric 35° 구도를 유지하고, 건물·도로·가로등·나무·인물·자동차·간판·전봇대·벤치의 크기 비례가 서로 일관되게 보이도록 한다.
- 전체 분위기는 과장된 3D 광고 렌더가 아니라, 작은 도시 모형을 섬세하게 전시한 편집 일러스트처럼 보여야 한다.
- {동네 콘셉트}, {구성 요소}, {렌더링 결}, {컬러 팔레트}, {시간대}, {비율}, {분위기}의 설정이 최종 이미지의 건축 양식, 질감, 색, 조명, 구성 비율, 생활 장면에 명확히 반영되어야 한다.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]
- Fake official seals/certifications
- Broken Korean characters
- Celebrity composites or unauthorized likeness

[1. PURPOSE]
Isometric 3D interior illustration for a compact lifestyle/editorial graphic, designed as a square social-media-friendly room overview.
Warm Dribbble/Behance-style room presentation with realistic everyday home details, small readable Korean labels, and a friendly Scandinavian interior mood.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Main structure: a single isometric room cutaway built at a consistent 35° axonometric angle, filling the square canvas as a complete miniature interior diorama.
- Space type: {공간} presented as a clearly readable interior shell with walls, floor plane, partial partitions, baseboards, and an optional open ceiling depending on the chosen room.
- Furniture and props: {가구와 소품} arranged in lived-in functional zones, with realistic scale relationships between major furniture, storage, lighting, textiles, and tabletop items.
- Everyday realism: include {생활 디테일} such as mugs, books, folded fabric, slippers, charging cable, small boxes, tissue case, wall hooks, framed art, calendar, and soft textiles to make the space feel inhabited.
- Texture and form: smooth 3D-rendered surfaces with subtle bevels, visible wood grain, woven fabric, ceramic sheen, paper edges, rug texture, and soft edge highlights.
- Label treatment: {라벨 방식} placed near key furniture zones, connected with small leader lines or tiny pill tags aligned to the isometric perspective.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
- Base room plane: establish the isometric floor in a stable 35° view, with walls, floor trim, doorway/window hints, and compact architectural boundaries mapped into a coherent room layout.
- Primary furniture zone: place the largest items from {가구와 소품} first so the room reads instantly as {공간}; set the dominant object slightly off-axis and allow secondary objects to wrap naturally around it.
- Secondary furnishing zones: add lamps, clocks, books, plants, baskets, wall shelves, cushions, side tables, toiletries, kitchenware, or office tools according to the selected room type.
- Surface detailing: apply light wood, fabric, matte painted wall, ceramic tile, paper, glass, and metal finishes with gentle tonal variation so the room feels designed and tangible.
- Graphic layer: add a small room-info tag, tiny floor-plan marker, date sticker, and Korean labels using {라벨 방식}; include {벽면 텍스트} as a small poster, calendar, memo, or framed print.
- Floor and textile layer: include {바닥 디테일} such as rug pattern, plank seams, tile grid, floor mat, slippers, or cable trail, all following the isometric angle.
- Final readability: maintain clear object silhouettes, readable labels, consistent scale, and recognizable room functions at thumbnail size.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: use Pretendard or Noto Sans KR for labels, medium weight, 12–18px equivalent, with tight but readable spacing and crisp anti-aliased edges.
- Color palette: use {컬러 팔레트} with soft cream base, natural oak wood tones, muted sage green accents, and warm amber highlights; let small decor items introduce gentle complementary colors.
- Border/shadow: use soft ambient shadow under furniture, 8px vertical offset, 18px blur, 12–18% opacity; add faint contact shadows at object feet, rug edges, shelves, and wall-mounted items.
- Render finish: polished editorial 3D with tactile materials, slightly glossy ceramic/glass details, matte textiles, softly rounded corners, and fine ambient occlusion in corners.
- Decoration: include wall art, calendar, small stickers, patterned rug, book spines, plant leaves, and practical household accessories that match {분위기}.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: isometric 3D render, orthographic-like axonometric view, equivalent to a 50mm clean product-render perspective with no dramatic distortion.
- Lighting: soft studio key from upper-left at about 45°, gentle fill from front-right, subtle ambient occlusion in corners, warm practical lamp glow where appropriate.
- Color grade: warm cream + oak + sage + amber with restrained contrast, slightly pastel midtones, realistic material response, and a calm editorial finish.

[6. MOOD]
{분위기} — modern design-platform interior mockup with a friendly Scandinavian home-decor feel, cozy lived-in details, and a curated lifestyle-magazine miniature-room quality.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: if visible labels are used, render the following Korean strings correctly as tiny but legible room graphics: "자취방", "거실", "주방", "욕실", "홈오피스", "신혼 침실", "침대", "책상", "소파", "식물", "오늘의 집", "5월 캘린더", "작은 가구 라벨".
- Perspective invariant: keep a consistent isometric 35° structure across the entire room, including furniture, labels, rug patterns, tiles, shelves, and wall decor.
- Layout invariant: labels, leader lines, furniture silhouettes, and tiny props must remain readable and not visually merge into one another.
- Rendering invariant: Korean letters must be intact, room geometry must remain stable, and object proportions must feel plausible for a compact interior.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]
- Fake official seals / certifications
- Broken Korean characters
- Celebrity composites or recognizable real-person likenesses
- Severe warped geometry that breaks the isometric view
