[1. PURPOSE]
3D SD character miniature render for cute collectible-figure style visuals, square composition for stickers, thumbnails, profile art, and boutique toy-catalog imagery.
A toy-like character portrait with chibi proportions, crafted to feel like a hand-finished painted figure photographed on a small premium display set.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Main subject: {캐릭터 컨셉} placed centrally and occupying about 60–70% of the frame, with the head larger than the body and the feet fully visible on a small display base unless the pose is dynamic.
- Pose and expression: {자세·표정} with clear silhouette separation, readable hands, bright eyes, and a face angle that makes the character personality immediately recognizable.
- Material treatment: {결} with smooth vinyl-like highlights, subtle clay grain, tiny painted edge variations, gentle sculpted seams, and softly rounded edges to emphasize miniature craftsmanship.
- Background: {배경} as a tiny scenic tabletop stage with layered miniature props that naturally match {캐릭터 컨셉}, such as a small pedestal, tiny accessory objects, molded floor tiles, paper cutout scenery, acrylic risers, or soft bokeh display lights.
- Color direction: {컬러 톤} applied consistently across character, props, base, and background accents, with one or two stronger accent points to guide the eye back to the figure.
- Framing: centered hero composition, square crop, controlled product-photography perspective, clear separation between subject and backdrop while still showing the miniature set context.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
- Character block: build {캐릭터 컨셉} as a stylized SD miniature with oversized head, compact torso, simplified limbs, expressive eyes, and a premium hobby-figure silhouette.
- Surface detail block: apply {결} using soft specular highlights, controlled reflections, faint brush-painted color variation, delicate sculpted seams, and small molded details that support the collectible look.
- Pose block: render {자세·표정} with readable gesture lines, stable balance, charming facial clarity, and a pose that works at small thumbnail size.
- Environment block: place {배경} as a miniature stage or tiny scenic set with shallow spatial layering, tabletop depth, small scale cues, and 2–4 supporting props related to the character concept.
- Base block: add a rounded display plinth, tiny platform, or diorama floor under the character, with subtle contact shadows, small decorative shapes, and optional miniature sticker-like icons that match the theme.
- Palette block: tint the entire scene with {컬러 톤}, blending pastel cream, soft peach, warm amber, pale mint, and a controlled accent color across the figure and set dressing.
- Output block: maintain a polished 3D toy-render finish, stylized smooth surfaces, hand-painted miniature charm, and realistic product-photo depth without turning the character into a real human.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: if text appears, keep it as tiny decorative packaging or base-label detail only, such as short Korean toy-label text like “미니 피규어”, “오늘의 친구”, or “컬렉션 01”; it should feel printed on the miniature set, not overlaid as a poster title.
- Color palette: use pastel cream, soft peach, warm amber, pale mint, and one accent color from {컬러 톤}; keep saturation moderate, highlights creamy, and shadows slightly warm.
- Prop styling: add small scale-appropriate accessories that match {캐릭터 컨셉}, with rounded toy-like forms, painted surfaces, subtle paper/cardboard texture, tiny fabric or felt accents, and soft translucent plastic details where appropriate.
- Border/shadow: soft studio shadow under the feet and display base, 8px y-offset, 18px blur, 12% opacity; subtle ambient occlusion around contact points and between stacked miniature elements.
- Finish: polished toy surface with gentle clay-like smoothing, warm handcrafted paint details, realistic micro-scratches on the display base, and controlled highlights that feel premium rather than cheap.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: 50mm lens look at f/4, front-facing studio product framing, slight downward angle of about 10° for a collectible-display feel.
- Lighting: softbox key light from upper-left at 45°, weak fill from front-right, and a faint rim light from behind to separate the figure from the background; add small practical glow accents in the miniature set if they match {배경}.
- Color grade: warm pastel grade with creamy highlights, amber mids, and slightly desaturated shadows; keep the overall temperature friendly, polished, and toy-catalog ready.
- Render quality: high-quality 3D render with soft global illumination, realistic contact shadows, shallow depth cues, fine bevels on props, and clean anti-aliased edges.

[6. MOOD]
Premium collectible figure art — like a boutique toy design shoot with a Pixar-meets-Funko presentation, charming miniature diorama details, and a warm handcrafted character-brand feeling.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: if tiny label text is included, render it as legible Korean such as “미니 피규어”, “오늘의 친구”, or “컬렉션 01”; avoid malformed characters.
- Composition invariants: keep the subject as a single centered SD miniature character with a clearly readable silhouette, large head-to-body ratio, compact body, and polished 3D toy finish.
- The image must preserve the miniature/figure impression; do not turn it into a full-realistic human portrait or a flat 2D cartoon.
- Preserve {캐릭터 컨셉}, {결}, {자세·표정}, {배경}, {컬러 톤}, and {비율} as the guiding inputs for character identity, surface finish, pose, setting, palette, and proportions.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]
- Fake official seals or certification marks
- Broken Korean characters
- Celebrity composites or unauthorized likeness

studio:prompts3:ours-609.content:
[INPUT]
- language: Korean
- output_size: 1024x1024

[1. PURPOSE]
3D product render for food, general goods, or beauty items, built as a square premium magazine-ad composition with a believable studio set. Suitable for ecommerce hero images, social ads, catalog thumbnails, launch teasers, and store-display visuals with rich material detail and realistic commercial styling.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Center the {제품} as the hero object, occupying about 58–65% of the frame, with enough surrounding context to show a real styled product set rather than a sterile mockup.
- Place the product slightly above exact center so the contact shadow, surface texture, small label card, and supporting elements can sit naturally around the base; keep the main silhouette fully visible and avoid awkward cropping.
- Background uses {배경} with a tactile studio surface such as coated paper, ceramic tile, frosted acrylic, brushed metal, warm stone, linen paper, or a softly curved cyclorama, depending on the product category.
- Build a balanced square layout with the hero product in front, 2–4 small contextual supporting elements around it: ingredient pieces for food, swatches and applicators for beauty, or functional accessories and packaging details for general goods.
- Add commercial packaging realism: readable front label areas, cap seams, folded box edges, embossed logo-like shapes, small stickers, nutrition or usage micro-copy, barcode block, price tag, and batch/date markings where appropriate.
- Apply {비율} as a strict square crop while maintaining a product-first composition with natural editorial depth.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
- Hero object layer: {제품} rendered as a crisp 3D object with realistic material response, gentle micro-reflections, clean edge definition, believable thickness, seams, caps, lids, folds, wrappers, transparent plastic, glass, paper, foil, ceramic, or cream textures as appropriate.
- Packaging/detail layer: include small realistic surface details such as a printed label, tiny barcode area, manufacturing/date stamp, dosage/weight line, scent/flavor note, refill mark, Korean product micro-copy, or a small retail price tag. Example Korean text may include: “NEW”, “오늘의 추천”, “₩18,000”, “공식몰 단독”, “50ml”, “120g”, “제조 2026.05”.
- Surface layer: place the product on a physical studio base with visible fine texture, soft dust-free imperfections, a grounded contact shadow, reflected color bounce, and subtle ambient occlusion beneath the product.
- Background layer: build {배경} as an editorial product set with soft gradients, layered panels, fabric folds, tiled seams, curved paper sweep, translucent acrylic riser, small plinth, or category-relevant props that enhance scale and realism.
- Supporting element layer: add natural, non-distracting props that match {제품}: fruit pieces, grains, cocoa, ice, herbs, spoon, cup, tray, cosmetic smear, brush, puff, mirror shard, folded towel, paper insert, ribbon, refill pouch, sample sachet, or small retail tag.
- Lighting layer: shape the object with {조명} so highlights stay dimensional and reveal material texture; preserve readable edges, soft shadows, and realistic reflection behavior.
- Finish layer: apply {결} to keep the overall render looking like a premium magazine product ad with high-end CGI realism, not toy-like plastic.
- Color layer: use {컬러 톤} as the main palette, combining one dominant product hue, one neutral surface tone, and one tasteful accent drawn from the product label, ingredient, or prop.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: allow small product-label and ad-card typography when it improves realism. Use Pretendard or Helvetica Neue Bold for Korean/English labels, with tiny supporting text in Regular or Medium; keep it sharp, well-spaced, and printed onto packaging, tags, or small cards.
- Suggested Korean text strings for rendered details: “신제품”, “베스트”, “하루 한 번”, “공식몰 단독”, “₩18,000”, “제조 2026.05”, “사용기한 2028.05”, “가볍게, 선명하게”, “오늘의 루틴”. Use only a few, placed naturally.
- Color palette: use the provided {컬러 톤} as the core palette, paired with muted studio neutrals such as #F4F0E8, #E7E1D6, #D9D2C7, #2B2B2B, and one product accent color.
- Border/shadow: avoid a graphic frame; use layered realistic shadows, soft contact shadow with 4px y-offset, 14px blur, about 16% opacity, and faint ambient occlusion around the base, plus natural reflections on glossy or transparent materials.
- Material fidelity: make paper labels slightly fibrous, glass subtly thick at edges, plastic caps lightly satin, metal foils brushed or crinkled, creams and liquids viscous, and food surfaces varied rather than perfectly smooth.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: studio product photography look, like a Phase One IQ4 with an 80mm macro lens at f/8, rendered in Octane / Cinema 4D realism.
- Lighting: soft multi-light studio setup, key light from upper-left at 45°, gentle fill from front-right, and a subtle rim light to separate the product from the background; include realistic bounce light from nearby props and surface color.
- Color grade: premium luxury grading with product signature colors preserved, neutral highlights, slightly warm off-white studio tones, rich but controlled contrast, and tactile texture visibility.

[6. MOOD]
Premium studio product editorial — Apple launch visual meets Daniel Wellington catalog polish, with the tactile richness of a high-end Korean lifestyle magazine product spread.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: if Korean text appears on labels, tags, stickers, captions, or price cards, it must be clean and legible, for example “신제품”, “오늘의 추천”, “공식몰 단독”, “₩18,000”, “제조 2026.05”, “50ml”, “120g”.
- Keep the product anatomy faithful to the source category: realistic proportions, clean geometry, correct cap/lid thickness, believable packaging seams, no warped edges, no melted surfaces, and no impossible material behavior.
- Supporting props must match the product category and scale; they should add realism, retail context, and tactile richness while keeping {제품} as the clear hero.
- Preserve the {컬러 톤}, {조명}, {결}, {배경}, and {비율} directives as the dominant art direction.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]
- Fake official seals / certifications
- Broken Korean characters

studio:prompts3:ours-608.content:
[INPUT]
- language: Korean
- output_size: 1024x1536

[1. PURPOSE]
Logo guideline sheet / brand identity reference page for a café or retail brand, presented as a realistic A4 portrait brand manual page with 6 logo variations, usage rules, color chips, scale notes, and production-ready identity details.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Page format: A4 vertical poster layout, with a structured editorial grid, visible page hierarchy, and realistic brand-manual annotations.
- Main composition: top title zone, central 6-variation grid, and bottom usage-guide zone stacked vertically, with a slim footer strip containing version/date/page metadata.
- {브랜드명·로고} should be the visual center of the sheet, supported by small production details such as section numbers, alignment ticks, color swatches, clear-space indicators, and caption labels.
- {레이아웃} must feel like a polished brand deck page from Pentagram / B&B style identity guidelines, with precise alignment, disciplined spacing, and a real design-system reference look.
- Background treatment: premium warm off-white paper surface with very subtle fiber grain, faint print texture, and crisp ink rendering, like a professionally printed guideline sheet photographed straight-on.
- Add realistic manual-page details: small header code “BRAND MANUAL 01”, date label “2026.05”, version text “VER. 1.0”, footer page number “p.01”, and tiny production notes in Korean.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
- Header area (top 12-15%): set a compact title block introducing the brand guide sheet, with {브랜드명·로고} displayed as the primary identity mark.
- Include title text “로고 가이드 시트”, a smaller subtitle “브랜드 아이덴티티 기준표”, a tiny issue/date line “2026.05 / VER. 1.0”, and a right-aligned micro label “BRAND MANUAL 01”.
- Main grid area (middle 58-62%): place the {6가지 variation} in a 2-column by 3-row grid, each version in its own measured cell with consistent padding, fine divider lines, and tiny labels beneath.
- Add subtle measurement marks around the grid: small baseline ticks, 1x clear-space notes, hairline cross references, and compact Korean captions that make the page feel like an actual design specification.
- Variation 01: hero/main signature version, largest and most visually emphasized; keep the exact wordmark proportions clean and centered, label it “01 메인 시그니처”.
- Variation 02: horizontal lockup, place the symbol and English wordmark side by side on one baseline, aligned with clear padding, label it “02 가로 조합”.
- Variation 03: vertical lockup, place the English wordmark below the symbol, stacked with tighter vertical rhythm, label it “03 세로 조합”.
- Variation 04: symbol-only mark, isolated in a specification cell with tiny clear-space guide lines and label “04 심볼 단독”.
- Variation 05: monochrome black version, rendered in solid charcoal-black ink with a small ink note “K 100 / Charcoal”, label it “05 단색 블랙”.
- Variation 06: monochrome white version, shown on a dark charcoal patch so the form is legible and contrast is obvious, label it “06 반전형 화이트”.
- Usage guide area (bottom 18-20%): place {사용 가이드} as a concise checklist with clear ✓ / ✗ visual rules and small explanatory labels.
- Include three compact usage examples: “✓ 흰 배경”, “✓ 다크 배경”, “✗ 회전·왜곡 금지”, using small thumbnail boxes and fine rule lines.
- Add a color specification strip with “컬러” label, 3-4 swatches including the brand signature color from {컬러 톤}, warm off-white, charcoal, and black, each with small hex-style text.
- Keep {비율} expressed as a clean specification note in the footer area, paired with tiny scale marks such as “기준 비율 1:1 / 최소 사용폭 18mm”.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: use Pretendard or Noto Sans KR for Korean UI text, medium and regular weights; use a clean geometric sans for English labels, with small sizes around 10-18pt equivalent.
- Titles and labels should be crisp, highly legible, evenly tracked, and editorial, with subtle typographic hierarchy rather than decorative flourish.
- Color palette: white #FFFFFF, warm off-white #F5F2EC, charcoal #2B2B2B, black #111111, and a single brand signature color from {컬러 톤}.
- Keep all rules, label lines, separators, scale marks, and swatch outlines thin and precise, using 1-2px strokes.
- Shadow treatment: use a very soft neutral contact shadow around the sheet edge and tiny printed-ink depth only, 2px y-offset, 6px blur, 8% opacity for separation.
- Add realistic print-design details such as tiny crop-like reference ticks, micro captions, color chips, and footer metadata while keeping the guide sheet professional and readable.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: front-on flat graphic layout, equivalent to a 50mm standard editorial framing with no perspective distortion.
- Lighting: evenly lit studio setup, diffuse overhead softbox feel, soft paper-edge shadow, no glare, no reflections.
- Color grade: clean premium brand-manual grade with neutral whites, controlled charcoal blacks, subtle warm paper tone, and restrained accent color usage.
- Rendering style: realistic printed identity sheet with crisp vector logo marks, sharp Korean typography, visible but subtle paper grain, and tactile ink-on-paper clarity.

[6. MOOD]
Premium identity system page — like a Pentagram brand guideline spread or a refined B&B studio presentation board, enriched with real-world manual details, production notes, swatches, and precise specification graphics.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: 반드시 정확히 보일 문자열: “로고 가이드 시트”, “브랜드 아이덴티티 기준표”, “사용 가이드”, “레이아웃”, “컬러”, “비율”, “✓ 흰 배경·다크 배경 / ✗ 회전·왜곡·컬러 변경 금지”.
- Additional visible micro text should be accurate and compact: “2026.05”, “VER. 1.0”, “BRAND MANUAL 01”, “p.01”, “01 메인 시그니처”, “02 가로 조합”, “03 세로 조합”, “04 심볼 단독”, “05 단색 블랙”, “06 반전형 화이트”.
- English text accuracy: the logo text and variation labels must remain crisp, clean, and properly spelled.
- Layout invariants: exactly 6 logo variations must be shown, with clear separation between each cell and consistent alignment across the grid.
- Keep the logo forms anatomically clean as vector-style marks, with no broken strokes or warped geometry.
- Preserve all placeholder-driven content exactly: {브랜드명·로고}, {6가지 variation}, {사용 가이드}, {레이아웃}, {컬러 톤}, {비율}.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]

- Broken Korean characters

[1. PURPOSE]
Brand color guide poster for a café or small brand, designed as a realistic editorial brand manual page with palette chips, HEX info, usage examples, version details, and practical application notes.
Vertical A4-style reference sheet for internal branding, client presentation, print proofing, or social sharing, with the feel of a real agency-delivered identity guideline page.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Overall format: tall A4 portrait layout, structured like a premium brand guideline sheet with clear hierarchy, document metadata, strong grid alignment, and realistic print-design details.
- Main hero zone: left side large color block occupying about 34% of the width, featuring the strongest brand color from {컬러 팔레트} as the anchor, with a paper-label overlay containing color specs.
- Right side: multi-row chip grid for the remaining palette, each chip paired with concise color data from {컬러 정보}, small contrast notes, and role labels such as PRIMARY, SUPPORT, ACCENT, NEUTRAL.
- Bottom zone: usage example area spanning the full width, showing {사용 예시} as a realistic application strip: café cup sleeve, menu corner, sticker label, loyalty card, shopping bag tag, or social profile swatch preview depending on the brand context.
- Margin and spacing: professional editorial margins with active header, footer, page number, version label, and small annotation marks; even gutters between modules, aligned to a 12-column editorial grid.
- Background treatment: matte off-white paper surface with subtle fiber texture, faint crop marks, light registration dots, and printed-ink depth so the guide feels like a photographed real brand manual sheet.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
1. Header strip at the top: set {브랜드명} in a restrained brand-manual title style, centered or slightly left-aligned, with thin divider lines, compact subtitle behavior, and realistic metadata text such as "BRAND COLOR GUIDE", "VOL.01", "2026.05", "내부 공유용".
2. Hero color block on the left: render the largest swatch as a solid matte field, with the color name, HEX, RGB, and CMYK values placed in a neat overlay box or adjacent label stack; add a small label reading "PRIMARY COLOR" and a short Korean note like "가장 먼저 기억되는 대표 컬러".
3. Palette grid on the right: arrange the remaining colors from {컬러 팔레트} in orderly chips, 2–4 rows depending on count, each chip showing {컬러 정보} in small technical typography; include small labels such as "서브 컬러", "포인트 컬러", "배경 컬러", "텍스트 컬러" where appropriate.
4. Tone system band: visually separate the main brand color, supporting colors, accent colors, and grayscale ladder so the palette reads like a professional manual; add tint steps such as 100 / 80 / 60 / 40 / 20 and a short descriptor using {컬러 톤}.
5. Usage example panel at the bottom: place {사용 예시} as a realistic mockup strip with presentation framing, showing the palette applied to actual branded materials; include small captions like "컵 슬리브", "메뉴 헤더", "스티커", "SNS 카드", "포장 라벨".
6. Layout label area: include {레이아웃} as an explanatory module with simple spacing diagrams, arrows, baseline marks, and proportion notes; add practical labels such as "로고 주변 여백", "텍스트 대비", "배경 적용 예시".
7. Tone note area: present {컬러 톤} as a short descriptor line in the same editorial system, supported by a small editorial note such as "따뜻한 중성 톤을 기준으로 계절감 있게 확장".
8. Size note: show {비율} as a compact technical footer note, aligned with the overall manual aesthetic; add document details such as "PAGE 01", "A4 PORTRAIT", "CMYK PRINT CHECK", "담당: 브랜드팀".

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: use Pretendard or Noto Sans KR for Korean UI text, with Bold 700 for headings and Regular 400 for technical labels; size hints 34–42px for title, 16–22px for labels, 12–14px for specs, and 9–11px for tiny metadata and captions.
- Color palette: use {컬러 팔레트} as the source palette, with neutral supports in off-white #F4F1EA, charcoal #2B2B2B, cool gray #B8B8B8, and light grid gray #E5E2DB.
- Border/shadow: use thin 1px charcoal rules, practical card borders, hairline dividers, small printed crop marks, and very soft drop shadows on mockup elements, around 4px y-offset, 10px blur, 12% opacity.
- Technical labels: make HEX, RGB, and CMYK values look like a real brand manual with tight tracking, small caps feel, crisp alignment, tabular numerals, and consistent separators.
- Realistic document details: include version code, date label, page number, small QR-placeholder box or barcode-like asset code area, proofing notes, and caption text in Korean without introducing new placeholders.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: product-photography editorial look, simulated with a 50mm lens at f/5.6 for the usage mockup area, plus a flat-lay precision feel for the palette grid.
- Lighting: soft diffuse studio light from upper-left at about 45°, with faint fill from right; natural paper shadow along the lower edge, gentle ink texture, and realistic depth on layered mockup cards.
- Color grade: clean neutral paper tone with accurate saturated swatches, balanced whites, precise dark text, and slight warm-gray paper cast.
- Material feel: matte premium paper, printed ink absorption, slight page curl at one corner, crisp vector-like typography, and subtle tactile differences between swatches, labels, and mockup cards.

[6. MOOD]
Premium brand guideline page — a Pantone / identity manual spread with the clarity of a modern agency presentation and the refined warmth of a real café or small-brand design system. It should feel like a finished client handoff sheet photographed for a portfolio, not a blank template.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: 반드시 정확히 보여야 하는 문구: "브랜드명", "컬러 팔레트", "컬러 정보", "사용 예시", "레이아웃", "컬러 톤", "비율".
- Also render short Korean guide labels clearly, for example: "대표 컬러", "서브 컬러", "포인트 컬러", "배경 적용", "텍스트 대비", "브랜드 컬러 가이드", "2026.05", "PAGE 01".
- Every color value in HEX, RGB, and CMYK must be rendered clearly and consistently formatted.
- Keep all blocks aligned to a strict grid; swatches must be cleanly separated and visually distinct.
- Maintain portrait A4 composition with a large left hero swatch, right-side palette grid, and bottom usage example band.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]

- Broken Korean characters
- Celebrity composites / unauthorized likeness

Mobile app loading screen still frame, static UI illustration for an animation stop-frame presentation. Friendly lifestyle app loading visual with realistic product details, app-store preview polish, and frozen micro-animation cues.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Create a vertical 9:16 mobile loading screen mockup for {앱명}, designed as a believable in-app transition page rather than a blank splash screen.
- Center a rounded mobile UI canvas inside the frame, filling most of the 1024x1536 composition while keeping the status bar, header, loading card, tip module, and footer readable.
- Background should be {배경스타일}, with soft texture, gentle dot rhythm, or faint abstract shapes that support the UI without overpowering the main loading indicator.
- Arrange the hierarchy from top to bottom: phone status bar, app header/logo, main loading animation card, message/progress section, helpful tip card, version/footer microcopy.
- All visible UI copy must be guided by {앱명}, {앱설명}, {로딩장면}, {로딩메시지}, {진행률}, {팁문구}, {날짜위치}, {버전정보}, and {브랜드컬러}.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
- Status bar area (top 5%): render a realistic mobile status bar with time “09:41”, cellular/Wi‑Fi/battery icons, and soft screen-safe spacing.
- App header area (top 13%): place a small rounded app icon, {앱명} as the primary app label, and {앱설명} as a compact subtitle; include {날짜위치} as a small pill-shaped context label on the right or beneath the subtitle.
- Main loading card (middle 42%): create a lifted rounded card containing {로딩장면}; show a circular progress ring with segmented amber/brand-color ticks, a friendly character illustration frozen mid-motion, tiny step marks, coffee steam, sleep bubble, or waiting dots that imply animation frames in one still image.
- Message block (lower-middle 16%): set {로딩메시지} clearly under the loading motif, with {진행률} displayed as smaller supporting progress text; include a slim progress bar with softly rounded ends and a small percentage marker.
- Tip module (lower 14%): add a compact informational card labeled “오늘의 팁” containing {팁문구}, plus tiny UI chips such as “동기화 중”, “안전 연결”, or “추천 준비”.
- Footer area (bottom 8%): show {버전정보}, a small “도움말” link, “개인정보” microcopy, and tiny decorative app-style dots/icons aligned with the overall UI system.
- Color system layer: apply {브랜드컬러} to the app icon, progress ring, active chips, and character accents; keep white and warm off-white as the base with amber used for warmth and friendliness.
- Final polish: preserve a stop-frame animation feel through frozen motion ticks, segmented ring accents, small pose ghosts inside the illustration card, and crisp vector-like UI edges.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: use Pretendard or Noto Sans KR for all UI text, semibold for {앱명} and {로딩메시지}, medium for labels/chips, regular for progress, footer, and helper text; maintain real app-like spacing and baseline alignment.
- Color palette: white #FFFFFF and warm off-white #FFF8EF as the base, warm amber #F4B66A as the accent, soft brand color from {브랜드컬러}, muted gray #6B7280 for secondary text, light gray #EEF2F7 for dividers and inactive progress segments.
- Border/shadow: use subtle 1px soft gray outlines on cards and panels, with a gentle drop shadow of 0px 8px 24px at 12% opacity to lift the main loading card from the screen.
- Rounded geometry: keep cards around 18–28px radius, chips around 999px radius, app icon around 20px radius, with crisp UI edges and tactile product-design depth.
- Include realistic small interface details: tappable-looking chips, tiny icon buttons, micro dividers, progress numerals, and footer links, all visually consistent with a polished Korean lifestyle app.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: front-facing UI mockup look, as if captured with a 50mm standard lens at f/5.6 in a studio product shot, straight-on and distortion-free.
- Lighting: soft diffused studio light from the upper-left with an even fill from the right, producing a clean screen-like glow and gentle card shadows.
- Color grade: bright white with warm amber accents and softened pastel brand tones, maintaining a fresh app-store preview aesthetic with realistic product mockup finish.

[6. MOOD]
Friendly premium lifestyle app loading screen — polished mobile product mockup feel, similar to a clean wellness, habit, or daily-life app onboarding visual with a gentle editorial UI finish and believable in-app microcopy.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: the following strings must appear exactly as written when defaults are used: “OUR APP”, “친근 라이프 앱”, “잠시만 기다려주세요... ☕”, “68% 완료”, “오늘의 팁”, “동기화 중”, “안전 연결”, “추천 준비”, “v2.4.7”.
- Render all Korean UI text clearly and neatly, including progress percentage, footer links, date/location label, and chip labels; no broken Korean characters or garbled punctuation.
- The loading motif must read as a still-frame animation stop-capture: circular progress + character illustration + frozen motion cues integrated into one coherent mobile UI.
- Maintain a vertical 9:16 mobile app-screen composition with stable alignment, realistic app interface hierarchy, and readable text at 1024x1536.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]

- Broken Korean characters or garbled UI text
- Celebrity composites or recognizable real-person likenesses
- Sexualized or revealing content

[1. PURPOSE]
Mobile app splash / launch screen design for a Korean app, optimized for first-open branding, quick recognition, and a polished real-product presentation.
Create a contemporary Korean startup screen with a centered {앱·로고}, memorable short tagline, brand gradient background, subtle launch-state details, and refined app metadata that feels ready for an actual App Store / Play Store release.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Main subject: {앱·로고} placed at the visual center, occupying about 22–28% of the frame width, rendered as a crisp app icon or logo mark with precise edges and premium finish.
- Supporting copy: {비주얼} positioned directly below the logo, aligned center, using a compact one- or two-line layout if needed; keep it clear enough to read at mobile-screen scale.
- App launch details: add small realistic splash-screen microcopy such as “시작하는 중”, “v2.4.7”, “© 2026 {앱·로고}”, and a tiny loading dot row or short progress indicator near the lower center.
- Background treatment: {배경} with soft geometric accents, faint brand-symbol patterns, translucent gradient blobs, or lightly layered interface-inspired shapes that support the centered logo.
- Color direction: {컬러 톤} with a premium, app-store-ready finish, using one distinct brand accent and carefully balanced neutrals.
- Framing: vertical mobile composition matching {비율} for 1024x1536 output, straight-on splash-screen layout with natural safe-area awareness at the top and bottom.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
- Top area: include a very subtle phone-safe-area feeling, such as a faint status-bar zone or barely visible top breathing band, without turning the image into a full app UI screen.
- Hero area: place {앱·로고} as the focal point in the center with polished vector-like sharpness, balanced spacing, and a believable app-launch scale.
- Brand identity stack: under the logo, render {비주얼} in Korean, then add one small secondary line such as “오늘을 더 쉽게 시작하세요” or “당신의 일상을 연결합니다” if it fits {컨셉}.
- Launch-state area: near the lower third, add tiny Korean microcopy “시작하는 중” with three animated-style dots, a slim soft progress line, or a quiet loading pulse.
- Footer metadata: at the bottom safe area, include a small version label like “v2.4.7”, a short privacy or company line like “개인정보 보호 · 안전한 연결”, and “© 2026 {앱·로고}”.
- Background layer: build {배경} as a soft radial gradient, layered two-tone blend, or refined brand field with faint icons, abstract cards, rounded capsules, light particles, or translucent app-symbol silhouettes.
- Brand tone: apply {컨셉} through color temperature, spacing density, typography mood, icon geometry, and the rhythm of background elements so the screen feels like a complete Korean mobile brand system.
- Final polish: use the look of a real Korean app splash screen with immediate logo recognition, readable Korean microcopy, tactile digital surfaces, and launch-screen credibility.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: clean sans-serif system such as Pretendard or Noto Sans KR; medium to semi-bold for the tagline, 20–36px equivalent for visible copy, 10–14px equivalent for footer metadata, with tight but readable letter spacing.
- Color palette: use {컬러 톤} as the main palette, with off-white, charcoal, warm gray, or soft dark-mode neutrals if needed; accents should feel brand-led and consistent across logo, loading details, and decorative shapes.
- Logo treatment: keep {앱·로고} crisp and intentional, with a believable app-icon radius, subtle depth, or matte shadow if appropriate to {컨셉}; the mark must remain readable and not melt into the background.
- Border/shadow: if shadow is used, make it modern and soft, e.g. 0–6px y-offset, 12–20px blur, 8–15% opacity; avoid heavy bevels or old-fashioned glossy effects.
- Surface quality: matte, clean, slightly tactile digital finish with delicate gradient depth, soft noise only if it improves realism, and carefully layered translucent accents.
- Decorative system: use small Korean-app-style details such as rounded capsules, faint map-pin/calendar/chat/card icons, small brand particles, or abstract UI fragments that make the splash feel produced by a real design team.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: digital product-style flat graphic composition, effectively a straight-on orthographic layout with no lens distortion; if rendered as a mockup, use a 50mm equivalent front-facing setup.
- Lighting: even studio-style illumination with a gentle upper-left emphasis and very mild fill from the opposite side; keep contrast controlled and screen-friendly.
- Color grade: Toss / 당근 / 카카오-inspired modern app tone, with crisp whites, stable neutrals, soft gradients, and one distinct brand accent; keep saturation refined and commercially polished.
- Rendering fidelity: high-resolution mobile UI artwork with sharp vector edges, clean Korean glyph rendering, realistic safe-area spacing, and subtle antialiasing suitable for a launch screen.

[6. MOOD]
Premium Korean mobile app launch screen — Toss and Kakao-style startup clarity with a warm, contemporary brand feel, enriched by real launch metadata, subtle motion cues, and polished first-open credibility.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: include “앱 스플래시·시작 화면”, “천천히, 함께”, “시작하는 중”, “오늘을 더 쉽게 시작하세요”, “v2.4.7”, “개인정보 보호 · 안전한 연결”.
- All on-image Korean and English text must be clean, correctly spelled, and fully legible.
- Composition invariant: centered {앱·로고} hero, small {비주얼} tagline below, refined brand background, subtle loading/footer details, vertical mobile splash layout.
- Keep all text hierarchy believable for a real app launch screen: logo first, tagline second, launch-state and metadata third.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]
- Fake official seals / certifications
- Broken Korean characters
- Celebrity composites / unauthorized likeness

5. Social proof details: add a small view-bait strip such as "끝까지 보면 반전" or "마지막 한입 주의", plus tiny like/comment/share icon hints that read as graphic UI elements rather than official platform branding.
6. Frame treatment: use a tight poster crop with thick visual weight around the center, layered typography, realistic shadows under the food, and saturated foreground details so the cover feels loud, urgent, and believable.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: use Pretendard ExtraBold or Noto Sans KR Black for the main hook, with 72–110px-equivalent size, slightly condensed spacing, bold black stroke, and off-white/yellow fill for maximum mobile readability.
- Secondary text: use Noto Sans KR SemiBold or Pretendard Bold, 28–40px-equivalent size, clean and compact, placed inside sticker labels, rounded capsules, or torn-paper caption strips.
- Color palette: follow {컬러 톤} with saturated red #E53935, yellow #FFD400, black #111111, spicy orange #FF6B00, and off-white highlight #FFF6E8 if needed.
- Border/shadow: apply a hard comic-style outer stroke on text, plus a subtle drop shadow at 4px y-offset, 10px blur, 20% opacity for separation; use glossy highlights and rim light on food edges.
- Layout density: include enough real mukbang context to feel lived-in: sauce bowl, napkin, condensation on cup, table reflections, tiny crumbs, chopstick marks, and heat steam, while keeping the key hook and face instantly legible.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: Canon EOS R5 with RF 50mm f/1.2 at an f/2.0 look for portrait-style framing, or RF 85mm f/1.8 for a tighter social-media poster crop.
- Lighting: bright frontal key light with slight top-left fill, warm rim light from behind the food, crisp specular highlights on sauce and steam, and controlled contrast to emphasize the reaction face.
- Color grade: saturated street-food poster grade with warm reds, vivid yellows, deep blacks, high clarity, realistic skin texture, and glossy food detail for a punchy reel-cover finish.
- Texture realism: show believable pores, fabric folds, reflections on plastic cup lids, wet sauce thickness, steam layering, and table surface grain so the design feels like a photographed mukbang cover enhanced with graphics.

[6. MOOD]
High-energy Korean food challenge poster — like a glossy YouTube Shorts / Instagram Reels thumbnail with a chaotic mukbang street-food feel, dramatic spicy-food tension, playful challenge stickers, and immediate "tap to watch" urgency.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: 반드시 정확히 보여야 하는 문구: "매운맛 챌린지 — 끝까지 갈까?"
- Also render short supporting Korean text clearly where appropriate: "성공률 3%", "30초 도전", "마지막 한입 주의", "#먹방챌린지", "@mukbang_now", "2026.05.01".
- Set the main cover line in Korean using {릴스 카피}, and ensure {챌린지 종류}, {컨셉·테마}, {모델 자세·표정}, {비주얼·소품}, {컬러 톤}, {비율} remain visually reflected in the final design.
- Text rendering must keep Korean characters clean, bold, and fully legible at mobile thumbnail scale.
- Food reaction and props must look physically plausible and naturally placed; no warped utensils, no distorted cups, no extra fingers if hands are visible.

K-pop/trend-dance challenge visual with bold headline copy, authentic short-form UI details, and high-impact movement frozen in a poster-like frame.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Main subject placement: {모델 자세·표정} occupies the center 60% of the frame, with the body angled slightly in a dynamic diagonal to create motion energy and a clear dance silhouette.
- Header/copy area: {릴스 카피} sits in the upper third or center-left depending on pose, large enough to remain readable at thumbnail size, with supporting micro-copy below it.
- Background treatment: {비주얼·소품} with a real performance-like environment such as a practice studio, rooftop night set, or small stage, including neon accents, floor reflections, light stands, cable details, and atmospheric haze.
- Framing direction: portrait 9:16 cover composition with strong silhouette separation, layered depth, readable title placement, and natural social-cover framing.
- Theme integration: {챌린지 종류} and {컨셉·테마} should feel like a real weekly challenge reel posted by an active dance account, not a generic dance poster.
- Palette direction: {컬러 톤} should dominate the full frame with high contrast between subject, text, background, stickers, and UI-like details.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
1) Background layer — Build a dark stage-like, rooftop, or dance-practice room environment with subtle depth, neon pink and cyan edge accents, reflective flooring, practical LED tubes, speaker boxes, mirror/glass hints, and a few believable set details.
2) Subject layer — Render {모델 자세·표정} as a frozen action pose with crisp limb separation, sharp outfit detail, natural fabric folds, sneakers grounded on the floor, hair motion, and a confident performance expression.
3) Motion accents — Add subtle streaks, glow trails, light fragments, rhythm marks, or beat-line graphics around the moving limbs to suggest dance energy without obscuring the body.
4) Text layer — Place {릴스 카피} in bold, highly legible Korean typography with strong contrast, positioned to avoid covering the face or key pose lines.
5) Social cover details — Add a small Instagram/Reels-style handle such as "@dance.weekly", a short Korean tag line like "오늘의 포인트 안무", hashtag-like text such as "#댄스챌린지 #릴스커버", a tiny save/share/heart icon row, and a small date label such as "2026.05.01 FRI".
6) Prop / set layer — Include {비주얼·소품} elements such as stage lights, floor reflections, rooftop railing cues, portable speaker, rehearsal tape marks, LED bars, or glossy floor scuffs, keeping them integrated with the scene.
7) Finish layer — Keep the full composition polished like a real short-form social cover image, with crisp thumbnail readability, layered poster depth, and authentic creator-channel energy.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: Pretendard ExtraBold or Noto Sans KR Black for the headline, 72–120px visual scale, tight but readable line spacing, slightly condensed tracking for impact.
- Supporting text: Use smaller Korean micro-copy in Pretendard SemiBold / Medium, including "DAY 1", "15초 포인트 안무", "저장하고 따라하기", and a channel handle such as "@dance.weekly".
- Color palette: use {컬러 톤} with specific anchors such as deep charcoal #101114, neon pink #FF2DAA, cyan #28D7FF, and white #F7F7F7.
- Border/shadow: add a soft but decisive drop shadow under the text, around 4px y-offset, 12px blur, 18% opacity, plus faint outer glow in neon accents.
- Graphic accents: Add small sticker-like labels, beat-count numbers "5·6·7·8", arrow marks near the arms or feet, and a compact bottom tag bar reading "WEEKLY CHALLENGE".

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: 35mm or 50mm digital editorial portrait look, f/2.8 equivalent, slight wide-angle energy without distortion, captured like a performance promo still.
- Lighting: concert-style key light from upper-left at 45°, neon rim light from right, subtle floor bounce fill, with controlled highlights on hair and outfit edges.
- Color grade: dark base with neon pink and cyan highlights, high contrast, slightly crushed blacks, crisp whites, and a polished music-show poster finish.
- Texture realism: show realistic skin texture, hair strands, fabric weave, sneaker material, floor shine, haze in light beams, and small imperfections from a real shooting location.

- Pose/layout invariants: the subject must read clearly as a dance challenge pose, with the body frozen in a dynamic motion moment, and the headline must remain legible at small reel-cover size.
- Keep the overall frame aligned to a vertical 9:16 social cover look with strong central focus and no text obstruction over the face.
- Preserve the selected {챌린지 종류}, {컨셉·테마}, {모델 자세·표정}, {릴스 카피}, {비주얼·소품}, {컬러 톤}, and {비율} exactly as the controlling prompt variables.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]

- Spacing and framing: cards evenly separated with consistent gutters, slight rotation variation only enough to feel naturally hand-arranged, but the overall grid remains tidy and aligned for a professional catalog look.
- Use {사장·매장}, {명함 결}, {QR 종류}, {컬러 톤}, {레이아웃}, {비율} as the configurable content anchors.
- Add realistic print details: paper grain, slight card thickness, crisp rounded corners, subtle edge shadows, tiny registration marks, small divider lines, micro icons for phone / map / Instagram / blog / payment.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
1. Top-left card cluster: one primary business card face showing the owner and store identity with strong Korean hierarchy, including owner name, shop name, title, phone number, address line, Instagram handle, and business hours.
2. Top-right card cluster: one business card back emphasizing QR use, with a large centered QR code, small label text such as “인스타·블로그 바로가기”, and short helper copy below the code.
3. Bottom-left card cluster: alternate business card variation with the same visual system, demonstrating consistency across the package through matching typography, accent color, divider rules, and icon set.
4. Bottom-right card cluster: QR-focused card variation with distinct QR purpose labeling, using four small QR card designs for “인스타·블로그”, “카카오톡 채널”, “결제”, and “단골 적립”.
5. Overall collage treatment: all 8 pieces should feel like a coordinated branding set, with print-ready sharp edges, realistic paper thickness, fine ink texture, and subtle shadow separation from the background.
6. Text content placement: integrate {사장·매장}, {명함 결}, and {QR 종류} so the package reads as a complete owner-brand kit rather than isolated samples.
7. Include a small package label strip near the layout reading “명함 4장 + QR 4장” and a tiny production-note style caption like “PRINT READY · LOCAL BRAND KIT · VOL.01”.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: Pretendard and Noto Sans KR for clean Korean sans-serif hierarchy, medium to semibold weights, title text around 26–34px equivalent, supporting labels 14–18px equivalent, micro contact text 9–12px equivalent but still legible.
- Color palette: cream #F4ECDD, charcoal #2F2F2F, warm beige #D8C6B3, muted brand accent from {컬러 톤}; use accent color for QR labels, dividers, small stickers, and tiny icon marks.
- Border/shadow: soft drop shadow with 4px y-offset, 14px blur, 16% opacity; thin paper-edge definition for each card, realistic matte card stock edges, slight rounded-corner highlights.
- Graphic details: fine line dividers, small rounded QR labels, tiny “SCAN ME” bilingual tag, dotted guide marks, subtle café receipt typography, and understated decorative corner marks that make the kit feel printed and real.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: overhead flat lay look, 50mm equivalent on a high-resolution studio setup, crisp print detail and controlled perspective.
- Lighting: diffused softbox from upper-left with gentle fill from right, controlled shadow falloff, natural paper texture visible, evenly exposed with believable contact shadows under every card.
- Color grade: warm cream + charcoal + muted signature accent, slightly desaturated retail stationery catalog tone with realistic ink-on-paper contrast.
- Rendering quality: ultra-sharp Korean typography, crisp QR-code geometry, tactile matte paper, natural tabletop depth, premium branding portfolio realism.

Premium small-business stationery catalog spread — like a refined Korean local-brand identity mockup seen in a high-end branding portfolio, but with lived-in shop-owner details, practical QR use cases, and friendly neighborhood-store warmth.

- Color system zone (mid-upper 20%): display swatches for {컬러 가이드} as rectangular chips with hex labels, usage ratio labels, CMYK/RGB micro text, and “배경 / 포인트 / 텍스트” application tags beneath each chip.
- Typography zone (mid-lower 20%): show {타이포} as specimen lines, with Korean and English sample text set in separated rows, visible size hierarchy, tracking notes, and {샘플 문구} as the specimen copy.
- Usage rules zone (lower 18%): present {로고 사용 규칙} as a concise do/don’t panel using check and cross marks, including small logo placement examples on cup sleeve, sticker, receipt header, and Instagram profile mockup tiles.
- Layout reference zone (bottom 16%): show {레이아웃} with miniature module previews, sample annotations, approval stamp-style text from {승인 정보}, document contact line, QR-placeholder square, and a clean footer rule to complete the one-page manual.

- Center the main product cluster so the diffuser bottle occupies about 45% of the frame, with the small perfume box placed slightly forward-right to create depth and a believable retail bundle.
- Use {매장·시그니처 향} as the conceptual product identity, letting the label and package hierarchy feel like a refined store scent line with a clear fragrance name, notes, volume, batch code, and boutique location.

- Place the products on {배경}, such as marble, warm wood, limestone, or a boutique counter surface, with natural material grain, soft reflections, and tactile realism.
- Add subtle lifestyle retail details around the package: dried eucalyptus or cotton flower stem, folded off-white receipt card, small barcode sticker area on the box side, thin ribbon or paper belly band, and a tiny price / product information card.

- Hero product zone (center 45%): render the diffuser bottle as the tallest element, with crisp glass edges, clear or lightly tinted liquid, 5–7 matte black or natural reed sticks, a premium front label, and a small neck tag tied with thin cotton string.
- Secondary package zone (lower-right 25%): place the small perfume box slightly angled at 10–15 degrees, close enough to feel bundled but separated enough to show the front panel, side barcode strip, and top flap seam.
- Label clarity zone (front-facing surfaces): place {라벨 정보} on the bottle and box with clean alignment; include readable Korean product hierarchy such as brand/store name, scent name, scent notes, volume, batch number, and location.
- Retail information zone (lower-left or near product base): include a small matching card with concise Korean details: “₩32,000”, “100ml”, “ROOM DIFFUSER”, “BATCH 0526”, “서울 성수점”, and a tiny QR-style square or barcode block for realism.
- Surface and backdrop zone (full frame): combine {배경} with a premium studio tabletop look; include believable stone/wood texture, contact shadows beneath each object, and slight paper fiber texture on labels and box surfaces.
- Color balance zone (entire composition): let {컬러 톤} define the palette across packaging, label accents, botanical props, ribbon/string, and background harmony.
- Type hierarchy zone (label area): use {타이포} for the packaging text structure, with clear spacing between brand name, scent name, support copy, volume, and batch details.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: use an elegant serif pairing such as Noto Serif KR or Nanum Myeongjo for the main Korean text, with a refined English serif companion; medium-to-light weight, 16–28 px label scale, tight but breathable tracking.
- Add realistic label text blocks in Korean and English: “오늘의 카페 — Coffee Bloom”, “매장 시그니처 향”, “향 이름”, “작은 카피”, “매장 위치”, “100ml / 3.4 fl. oz.”, “TOP: 베르가못”, “MID: 커피 플라워”, “BASE: 머스크 우드”.
- Color palette: base the scene on {컬러 톤}, plus off-white paper tones, muted stone gray, warm wood, translucent amber liquid, and restrained metallic gold accents; keep black text soft charcoal rather than pure black.
- Packaging finish: show matte paper box texture, slight embossing or debossed line detail, a thin gold foil rule, clean folded box edges, a realistic barcode panel, small manufacturing-style text, and subtle label adhesive edges.
- Border/shadow: add a soft drop shadow with 4px y-offset, 14px blur, 15% opacity; no hard outline, no neon edge glow.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: studio product photography look with a Canon EOS R5 and 85mm f/1.4 lens, shot at f/4 for controlled depth and crisp package edges.
- Lighting: soft natural window light from upper-left at roughly 45°, with a faint fill on the right and gentle shadow falloff; keep highlights clean on the glass bottle, liquid meniscus, reed sticks, paper label, and box edges.
- Color grade: cream beige + gold + charcoal with subtle warm paper tones, inspired by Le Labo and Diptyque retail packaging photography.
- Realism details: include micro-scratches in glass highlights, mild paper grain on the label, tiny dust specks on the tabletop only where natural, precise contact shadows, and slightly varied reed-stick heights for a photographed product feel.

[6. MOOD]
Premium fragrance-brand editorial — quiet luxury boutique shelf aesthetic with Le Labo / Diptyque-inspired restraint, tactile retail packaging, warm café-like comfort, and meticulous product finish.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: the following Korean strings must appear correctly and cleanly in the rendered image: “오늘의 카페 — Coffee Bloom”, “매장 시그니처 향”, “매장 로고”, “향 이름”, “작은 카피”, “매장 위치”.
- Also include short realistic package details in Korean where space allows: “서울 성수점”, “₩32,000”, “100ml”, “BATCH 0526”, “커피 플라워 · 머스크 우드”, “시향 카드”.
- Keep the package composition balanced and premium, with all major label elements sharp and legible at thumbnail size.
- Maintain product realism: glass, liquid, paper, reed sticks, metallic foil, barcode area, and printed typography should look physically plausible and not warped.

[1. PURPOSE]
Create a vertical store notice board for small businesses, designed for door or wall display. Clear, printable Korean information poster for business hours, closed days, monthly events, SNS QR guidance, and quick customer contact details.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Poster format: A4-style vertical layout, optimized for 1024x1536 print-ready signage.
- Main headline area at the top 16%: bold title for {매장명}, with a compact subtitle line showing {업종설명}.
- Include realistic storefront details: notice date {공지일자}, address {주소}, contact {연락처}, SNS handle {SNS계정}, and a small QR placeholder labeled for scanning.
- Information blocks stacked in a readable hierarchy: operating hours, closed day, monthly event, reservation or pickup note, and SNS QR area.
- Visuals should combine {비주얼요소} with small icons such as clock, calendar, gift, map pin, phone, and SNS symbol.
- Background should feel like premium printed board stock: off-white cream paper texture with subtle grain, faint ink absorption, and gentle card shadows.
- Add practical printed-board details such as thin dividers, small label chips, corner tape illustration, and a footer note so it feels like an actual notice posted at a shop entrance.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
- Top header band: place the main store name “{매장명}” and short descriptor “{업종설명}” in a centered or slightly left-aligned masthead, using {타이포스타일} with strong visual weight.
- Brand/identity area: integrate a logo placeholder or illustrated shop mark using {비주얼요소}; add a small tag line “오늘도 따뜻하게 준비했습니다”.
- Date label: near the header, include “NOTICE · {공지일자}” and a small shop bulletin label such as “DOOR GUIDE”.
- Information section 1: present operating details in clearly separated rows or cards: “영업시간 {영업시간}”, “휴무 {휴무일}”, “주문/예약 {예약안내}”.
- Information section 2: reserve one highlighted event area for “이번 달 이벤트”, showing {이벤트명}, {이벤트기간}, and a short benefit line {이벤트혜택} with a gift or star icon.
- Local information strip: include “주소 {주소}” and “문의 {연락처}” in smaller text with map pin and phone icons.
- QR/SNS zone: include a compact QR placeholder with a proper quiet zone inside the QR box, label it “SNS QR”, and place “{SNS계정}” plus “팔로우하고 새 소식 받기”.
- Footer strip: add a thin closing line with a practical notice such as “방문 전 영업 변동은 SNS에서 확인해 주세요” and a small page-like code “SHOP NOTICE 01”.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: use Pretendard Bold or Noto Sans KR ExtraBold for main headers, Pretendard Medium for subheads, and Pretendard Regular or Nanum Gothic for small information text; headline size around 70–90px equivalent, body around 26–34px equivalent, label text around 18–22px equivalent.
- Color palette: cream #F6F0E6, charcoal #2E2E2E, warm beige #D8C7B3, muted accent based on {컬러톤}; keep high contrast for readability.
- Border/shadow: use thin charcoal rules, rounded boxes, label ribbons, divider lines, and a very soft drop shadow with 4px vertical offset, 12px blur, 15% opacity for layered cards.
- Icon style: simple mono-line or filled Korean editorial icons, matched stroke weight, with small accent circles or stickers for event emphasis.
- Print realism: include subtle paper grain, slight ink texture on black text, and tiny registration-like footer marks without making the layout look like an official certificate.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: clean flat graphic poster look, as if photographed with a 50mm standard lens and then converted into a precise editorial layout; no distortion, no perspective warp.
- Lighting: soft diffused daylight from upper-left, even exposure across the page, with only a faint paper-shadow feel around cards and icons.
- Color grade: warm cream + charcoal + muted store-sign accent, with lightly desaturated tones and print-friendly contrast.

[6. MOOD]
Practical small-business storefront signage — warm Korean print design with a Kinfolk-style editorial calm, friendly neighborhood-shop personality, and organized daily bulletin-board charm.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: 반드시 정확히 보여야 하는 문구: “매장 안내 게시판”, “{매장명}”, “영업시간 {영업시간}”, “휴무 {휴무일}”, “이번 달 이벤트”, “SNS QR”, “{SNS계정}”.
- Include realistic rendered notice details: “NOTICE · {공지일자}”, “주소 {주소}”, “문의 {연락처}”, “{이벤트명}”, “{이벤트기간}”, “{이벤트혜택}”.
- Layout invariant: vertical A4-style composition, legible at storefront distance, with rich but readable hierarchy and clearly separated information cards.
- Text must remain crisp and correctly spelled in Korean, with no broken or garbled characters.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]
- Fake official seals / certifications
- Broken Korean characters
- Celebrity composites or face morphing

[1. PURPOSE]
Korean hand-lettered chalkboard menu board for a cafe or storefront exterior, designed as a vertical hero photograph for menu display and venue presentation.
Street-facing blackboard sign with pastel chalk typography, realistic chalk dust, multiple menu items with prices, store details, small food doodles, and the lived-in atmosphere of a real neighborhood {매장 종류} entrance.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Main chalkboard occupies about 80% of the frame, photographed vertically at {비율}; title zone at the top 18%, signature/menu list through the center 58%, price alignment column on the right 12%, and store/contact details along the lower 12%.
- Hero surface is a matte black chalkboard with visible chalk smudges, erased ghost marks, fingerprints near the edges, and a slightly worn wooden or metal frame mounted outside a storefront.
- Surround the board with realistic exterior context from {배경}: partial glass door reflection, window edge, brick or concrete wall, small chalk tray, clipped paper notice, planter, umbrella stand, or sidewalk texture, while keeping the menu text dominant and readable.
- Include a practical cafe-menu layout: store name, category dividers, item names, prices, today’s recommendation marker, small operating-hours/contact line, and decorative chalk divider rules.
- Use {매장 종류}, {메뉴 구성}, {손글씨 결}, {컬러 톤}, {레이아웃}, {배경}, {비율} placeholders exactly as provided.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
1. Header zone (top 18%): set the main title '손글씨 칠판 메뉴판' in large hand-drawn chalk lettering, slightly uneven for a natural handwritten feel. Add a smaller store label such as '연남동 작은 카페', '{매장 종류}', or 'TODAY MENU' depending on {레이아웃}.
2. Menu body (middle 58%): place {메뉴 구성} as a stacked Korean list with realistic item names and right-aligned prices, for example '아메리카노 4,500', '카페라떼 5,000', '바닐라빈 라떼 5,800', '딸기 크림 라떼 6,500', '소금빵 3,800', '바스크 치즈케이크 6,800'. Keep spacing lively like real handwriting but make every line legible.
3. Category and price hierarchy: include chalk category labels such as '카페', '시그니처 메뉴', '디저트', and '가격'; use thin chalk divider lines, dots, arrows, and small boxes to organize the board.
4. Accent illustrations: add tiny chalk doodles around list edges in the style of {손글씨 결}, such as coffee cups, steam curls, croissant, donut, beans, milk bottle, cake slice, leaf sprigs, stars, and price-tag shapes. Let the doodles feel hand-drawn and integrated with the menu rather than printed icons.
5. Bottom information band: add realistic store details in small Korean chalk text, such as 'OPEN 10:00 - 21:00', '라스트오더 20:30', '서울 마포구 연남로 12', '@daily_cafe', and '문의 02-123-4567'. Include a small QR-code-like chalk square or reserved sticker area drawn softly, not as an official mark.
6. Board context (outer frame): show {배경} with storefront cues—doorframe, window reflection, wall texture, hanging string light reflection, metal stand legs, sidewalk, seasonal leaves, or a small potted plant—captured as part of a real cafe exterior.
7. Color balance: apply {컬러 톤} with crisp warm white chalk for structure, pastel yellow/pink/mint/sky-blue accents for highlights, and a deep charcoal-black board base that preserves texture and contrast.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: hand-drawn chalk lettering with bold brush-chalk headers, medium-weight menu lines, small caption text, and visibly varied pressure; mimic casual cafe signage written by hand rather than polished digital type.
- Fonts reference: handwritten Korean chalk style inspired by Hongdae / Yeonnam cafe signage, with playful but readable Hangul proportions; avoid clean sans-serif computer text.
- Color palette: {컬러 톤} plus soft pastel yellow, pink, mint, sky blue, and warm off-white chalk highlights; blackboard base should remain deep charcoal-black with natural powder buildup.
- Border/shadow: use a hand-drawn double chalk border, small corner flourishes, dotted separators, and soft chalk dust halos around letters. Add natural shadow from the board frame and realistic contact shadows on the wall or sidewalk.
- Surface realism: include erased previous-menu traces, chalk crumbs on the ledge, smudged fingertip corrections, slightly uneven line alignment, and tiny scratches on the frame for a photographed storefront feel.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: 35mm lens, f/2.8, straight-on storefront sign framing with mild perspective realism.
- Lighting: overcast diffused daylight or soft shade from upper-left, with gentle ambient fill so the chalk texture is visible without harsh glare; slight reflections on nearby glass are acceptable.
- Color grade: matte black + chalk white + pastel candy accents, slightly muted for a real street-side cafe sign look, with subtle filmic contrast and natural street-environment color.
- Depth and realism: board face remains sharp; surrounding storefront elements may fall slightly softer toward the edges, preserving the feeling of a real photographed exterior menu board.

[6. MOOD]
Editorial storefront-sign aesthetic — like a photographed Hongdae / Yeonnam cafe blackboard menu captured for a design portfolio, warm and approachable, with enough real shop details to feel ready for customers walking by.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: 반드시 아래 문구가 또렷하게 보여야 함: '손글씨 칠판 메뉴판', '카페', '시그니처 메뉴', '가격'.
- Also include readable Korean menu/store microcopy such as '오늘의 추천', 'OPEN 10:00 - 21:00', '서울 마포구 연남로 12', '@daily_cafe', and at least 5 menu items with won prices like '₩4,500' or '4,500원'.
- Keep Korean chalk strokes natural and legible; no broken Hangul, no gibberish characters, no scrambled line order.
- Preserve a realistic chalkboard layout with clear title, menu categories, item list, right-aligned prices, and small bottom contact/address information.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]
- Fake official seals / certifications
- Broken Korean characters

[1. PURPOSE]
Create a square store music playlist card for social posting and in-store display, styled like a Spotify/Apple Music inspired editorial graphic.
Use the card to present {매장 무드} with a polished music-app aesthetic, realistic café/store atmosphere, and clear Korean/English typography that feels like an actual printed card photographed for social media.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Center the main playlist card at about 82-88% of the frame, photographed on a realistic store counter or café tabletop with subtle paper grain, soft shadows, and tactile surface texture.
- Build the background from {컬러 톤}: a real material surface such as matte paper, painted wood, stone counter, or fabric placemat, with small natural contextual details like a receipt corner, coffee cup edge, sticker label, cable loop, plant shadow, or tiny listening-note card.
- Place the title/header near the top 12% area, the playlist rows in the middle 50-55%, and the visual block for {대표 비주얼} in a prominent side or lower section depending on the card layout.
- Use {비율} as the final canvas framing and keep the design compact, poster-like, and readable at thumbnail size while still feeling like a real social post photographed in-store.
- Ensure {플랫폼} is clearly communicated through platform-inspired color blocking, rounded UI cues, app-style chips, progress-bar elements, and a small text badge such as "PLAY ON {플랫폼}".
- Add realistic social card details: store playlist handle "@store.sound", small save/share micro icons, hashtag-like text "#매장음악 #오늘의플레이리스트", a tiny QR-code area, and a printed-card footer line.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
1. Header zone (top 12-15%): Set a bold playlist heading tied to {매장 무드}, with smaller subtitle text beneath it in a clean app-card hierarchy. Include short Korean display text such as "오늘의 매장 플레이리스트", "VOL.052", and "2026.05.01 FRI".
2. Playlist body (middle 45-55%): Typeset the {곡 리스트 5} as exactly five neat rows, each with track number, title, artist, and a small duration-style detail aligned to the right. Add a subtle "오늘의 픽" badge near the first track without creating an extra track row.
3. Feature visual block (lower-left or right 30-35%): Render {대표 비주얼} as a rich collage-like panel with crisp cut edges, layered paper pieces, small tape tabs, tiny waveform graphics, and premium playlist-card styling.
4. Platform accent system: Apply {플랫폼} cues through UI strips, progress-bar-like elements, playback dots, rounded accent chips, and a platform name badge while keeping the overall design original.
5. Palette integration: Blend {컬러 톤} into the tabletop, printed card stock, title, separators, highlight shapes, sticker accents, and small decorative waveform elements so the card feels cohesive and physically present.
6. Information hierarchy: Keep the most important playlist title and first track visually strongest, with the rest of the lines stepping down in size and weight.
7. Footer utility area: Add a bottom strip with "매장 BGM CURATION", "OPEN 10:00-22:00", "서울 성수동 사운드 스토어", "저장 · 공유 · 듣기", a tiny QR block, and small credit text "curated by @store.sound".

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: Use Pretendard or Noto Sans KR for Korean UI text, with bold 700-800 weight for headers and 400-500 weight for track rows; pair with a simple sans-serif Latin face for English artist names.
- Color palette: Derive the palette from {컬러 톤}, using platform-inspired dark green/black if {플랫폼} leans Spotify, or clean white/soft gray with subtle blue-green accents if it leans Apple Music; keep contrast high and text readable.
- Border/shadow: Add a soft drop shadow with 4px y-offset, 14px blur, 18% opacity under the main card; use thin 1px divider lines and rounded corners around 18-24px.
- Physical print detail: Add faint paper fibers, tiny ink gain, slight edge thickness, realistic corner curvature, soft contact shadows, and small printed registration marks to make the card feel photographed rather than flat-generated.
- Decorative UI details: Include tiny equalizer bars, waveform snippets, a progress slider, circular play/pause control, volume dot, playlist count label "5 TRACKS", and micro labels like "STORE MIX" and "NOW PLAYING".

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: Graphic design mockup rendered like a clean product poster, photographed with a Canon EOS R5 and RF 35mm f/1.8 lens in an overhead top-down layout equivalent to a 35mm flat composition.
- Lighting: Studio-like even illumination with a slight upper-left highlight, gentle shadow falloff on the card edges, soft reflections on any nearby cup or sticker surface, and realistic ambient light from a store window.
- Color grade: Music-app editorial grade with deep charcoal, forest green, off-white, and muted accent hues matched to {컬러 톤}.
- Surface realism: Use tangible counter texture, printed paper finish, subtle fingerprints on glossy sticker areas, and natural occlusion where props overlap the edge of the card.

[6. MOOD]
Premium in-store music curation card — Spotify editorial UI meets a modern café playlist poster aesthetic, with warm real-world store details and a curated social-media-ready atmosphere.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: resolved values for {매장 무드}, {곡 리스트 5}, {플랫폼}, {대표 비주얼}, {컬러 톤}, and {비율} must render cleanly with correct Korean spacing, punctuation, and line breaks.
- 반드시 정확히 표시되어야 하는 한글 문자열: "오늘의 매장 플레이리스트", "오늘의 픽", "매장 BGM", "저장", "공유", "듣기", "서울 성수동 사운드 스토어", "#매장음악", "#오늘의플레이리스트".
- The playlist must contain exactly 5 visible track lines matching {곡 리스트 5} structure; do not add a sixth song, bonus track, or duplicate list row.
- {플랫폼} must appear as readable text at least once, for example in a badge reading "PLAY ON {플랫폼}".
- All Korean text must render cleanly with correct spacing, punctuation, and line breaks.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]
- Fake official seals / certifications
- Broken Korean characters
- Celebrity composites or unauthorized likeness

- Embroidery placement: {자수·로고} placed on the chest or apron pocket area in a small but legible size, aligned straight and centered for mockup clarity, rendered as real thread with slight raised texture and stitch direction.
- Color emphasis: {컬러 톤} applied to garment accents, thread color, trim, label tabs, hangtag ink, and tiny brand marks, while keeping the base textile neutral, premium, and commercially believable.
- Supporting details: include a neat Korean sample label card reading '사장님 유니폼 샘플', a small date line '2026 봄 시즌', a tiny note '앞치마 자수 위치', and a product memo strip with size/finish cues such as '원단 견본' and '매장용 샘플'.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
1) Base layout — Center the {매장} uniform mockup in a square composition, with the apron as the main visual anchor and the cap/secondary piece supporting the complete shop-owner brand set.
2) Garment surface — Render {유니폼 결} with realistic cloth thickness, subtle weave detail, neat stitching, softened folds, reinforced seams, pressed-but-worn fabric behavior, and a product-photography finish rather than illustration-like flatness.
3) Brand mark zone — Place {자수·로고} in a small embroidered treatment that looks stitched into the fabric, with precise spacing, sharp edges, visible thread ridges, and no broken characters.
4) Color mapping — Apply {컬러 톤} consistently across piping, thread, label accents, cap trim, hangtag line art, or pocket details so the set feels like a cohesive brand mockup.
5) Background plane — Build {배경} as a believable boutique studio surface with soft matte texture, gentle contact shadows, a pinned fabric swatch, folded sample cloth, pencil mark or measuring tape edge, and small catalog-style labels that add context while keeping the garment dominant.
6) Format balance — Maintain {비율} proportions with comfortable product-catalog spacing, allowing the uniform silhouette, cap, hangtag, swatch, and memo labels to read clearly within the 1:1 frame.
7) Catalog realism — Add small production-preview elements: a woven neck label, a kraft paper hangtag, a short care-label tab, a compact fabric swatch card, and tiny Korean spec notes such as '자수 샘플', '컬러 확인', and '앞주머니 디테일'.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: use restrained Pretendard or Noto Sans KR style in medium weight for small catalog labels, hangtags, and spec notes; set Korean text cleanly, including '사장님 유니폼 샘플', '앞치마 자수 위치', '원단 견본', '매장용 샘플', and '2026 봄 시즌'.
- Color palette: craft brown, matte black, warm cream, natural cotton beige, and the shop’s signature accent from {컬러 톤}; keep saturation controlled and commercially believable.
- Border/shadow: soft studio drop shadow under the garment, about 4px y-offset, 12px blur, 15% opacity, with subtle edge falloff for a polished mockup look.
- Material details: fabric should show woven fibers, mild wrinkles near strap bends, stitched reinforcement, slightly raised embroidery, matte metal adjusters if present, and believable sewing construction.
- Decorative graphic elements: include small catalog ticks, fine divider lines, swatch labels, and a modest hangtag layout, all scaled like real uniform-sample documentation rather than poster headlines.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: studio product shot, 85mm f/2.8 equivalent, front-facing composition with minimal perspective distortion.
- Lighting: even softbox key light from upper-left at about 45°, gentle fill from right, light shadow separation to reveal fabric structure, embroidery depth, paper tag texture, and layered garment edges.
- Color grade: neutral warm editorial grade with craft-brown, black, warm cream, and muted accent tones; slight desaturation for a premium local-brand merchandise feel.
- Rendering style: photorealistic product editorial image with tactile textile detail, realistic contact shadows, accurate stitch scale, and a practical boutique-workshop atmosphere.

[6. MOOD]
Local boutique merchandise preview — feels like an urban lifestyle magazine product spread for a real shop owner choosing a uniform, with polished product photography, practical sample-room details, and brand-ready presentation.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: the exact Korean strings that must appear correctly are {매장}, {유니폼 결}, {자수·로고}, {컬러 톤}, {배경}, {비율} if any visible text or label is included in the design.
- Additional visible Korean text must be spelled correctly if used: '사장님 유니폼 샘플', '앞치마 자수 위치', '원단 견본', '매장용 샘플', '2026 봄 시즌', '자수 샘플', '컬러 확인', '앞주머니 디테일'.
- Composition invariant: the apron/uniform set must remain the main hero object, centered and readable as a mockup, with supporting swatches, tags, and notes kept secondary.
- Fabric realism: seams, straps, embroidery, pockets, labels, and garment edges must look physically plausible and neatly finished.
- Brand preview clarity: {자수·로고} must look embroidered into the apron or pocket area, not printed flat or floating above the fabric.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]
- Fake official seals / certifications
- Broken Korean characters

[1. PURPOSE]
Korean store table mat design for dine-in use, one-time-use or recyclable print layout.
A horizontal branded placemat that works as tableware, mini menu, store promotion, and QR call-to-action in one realistic printed sheet.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- The sheet fills the full landscape canvas in a {레이아웃} proportion, with tiny crop ticks, realistic paper edges, and a practical print-safe area for disposable/recyclable table mat production.
- Main visual area uses {시그니처 비주얼} as the focal illustration block, placed slightly left of center with small caption tags and menu dividers around it.
- {매장}, {매장 영문명}, and {로고 문구} are integrated as a branded in-store goods piece, like a premium café or casual dining placemat.
- Add functional restaurant-mat information: {대표 메뉴}, {가격대}, {매장 주소}, {연락처}, {이벤트 문구}, and a clear {QR 안내} zone in the lower-right corner.
- Background uses kraft-paper texture, soy-ink grain, warm off-white panels, small tableware icons, dotted divider lines, coupon-style tabs, and a soft recycled paper fiber feel.
- The design should feel actually printed and used on a tabletop: flat paper surface, slight ink absorption, crisp Korean typography, and a balanced mix of illustration, menu text, event notice, and QR block.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
- Header area (top 15%): place {매장} as the main store label, pair it with {매장 영문명}, add {로고 문구}, and include small issue-like details such as “TABLE MAT No. 05”, “TODAY’S TABLE”, and a small date label “2026.05”.
- Hero visual area (left-mid 42%): display {시그니처 비주얼} as the largest element, with a caption reading “오늘의 시그니처” and a small handwritten note beside the illustration.
- Copy and menu area (center-right 26%): set {한 줄 카피} as the main slogan, then add a compact menu/pricelist block using {대표 메뉴} and {가격대}; use clear dividers, bullet dots, and tiny labels like “추천 메뉴”, “포장 가능”, and “매장 인기”.
- QR and event area (bottom-right 14%): place {QR 안내} inside a clearly scannable square zone; below or beside it, add {이벤트 문구} as a coupon-style CTA with small arrows pointing toward the QR.
- Footer strip (bottom 10%): include {매장 주소}, {연락처}, a small recycling note “재활용 종이 매트”, and tiny icon-style marks for dine-in, take-out, review, and social follow.
- Base layer: use kraft brown, deep black, muted accent ink, and warm paper tones from {컬러 톤}, making the placemat readable from an overhead dining-table view.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: {타이포}; combine Nanum Myeongjo for Korean headline emphasis with Pretendard or Noto Sans KR for menu, address, QR instructions, and event details; use bold weights for prices and CTA labels.
- Color palette: {컬러 톤} should translate into kraft brown paper, deep black ink, muted store-brand accent color, warm off-white menu panels, and print-friendly contrast.
- Graphic system: use thin framing rules, dotted dividers, small stamp-box shapes, map-pin icons, cup/plate/chopstick line icons, and coupon-tab graphics to make it feel like a real shop placemat.
- Print texture: show natural paper fiber, slight ink spread, small halftone accents, and subtle soy-ink irregularity while keeping all Korean letters and prices sharp.
- Brand layout: logo, menu, address, contact, event, and QR should feel intentionally designed as a cohesive store identity system rather than isolated text blocks.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: top-down flat-lay composition, 35mm lens look, f/5.6, sharp printed-paper detail across the whole mat.
- Lighting: even overhead studio lighting with slight softbox falloff, no harsh specular glare, designed to resemble a photographed packaging and tableware print mockup.
- Color grade: warm kraft brown + black + muted signature accent, with natural paper texture, edible dining warmth, and restrained editorial contrast.

[6. MOOD]
Premium café tableware editorial — polished retail-brand placemat design with independent neighborhood-store warmth, practical menu information, and eco-conscious recyclable paper character.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: 반드시 정확히 보여야 하는 문자열: “{매장}”, “{매장 영문명}”, “{로고 문구}”, “{한 줄 카피}”, “{대표 메뉴}”, “{가격대}”, “{매장 주소}”, “{연락처}”, “{QR 안내}”, “{이벤트 문구}”.
- Additional readable Korean microcopy: “오늘의 시그니처”, “추천 메뉴”, “포장 가능”, “매장 인기”, “재활용 종이 매트”, “식사 후 QR로 리뷰 남기기”.
- Layout invariant: horizontal placemat composition only; QR must stay in the lower-right zone and remain clearly scannable with a realistic quiet zone around the code.
- Print clarity: all Korean characters, prices, address, contact, and menu labels must be clean, complete, and fully legible with no warped or broken glyphs.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]
- Fake official seals / certifications
- Broken Korean characters
- Celebrity composites or recognizable public-figure likenesses
