[1. PURPOSE]
K-pop comeback teaser poster for a dark chic campaign, vertical editorial key visual for album reveal, showcase announcement, and social teaser use.
High-impact idol poster with a premium music-magazine and arena-concert feel, designed to look like a real comeback announcement with release information, showcase details, ticket notice, label credit, and sponsor strip.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- One {아티스트} hero dominates the frame at about 65% height, placed slightly off-center with a confident stage-ready pose and dramatic eye contact or profile silhouette.
- Background is a dark studio-stage environment with layered smoke, reflective floor hints, faint concert rigging silhouettes, LED scan lines, small lens flares, and out-of-focus audience-light bokeh for a believable comeback-poster atmosphere.
- {대표 비주얼} should read instantly at thumbnail size: strong silhouette, crisp facial readability, styled hair and wardrobe detail, one memorable accent rim light, and a polished idol-editorial finish.
- Title zone sits in the upper or lower third depending on pose balance; make {타이틀} the main anchor, with {발매일}, {멤버명}, and {한글부제} arranged as real teaser-poster information.
- Add practical poster details: {쇼케이스정보}, {장소}, {티켓정보}, a small QR-style block or barcode-like ticket mark, label credit, and {스폰서문구} in a bottom sponsor area.
- Integrate {컨셉} and {컬러톤} through costume accents, light streaks, smoke color, typography highlights, and decorative graphic fragments while keeping {비율} as a tall vertical poster layout.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
1) Hero render: place {아티스트} as the main subject, framed waist-up to full-body depending on pose, with crisp facial focus, luxury stage styling, glossy hair detail, and confident comeback-era presence.
2) Light architecture: build a dark theatrical scene using smoke layers, hard back rim lights, front fill, LED bar reflections, bokeh points, and faint arena equipment silhouettes so the subject separates clearly from the background.
3) Title treatment: set {타이틀} as the primary typographic anchor, large and bold, with {발매일} and {멤버명} placed like official album teaser copy rather than a generic flyer.
4) Supporting text system: include {한글부제}, “COMING SOON”, “1ST MINI ALBUM”, “TRACKLIST OPEN”, or similar small teaser labels, plus Korean release copy that looks commercially printed.
5) Event information: add {쇼케이스정보}, {장소}, {티켓정보}, small seat/open notice, ticket code, and a compact QR/barcode-style graphic in the lower third or side column.
6) Sponsor and credit strip: include {스폰서문구}, label/production credit, styling credit, photographer credit, and small decorative separators, using realistic poster micro-typography.
7) Color accents: apply {컬러톤} as selective glow, edge light, chrome lettering, glassy overlays, or graphic highlight while preserving deep blacks and high contrast.
8) Finish pass: refine the poster with polished editorial contrast, sharp subject edges, believable printed-poster texture, cinematic smoke depth, and precise alignment between image, graphics, and typography.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: use bold English sans-serif such as Helvetica Neue, DIN Condensed, or Pretendard ExtraBold for the main title, with Korean information in Pretendard Medium or Noto Sans KR; main title size should feel poster-scale, while event details and credits use compact music-promo microtype.
- Color palette: deep black #050507, charcoal #17171C, electric blue #2D7CFF, neon pink #FF4FA3, metallic gold #C8A45D, cold silver #BFC6D1.
- Graphic treatment: allow thin chrome lines, holographic fragments, waveform motifs, star glints, stage-light cones, QR/barcode-like marks, ticket dividers, and a bottom sponsor band that feels like a real entertainment poster.
- Text effects: use soft 8px shadow with 18% opacity behind bright text if needed, subtle rim-light glow around the hero, slight chromatic edge on the title, and metallic gradients for selected title strokes.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: full-frame fashion/editorial look, Sony A7R IV with 85mm f/1.4 portrait lens, shallow depth of field, sharp subject separation, poster-grade clarity.
- Lighting: stage-keyed cinematic lighting with a hard back rim from upper-left, soft fill from front-right, thin smoke diffusion, scattered practical bokeh lights in the rear, and glossy reflections on wardrobe or floor.
- Color grade: dark noir base with blue-magenta accent glow, slight metallic gold highlights, high contrast, cool shadow bias, polished music-promo finish.

[6. MOOD]
Premium K-pop comeback teaser — like a high-end music magazine cover meets an arena-concert poster, with a sleek SM/HYBE/JYP-style promotional finish, dramatic idol confidence, and real-world album showcase information.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: 반드시 정확히 보여야 하는 문구: "NEW WAVE", "2026.06", "{멤버명}", "{한글부제}", "{쇼케이스정보}", "{장소}", "{티켓정보}".
- 포스터 내 실제 렌더링 문구 예시: "1ST MINI ALBUM", "COMEBACK TEASER", "2026.06.14 6PM KST", "쇼케이스 2026.06.20 SAT 19:30", "서울 블루스퀘어 마스터카드홀", "티켓 오픈 2026.06.03 20:00", "예매 코드 NW-0620", "VOL.01 TEASER POSTER".
- Layout invariants: one hero subject only, strong stage-like contrast, readable comeback title hierarchy, realistic poster information blocks, accurate idol proportions, sharp eyes, refined hair strands, and disciplined typography.
- Preserve the dark chic comeback-poster composition with cinematic smoke, bokeh, bold editorial typography, ticket/showcase details, label credits, and a polished entertainment-industry print finish.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]
- Fake official seals / government-style certifications
- Broken Korean characters or garbled Hangul
- Unlicensed celebrity composites or copying an identifiable real idol face

[INPUT]
- language: Korean
- output_size: 1024x1536

[1. PURPOSE]
Korean seasonal greeting card for new semester and graduation season, portrait editorial layout for academy, church, and small-business encouragement use.
A warm vertical card for March back-to-school and year-end graduation messaging, designed like a photographed premium stationery piece with real printed details, seasonal captions, and keepsake-card texture.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Main layout: centered 70% hero composition with a soft seasonal illustration cluster in the middle, headline occupying the upper 18% and message block the lower 22%, layered with realistic printed-card details.
- Background treatment: warm off-white paper texture with subtle spring haze, faint bokeh, airy sky gradient near the top, and lightly visible fibers, paper grain, and soft shadows from overlapping stationery.
- Framing direction: portrait greeting-card design with a balanced editorial hierarchy; include practical card details such as a date label, sender line, small caption, seasonal stickers, and a tiny keepsake tag while keeping the main message instantly readable on mobile.
- Use {시즌}, {메시지}, {비주얼}, {컬러 팔레트}, {타이포}, {비율} as user-customizable placeholders.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
1. Header zone (top 15%): set a small seasonal label based on {시즌}, aligned center, with thin separator rules above and below in charcoal gray; add realistic micro text such as “2026 SEASON CARD”, “VOL.03”, and a small date badge “3월·12월 응원 카드”.
2. Main hero zone (middle 50%): show {비주얼} as a friendly seasonal collage with school items arranged around a soft student silhouette; include layered notebook paper, a graduation cap ribbon, a pencil, tiny pressed-flower accents, translucent tape pieces, and a small photo-corner detail for depth.
3. Typography zone (upper-middle): place the main message {메시지} in a refined Korean serif style, large enough to dominate the card; include the required greeting line “새 학기, 새 마음 — 응원합니다” as a clear printed headline or subtitle.
4. Support line zone (lower-middle): place {타이포} as a smaller secondary line, spaced out with tracking, using a neat editorial arrangement; add short Korean card copy such as “오늘의 시작을 오래 기억하기”, “함께 걸어온 시간을 축하합니다”, and “새로운 교실, 새로운 꿈”.
5. Footer zone (bottom 15%): use seasonal accents that echo {컬러 팔레트}, with paper scraps, pencil marks, tiny leaf-like spring motifs, a small sender credit “from. 우리반 선생님”, a location/date line “Seoul · 2026.03 / 2026.12”, and tiny social-style tags “#새학기 #졸업축하 #응원카드”.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: Noto Serif KR or Nanum Myeongjo for the main Korean message, weight 600–700, headline size hint 58–72px; Pretendard or Inter for secondary English and micro labels, weight 500, 18–24px, wide letter spacing.
- Color palette: {컬러 팔레트} interpreted as beige #E9DDC9, white #FFFFFF, charcoal #2D2D2D, spring pink #F3B7C6 accents, with soft ink density variation like high-quality risograph or letterpress-inspired printing.

- Vertical poster in 1024x1536 ratio with a strong hero drink occupying the center 55–60% of the frame, plus a top campaign header and a lower information/menu zone.
- Main drink should be placed slightly below center for a premium editorial balance; seasonal props from {비주얼} should frame the cup/glass naturally, as if arranged on a real café counter.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
1) Header zone (top 15–18%): Set the main headline as “시즌 한정” in bold Korean type. Add {시즌명} as a small label chip, {영문부제} beneath the headline, and an editorial tag such as “SEASON SPECIAL VOL.04 / 2026”.
2) Hero zone (middle 50–55%): Feature {메뉴명} as the central drink image, rendered as polished café commercial food photography with garnish, ice/foam/steam, reflections on the cup, and seasonal props from {비주얼}.
3) Atmosphere layer: Add a real café counter, blurred espresso machine or display shelf lights in the background, subtle staff movement bokeh, and season-matched haze so the product belongs in a real store environment.

6) Companion menu strip: Add two small side menu cards: {추천메뉴1} / {추천가격1}, {추천메뉴2} / {추천가격2}, separated by thin dividers and tiny cup or pastry icons.
7) Promotional badge: Add a seasonal sticker-style badge containing {프로모션문구}, plus a small QR-style coupon square labeled “쿠폰 확인”.
8) Accent details: Use flowers, leaves, fruit slices, cinnamon, cocoa powder, frost, droplets, or warm steam depending on the season, with tactile textures visible on props and counter.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: bold Korean sans-serif such as Pretendard Black or Noto Sans KR ExtraBold for the main title, with a clean geometric English subtitle in Pretendard SemiBold or Montserrat Bold; size hierarchy should be obvious at a glance.
- Use {타이포} as the typographic direction. Korean text must be crisp, evenly tracked, and fully legible on all headline, menu, price, and footer elements.
- Color palette: use {컬러 팔레트} as the seasonal base, with cream paper-label panels, translucent sticker chips, or warm café-card blocks when needed for contrast.
- Border/shadow: subtle editorial drop shadow under the hero product, about 4px vertical offset, 12px blur, 15% opacity; use gentle reflection and surface contact shadow on the café counter.

- Background should be a warm off-white hanji paper tone with visible matte fiber texture, faint ink grain, and subtle printed-page imperfections so the design feels like a real seasonal editorial poster.

- Enrich the frame with realistic printed magazine-cover details: issue number, date label, short feature blurbs, small editorial credits, barcode area, price label, and tiny spine-style side text.
- Use a celebratory Korean festive border language with bojagi-inspired pattern strips, small tassels, stamp-like decorative labels, food-table accents, floral or seasonal sprig motifs, and paper cutout ornaments that match {시각 모티프}.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
1. Header zone (top 15%): set the holiday identity for {명절} in a bold Korean title treatment, aligned centrally with a small secondary accent line beneath; include magazine details such as “VOL.247”, “2026 명절 특별호”, and “계절 인사 에디션”.
2. Main illustration zone (middle 55%): show {시각 모티프} as a flat, cohesive holiday tableau, with the largest motifs anchored in the center and smaller symbolic items arranged diagonally to create rhythm; add contextual objects such as folded hanbok fabric, traditional food plates, gift wrapping, moon/sun symbols, lanterns, flowers, grains, or seasonal tableware when culturally appropriate to {명절}.
3. Greeting zone (lower middle 15%): place {인사} in a prominent, readable band with strong contrast against the background; support it with a small caption such as “마음을 전하는 오늘의 인사” or “가족과 이웃에게 보내는 따뜻한 한 줄”.
4. Editorial detail layer: add 2–3 short Korean cover-line blurbs around the hero area, for example “온 가족이 함께”, “차례상과 마음”, “보름달 아래 소원”, “새해 복을 담다”, adapting the wording to {명절}.
5. Footer zone: include a small barcode block at the lower right, a price/date line such as “₩7,500 · 2026 시즌호”, tiny credit text such as “일러스트 김하루 · 편집 한빛스튜디오”, and a page-like marker “HOLIDAY CARD 01”.
6. Color support: apply {컬러 팔레트} across clothing, food, ornaments, pattern strips, caption labels, and decorative accents, keeping the palette consistent by holiday while allowing natural paper, ink, fabric, food, and shadow tones.
7. Typography treatment: render {타이포} as the main typographic voice, with a magazine-cover hierarchy: large holiday title, medium greeting band, small cover blurbs, micro editorial credits, and barcode/date labels.
8. Style finish: keep {비주얼 결} consistent across the whole card, using flat illustration shapes, crisp printed edges, paper texture, screen-print grain, and a refined cultural magazine finish.
9. Format enforcement: maintain the vertical {비율} canvas with a strong poster-cover structure from top masthead to footer details.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: bold Korean serif for headers, with a secondary Hanja-support line only if it stays legible; use Pretendard Bold or Noto Serif KR Bold for the main line, around 44–64px equivalent, with confident magazine tracking.
- Korean cover text hierarchy: set the main title as “{명절}”, set the greeting as “{인사}”, and add small supporting Korean strings such as “VOL.247”, “2026 명절 특별호”, “계절 인사 에디션”, “온 가족이 함께”, “마음을 담은 선물”, “전통의 맛과 빛”.
- Color palette: use the exact seasonal sets from {컬러 팔레트}; for print texture, anchor the page in warm ivory #F5EFE3, deep black #1A1A1A, festive red #B0181E, gold #C9A24A, beige #D8C6A6, brown #7A5538, and muted green #5F7A4B.
- Border/shadow: use subtle paper-edge framing, bojagi-pattern side strips, inked corner marks, and very light inner shadow 3px y-offset, 10px blur, 12% opacity; avoid heavy bevels or glossy effects.
- Illustration detail: include tangible holiday materials such as hanji, silk ribbon, brass dishware, ceramic bowls, rice cakes, fruit, pine needles, moon motifs, lantern paper, red-and-gold envelope accents, or seasonal grains where appropriate.

- Lighting: even studio softbox illumination from upper-left at 45° with a faint fill from lower-right, producing soft, print-friendly separation without harsh highlights.

- Surface realism: show tactile paper grain, slight ink misregistration, tiny speckles, soft drop shadows under paper labels, and layered printed stickers so the flat illustration feels physically printed and photographed.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Main hero area: a centered couple illustration with a soft romantic silhouette, occupying about 48% of the frame height, surrounded by layered stationery pieces such as washi tape, tiny stickers, and hand-drawn marks.
- Top headline zone: {기념일 종류} near the upper third, paired with {D+숫자} as a numeric anniversary badge and a small date label {날짜}.
- Memory label zone: add {장소} as a location tag, plus {커플이름} as a small signature line that feels like a personal keepsake.
- Message zone: {메시지} placed in the lower-middle area with handwritten rhythm, supported by a tiny caption {사진캡션} beside the Polaroid element.
- Decorative elements: star doodles, heart doodles, calendar sticker, tiny ribbon label, pressed-flower-like paper cutouts, blush-pink tape strips, and a few soft sparkles around the hero area.
- Social sharing details: include {인스타핸들}, {해시태그}, and micro save/share icons near the bottom as if the card is ready for Instagram story or feed sharing.
- Background treatment: warm beige paper texture with subtle grain, cream-to-warm-white base, soft amber stains, faint pencil scuffs, and tactile handmade stationery shadows.
- Composition flow: slightly asymmetrical scrapbook arrangement with overlapping paper pieces, a tilted Polaroid frame, and decorative accents guiding the eye from headline to couple illustration to message.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
1. Background — lay down a textured paper surface in beige and warm white, with subtle grain, faint fiber marks, warm amber smudges, and a handmade card look.
2. Main illustration — place the couple illustration as the central focal point, cleanly integrated with soft edges, charming proportions, cozy outfits, and gentle affectionate body language.
3. Anniversary markers — set {기념일 종류} prominently near the top and {D+숫자} as a secondary numeric accent inside a rounded sticker or calendar badge, aligned to the card’s vertical rhythm.
4. Date and place details — render {날짜} and {장소} as small scrapbook labels, like a diary entry from the day being celebrated.
5. Message block — render {메시지} in a handwritten-style layout below the hero illustration, making it feel like a heartfelt note rather than a formal caption.
6. Decorative doodles — add stars, hearts, sparkles, tiny arrows, mini flowers, tape strips, and sketch marks around the illustration with a natural hand-placed feel.
7. Photo accent — include a small Polaroid-style photo frame element with a warm border, slight tilt, soft shadow, and the caption {사진캡션} written on the lower white margin.
8. Social footer — place {인스타핸들}, {해시태그}, and small save/share/heart micro icons near the lower edge, styled like a personal couple post rather than a commercial ad.
9. Final balance — ensure the card reads clearly at a glance, with typography, doodles, labels, and Polaroid elements framing the couple illustration in a realistic scrapbook layout.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: use a handwritten Korean script style for the main message, paired with a neat sans-serif subtitle look for {기념일 종류}, {D+숫자}, {날짜}, and {장소}; keep the headline around bold 42–60px, support text around 20–28px, and micro labels around 14–18px.
- Color palette: beige, warm amber, blush pink, and white, matching {컬러 팔레트}; add muted rose, soft brown ink, and cream paper tones for a tactile stationery finish.
- Scrapbook details: use paper stickers, washi tape textures, soft pencil doodles, tiny calendar marks, a ribbon tag reading {작은태그}, and a small heart stamp motif.
- Border/shadow: apply a subtle paper-edge shadow, 4px y-offset, 12px blur, 15% opacity, with a faint warm outline on the Polaroid frame and layered paper pieces.
- Illustration style: match {비주얼} with a cute couple illustration, warm facial expressions, simplified features, cozy clothing, and a soft romantic pose.
- Layout tone: preserve a personal handmade-card feeling, with realistic stationery depth, slight rotations, visible paper fibers, and soft desk-photography shadows.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: editorial flat-lay poster look, 35mm lens feel with a mild top-down perspective, as if photographed on a desk setup at f/5.6.
- Lighting: soft diffused window light from upper-left at about 45°, with very gentle fill from the right and no hard shadow edges.

- Material realism: matte paper, lightly textured sticker surfaces, satin tape sheen, soft graphite-like doodle lines, and a warm Polaroid border with subtle handling marks.

[6. MOOD]
Romantic scrapbook-style anniversary card — like a gentle Kinfolk stationery spread mixed with a Korean couple diary illustration, personal Instagram memory post, and handmade love-note collage.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: the following strings must appear exactly as rendered text:
  - {기념일 종류}
  - {D+숫자}
  - {메시지}
  - {날짜}
  - {장소}
  - {커플이름}
  - {사진캡션}
  - {인스타핸들}
  - {해시태그}
  - {작은태그}
- Render the micro social text as small Korean-friendly UI details: “저장”, “공유”, “좋아요” beside simple line icons.
- Maintain a vertical couple greeting-card layout with a centered illustration, doodle accents, scrapbook labels, and a small Polaroid-style photo element.

- Background treatment: soft warm cream paper texture with visible fine grain, pressed-fiber detail, a slight warm vignette at the edges, and delicate paper-layer shadows.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
- Header zone (top 14%): set {기념일} in a refined small-title style, centered, with slight letter spacing, a slim decorative divider, tiny rose-gold dots, and a small seasonal icon such as a heart, rose, diary tab, or candy wrapper motif.

- Footer zone (bottom 16%): finish with a small card code {카드코드}, a delicate maker-style line, and subtle stationery marks such as perforation dots, corner tabs, or foil flecks so the card feels printable and collectible.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: use {타이포}; main Korean message in Noto Serif KR or Nanum Myeongjo, medium-to-semibold weight, large size; pair with a clean handwritten English or Korean accent in a restrained script style for TO/FROM and caption details.

- Seasonal identity: {신년 종류} expressed through traditional Korean New Year cues, including small printed date labels, holiday captions, and folk-inspired ornament details rather than corporate branding.
- Real-world card context: include a partially visible cream envelope, red silk thread, a small gold paper tag, subtle hanji fibers, and seasonal tabletop details such as pine needles, tangerine peel, bokjumeoni fabric texture, or yut-nori sticks near the edges.
- Background treatment: warm off-white paper base with visible hanji texture, tiny fiber flecks, slightly raised ink, and delicate gold-foil catching the light.
- Framing and depth: make the card feel physically printed and photographed, with layered edges, soft shadows, and realistic paper thickness.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
1. Background layer — Use a warm paper texture in off-white/cream, lightly aged and tactile, with visible hanji fibers, soft surface variation, and natural studio falloff.
2. Real card presentation layer — Show the greeting card as a physical vertical sheet resting on a seasonal tabletop with a cream envelope peeking from behind, a red silk cord crossing one corner, and a small blank sender tag printed with “보내는 이: 우리 가족”.
3. Decorative frame layer — Add traditional Korean New Year ornaments inspired by cloud motifs, brush strokes, folk-art accents, dancheong-like curves, small plum blossoms, gold confetti flecks, and hand-painted corner flourishes.
4. Main motif layer — Build the central holiday visual around {시각 모티프}, with the most prominent motif near the lower-middle area and smaller supporting motifs balancing the left and right sides, rendered as printed illustration, foil stamping, or embossed paper cutout.
5. Message layer — Place {인사 메시지} in the upper-middle as the dominant text block, with clear hierarchy, elegant line spacing, and strong contrast against the paper background.
6. Secondary identity layer — Include a small English subtitle reading Happy New Year 2027 near the main headline area, discreetly sized so it supports rather than competes with the Korean message.
7. Date and greeting details — Add small Korean printed details that enrich the card: “2027 새해 인사”, “음력 1월 1일 · 설날”, “복을 담아 전합니다”, and a tiny lower caption “새로운 한 해, 따뜻한 마음을 전해요”.
8. Typography integration — Style the main Korean lettering to feel like bold Korean serif or brush calligraphy using {타이포}, harmonized with traditional motifs and premium print finishing.
9. Finish details — Add refined metallic gold accents, subtle red ink density variation, paper-finish realism, embossed edges, and an editorial greeting-card polish so the result feels like a high-quality seasonal card photographed for a magazine.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: use {타이포}; main headline should feel like bold Korean serif such as Noto Serif KR or expressive brush-calligraphy, headline weight heavy, subtitle in clean sans-serif such as Pretendard Medium, with the English line smaller and understated.
- Color palette: use {컬러 팔레트} with deep vermilion red, metallic gold, clean ivory white, and black ink accents; keep saturation rich, warm, and print-realistic.
- Printed text accents: add small supporting Korean labels in realistic card typography, including “2027 새해 인사”, “음력 1월 1일 · 설날”, “복을 담아 전합니다”, “보내는 이: 우리 가족”, and “새로운 한 해, 따뜻한 마음을 전해요”.
- Border/shadow: add a subtle paper edge and soft cast shadow, with 4px vertical offset, 12px blur, and 15% opacity for a gentle layered-card effect.
- Materials: show visible hanji grain, faint ink absorption, slightly raised gold foil, embossed motif edges, and tiny imperfections that make the print feel real.
- Decorative realism: include festive but tasteful seasonal details such as red silk cord, small gold paper tag, pine sprig, yut-nori sticks, or bojagi textile texture around the card to support the New Year atmosphere.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: studio poster photography look, captured as if with a 50mm lens at f/5.6 for balanced perspective and crisp graphic clarity.
- Lighting: soft studio key light from upper-left at 45°, with a very mild fill from the right to preserve detail in red and gold areas; allow metallic foil highlights to glint naturally.
- Color grade: classic Korean holiday palette with warm red, antique gold, ivory white, and deep black, slightly muted to feel editorial rather than neon.
- Surface detail: realistic paper fibers, slight card warping, gentle envelope shadow, foil reflectivity, and fine printed halftone/ink texture visible on close inspection.

[6. MOOD]
Premium Korean seasonal editorial card — like a refined magazine spread for Lunar New Year, combining traditional folk design, tactile hanji print craft, warm family greeting details, and polished contemporary layout.

[7. CRITICAL]

- Keep {카테고리 8종}, {아이콘 결}, {배경 컬러}, {레이아웃}, {아이콘 컬러}, {라벨}, and {비율} conceptually respected without changing the 1024x1024 square format.

- Broken Korean characters

[INPUT]
- reference_image: {참고 이미지}
- language: Korean
- output_size: 1024x1024

[1. PURPOSE]
KakaoTalk profile photo i2i, polished square portrait crop with a natural lifestyle-photo finish. Preserve the original person’s identity while turning the image into a warm, real-looking profile image that feels casually taken in a tasteful everyday setting.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Subject placement: {원본 인물} occupies the central 62–70% of the frame, with the face as the primary focal point and a tight square crop optimized for KakaoTalk profile icons.
- Background treatment: {배경} rendered as a believable lifestyle or studio-adjacent environment with soft depth separation, such as a sunlit wall, cafe corner, window curtain, bookshelf blur, leafy plant silhouette, or textured plaster surface.
- Spacing and framing: keep a comfortable margin around the head and hairline, with shoulders cropped naturally and a stable profile-thumbnail silhouette.
- Visual concept: apply {컨셉} as the overall portrait direction while allowing subtle real-world details around the subject to make the image feel lived-in and authentic.
- Portrait-card accents: add a very small tasteful date/location label or sticker-like caption near the lower edge, for example Korean micro text such as “2026.05 · 서울”, “오늘의 프로필”, or “soft mood”, placed so it does not cover the face.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
- Hero area (full frame): {원본 인물} is the dominant subject, clearly separated from the background with natural edge detail in hair, face, and clothing.
- Background layer: build {배경} behind the subject using shallow depth of field, with realistic environmental textures such as soft fabric, warm wood, painted wall grain, glass reflections, distant lights, or blurred greenery.
- Light shaping: apply {조명} so the face has soft dimensionality, subtle cheek highlight, catchlights in the eyes, and balanced shadow falloff without glossy skin.
- Color finish: grade the image using {컬러 톤} while keeping skin tones believable and avoiding over-saturation or plastic smoothing.
- Retouch pass: use {후처리} to tidy temporary distractions while preserving pores, hair texture, fine facial detail, clothing weave, and realistic facial structure.
- Crop finalization: lock the image into {비율} with centered balance for KakaoTalk profile display, keeping the face readable even when shown as a small circular avatar.
- Detail layer: include subtle lifestyle cues such as a softly visible necklace, knit texture, shirt collar, warm window reflection, blurred mug shape, small plant leaves, or gentle bokeh dots when they fit {컨셉} and {배경}.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: allow only tiny profile-card style text accents in Korean or simple English near the lower edge; keep them secondary, clean, and legible. Example: “2026.05 · 서울”, “오늘의 기록”, “daily profile”.
- Color palette: follow {컬러 톤} with restrained neutrals, soft warm beige, charcoal accents, and controlled amber highlights when appropriate.
- Border/shadow: use a faint natural vignette, film-like falloff, or soft shadow only if it helps the subject separate from the background; it should feel photographic rather than graphic.
- Environmental realism: keep background objects softly out of focus but recognizable enough to suggest a real place, with believable textures, reflections, and natural imperfections.
- Profile usability: all decorative labels, stickers, or background details must stay away from the eyes, nose, mouth, and main facial contour.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: full-frame portrait setup, 85mm f/1.8 or 50mm f/1.4 look, shallow depth of field, clean facial perspective.
- Lighting: natural side light from one side at roughly 45°, softened through a window or diffused source; gentle fill on the shadow side for even facial readability.
- Color grade: subtle warm-neutral grade with beige, taupe, and amber balance; keep whites clean and avoid heavy cinematic contrast.
- Texture rendering: realistic skin texture, soft fabric detail, natural hair strands, and slight lens softness at the edges for a real camera feel.
- Depth cues: background bokeh, window glow, wall texture, or soft foreground blur may be used to create a richer portrait atmosphere while preserving the square profile focus.

[6. MOOD]
Natural lifestyle portrait — calm editorial profile-photo feel with the warmth of a quiet cafe, home studio, or soft-window-light headshot. Refined, personal, approachable, and suitable as a KakaoTalk profile image.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: if any small label appears, render it cleanly and correctly, such as “2026.05 · 서울”, “오늘의 프로필”, or “좋은 하루”.
- Maintain the original person’s identity clearly; facial structure, gaze direction, and overall likeness must remain recognizable.
- Keep the framing square and profile-friendly, with a centered head-and-shoulders composition.
- Do not let stickers, captions, props, or background elements cover or distort the face.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]
- Fake official seals / certifications
- Broken Korean characters
- Celebrity composites or unauthorized likeness imitation

[INPUT]
- language: Korean
- output_size: 1024x1536
- ratio: {비율}

[1. PURPOSE]
Local business magazine-style story card for a shop owner, combining a short founder story, three scene photos, customer quote, issue metadata, captions, and neighborhood editorial details into a vertical magazine-cover-meets-feature-page layout.
Designed like a real local lifestyle magazine page with urban-local credibility, suitable for social sharing, store branding, and a believable printed editorial feature.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Overall layout: a polished 3-column vertical magazine page with a strong top masthead/headline zone, a middle founder story block, a large three-photo editorial strip, and a bottom testimonial plus magazine footer; the main subject area should occupy about 55% of the frame height.
- Subject framing: {매장·사장님} is presented as the editorial focal point, with the three photos arranged in a natural reading sequence that leads the eye from owner portrait to storefront/interior context to signature menu/product.
- Background treatment: warm off-white printed paper texture with subtle grain, light beige editorial margins, thin charcoal dividers, small registration marks, tiny page metadata, and realistic magazine production details.
- Magazine details: include issue number, date label, price, barcode area, short feature headline blurbs, small spine/credit text, and a model-name/editorial credit line to make the page feel like a real neighborhood magazine feature.
- Spacing: maintain professional editorial gutters and crisp alignment while allowing authentic content density, layered captions, small labels, and readable microcopy.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
- Top header zone (12–15%): place a bold magazine masthead-style title introducing {매장·사장님}. Add issue metadata such as “LOCAL SHOP MAGAZINE”, “VOL.247”, “2026년 5월호”, and “₩7,500” near the masthead. Add a smaller subtitle line that carries the story tone of {스토리 한 줄}.
- Feature blurbs around the header: include 2–3 short Korean cover lines such as “동네의 맛을 기록하다”, “단골이 사랑한 이유”, and “오늘의 추천 메뉴” in compact editorial typography, positioned like magazine teaser blurbs.
- Story lead block (18–22%): set the founder story as a short quote or pull-quote in a prominent editorial style, using quotation marks and a strong typographic hierarchy. Add a small label like “FOUNDER STORY” and a byline such as “글 편집부 · 사진 로컬매거진팀”.
- Three-photo strip (40–45%): arrange {3컷 사진} as exactly three separated image panels with realistic captions. The first panel should feel like an interview portrait of the owner, the second like a storefront/interior context shot with natural shop details, and the third like a hero product or signature menu shot. Add tiny captions in Korean: “01 사장님의 하루”, “02 매장의 온도”, “03 대표 메뉴”.
- Customer review block (12–15%): place {고객 후기} in a boxed testimonial area with a slightly darker background tint for emphasis, like a magazine callout. Add a small reviewer-style label such as “단골 고객 후기 · @local_guest” and a five-dot or star-style rating graphic.
- Footer zone (5–8%): include palette cue from {컬러 톤}, thin rules, small page number “p.08”, section marker “SHOP STORY”, a barcode block on the lower-right, a tiny address/contact-style line like “서울 동네길 12 · 02-000-0000”, and small spine/credit text reading “Neighborhood Archive / May Issue”.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: use Pretendard Bold for headline, Pretendard Medium for body, and Noto Sans KR Regular for quote text; headline size should feel large and editorial, while body text remains compact and highly legible.
- Color palette: match {컬러 톤} with cream, charcoal, and warm amber; use hex suggestions like #F5EFE4, #2F2A26, and #C97A3D.
- Border/shadow: use thin 1px charcoal rules, subtle paper-edge framing, printed registration ticks, fine divider lines, and a soft drop shadow at 4px y-offset, 12px blur, 15% opacity on photo cards.
- Editorial realism: use natural column rhythm, real magazine hierarchy, caption numbers, small page furniture, barcode texture, price label, issue label, and tiny production notes while keeping all Korean text readable.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: editorial documentary look captured on Canon EOS R5; 35mm or 50mm equivalent for the owner portrait, 24mm wide flat editorial framing for the interior, and 85mm product-style framing for the signature menu.
- Lighting: soft window light from upper-left at 45°, with gentle fill from front-right; interior and product panels should retain natural ambient warmth, visible shop texture, believable surfaces, and appetizing product detail without harsh highlights.
- Color grade: cream paper base with charcoal contrast and amber warmth, lightly desaturated for a printed local-magazine finish, with realistic ink density, subtle halftone feel in photos, and gentle paper grain.

[6. MOOD]
Neighborhood editorial magazine spread — like Urbanplay or local lifestyle journalism, with the calm, trustworthy feel of a well-designed community feature. Warm, lived-in, credible, and human, as if the shop was genuinely interviewed for a monthly local magazine.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: 반드시 다음 문구가 정확히 보여야 함: {매장·사장님}, {스토리 한 줄}, {고객 후기}.
- Additional Korean magazine text should be readable and natural, including “VOL.247”, “2026년 5월호”, “동네의 맛을 기록하다”, “단골이 사랑한 이유”, “오늘의 추천 메뉴”, “FOUNDER STORY”, “단골 고객 후기”, and “SHOP STORY”.
- The three-photo sequence must remain exactly 3 panels, preserving the owner portrait / interior / signature menu order.
- Keep all typography crisp, with no broken Korean characters, no garbled spacing, and no overlapping text.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]
- Fake official seals / certifications
- Broken Korean characters
- Any layout that removes the 3-panel magazine structure

[INPUT]

- output_size: 1024x1536

[1. PURPOSE]
Korean self-service store information sign for a 24h unmanned café, self-laundry, photo studio, convenience store, or print shop.
Vertical A4-style notice poster for entrance doors and interior wall placement, optimized for fast legibility at a glance and realistic in-store use.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Compose a portrait A4 notice board with a large header, five stacked guidance cards, and a practical footer containing contact, address, QR 안내, and emergency information.
- Build the layout as clearly separated rounded boxed sections, each with a small pictogram on the left, a numbered accent badge, bold Korean heading, and a concise detail line using {시각 결}.
- Use realistic store-sign details: store name {매장명}, store type {매장 종류}, entrance notice sticker feel, CCTV 안내, QR payment cue, emergency contact, Wi‑Fi note, and small English helper labels.
- Keep the poster straight, front-facing, and readable as if printed on matte paper and taped or mounted on a glass entrance door.
- Use {안내 항목 5}, {컬러 톤}, {레이아웃}, {주소}, {문의 연락처}, {비상 연락처}, {QR 안내 문구}, and {와이파이 안내} as editable content placeholders while preserving the same hierarchy.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
- Header zone (top 15%): display a small pill label “24H SELF SERVICE” above the main Korean title “무인매장 안내”; place {매장명} and {매장 종류} beneath as a secondary descriptor, with a compact accent line or icon row.
- Main body (middle 65%): divide into 5 stacked guidance boxes, each box containing one numbered item from {안내 항목 5}; place the number in a solid circle or rounded square, followed by bold Korean text, a tiny English helper label, and one short practical detail line.
- Item 01: payment method box with card, QR, and mobile payment pictograms; include a small “PAY HERE” micro label and {QR 안내 문구} beside a realistic QR placeholder square.
- Item 02: operating hours box with a clock pictogram and “연중무휴 / 24시간 이용 가능” support text.
- Item 03: usage guide box with step icons such as 선택 → 결제 → 이용 → 정리, rendered as small arrows inside the section.
- Item 04: CCTV and cleanliness box with camera and trash-bin pictograms, including a courteous cleanup reminder.
- Item 05: emergency contact box with phone icon, {비상 연락처}, and a short note for machine trouble or safety issues.
- Footer zone (bottom 20%): include a service note strip, address line {주소}, inquiry line {문의 연락처}, {와이파이 안내}, small “도움이 필요하면 연락 주세요” text, and a tiny page-like code such as “NOTICE-SELF-24”.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: Pretendard ExtraBold for main Korean headings, Pretendard Medium for supporting text, Noto Sans KR for small English helper text; title around 44–56 px, body around 22–28 px, detail text around 16–20 px, helper text around 14–16 px.
- Color palette: {컬러 톤} with a white base (#FFFFFF), charcoal text (#222222), soft gray dividers (#D9D9D9), warm light-gray section fills (#F7F7F5), and one brand accent color for numbers, icons, QR frame, and small labels.
- Border/shadow: thin 1.5 px charcoal or gray rules, rounded boxes with 10–14 px corner radius, subtle paper shadow (0px 6px 14px, 10–12% opacity) for realistic printed separation.
- Icon language: flat line pictograms with consistent stroke weight, simple filled accent badges, clear arrows, QR placeholder, phone icon, CCTV icon, card terminal icon, Wi‑Fi icon, and small store-operation symbols.
- Print realism: matte poster texture, very slight paper fiber, precise alignment, practical notice-board spacing, and crisp ink edges suitable for a door-mounted sign.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: front-facing flat poster capture look, equivalent to a 50mm lens perspective with low distortion and perfectly parallel verticals.
- Lighting: even studio softbox lighting from front-left at 45° with gentle fill from the right, no harsh glare, clean print-ready exposure.
- Color grade: crisp white, charcoal, warm gray, and brand accent tones with slightly cool neutral balance; keep the palette faithful to a real in-store notice sign.

[6. MOOD]
Practical Korean self-service store signage — friendly, orderly, modern retail wayfinding poster with calm typography, useful micro-information, and trustworthy unmanned-store clarity.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: the following Korean strings must appear clearly and without corruption: “무인매장 안내”, “결제 방법 (카드·QR)”, “운영 시간 24h”, “사용법”, “CCTV·청결”, “비상 연락처”.
- Additional realistic rendered text should include: “24H SELF SERVICE”, “연중무휴”, “선택 → 결제 → 이용 → 정리”, “도움이 필요하면 연락 주세요”, “NOTICE-SELF-24”.
- Layout invariant: 5 vertically stacked information boxes, each visually separated and easy to scan, with bold Korean text as the primary element.
- Contact and footer details must be legible: {매장명}, {주소}, {문의 연락처}, {비상 연락처}, {와이파이 안내}.
- All typography must be crisp, upright, and correctly spaced; no warped letters, no mirrored text, no broken Korean characters.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]
- Fake official seals / certifications
- Broken Korean characters
- Fake government or police/emergency authority marks
- Celebrity composites or real-person endorsement portraits
